name: Client instance provisioning
summary: A ready-made recipe that sets up a new client in one go: a live site and a separate practice (test) site, already loaded with the settings chosen for that client. Each client site has a status with defined behaviour at each stage.
description: A ready-made recipe that sets up a new client's website in one go: a live site plus a separate practice (test) site, already loaded with the settings chosen for that client. Each client site has a status (being set up, active, suspended, archived, restored) with the right behaviour at each stage.
whyItMatters: New clients go live by switching things on, not by writing new code, so onboarding is fast and the same every time.
whatItDoes: Set up a new client from one recipe that creates a live site and a separate practice site, each with its own data and the same product release.
Load the settings chosen for that client into both sites as part of set-up.
Keep the practice site free of real customer, order and payment data; it uses its own connection details for outside services.
Run a go-live checklist and record each item as passed or failed, with evidence.
Suspend a client site with a reason: the shop shows a "store closed" page and the client contact is told.
Archive a client site after a final, verified backup, and later restore it from that backup.
clientRules: The practice site becomes active first.
Proposed, to be confirmed: the live site cannot go active until user acceptance sign-off (reference, signed by, date) is recorded.
Proposed, to be confirmed: the live site cannot go active while any go-live checklist item has failed.
Proposed, to be confirmed: if a set-up step fails, the platform team is told which step failed and the live site is not opened.
Every status change is recorded, and the client contact is told.
benefit: New clients go live by switching things on, not by writing new code, so onboarding is fast and the same every time.

name: Client data isolation
summary: Each client gets its own copy of the system and its own data store, so one client's customers, orders and prices can never be seen by another client.
description: Each client gets its own copy of the system and its own database, so one client's customers, orders and prices can never be seen by another client.
whyItMatters: Protects every client's business data and makes data-protection compliance simpler.
whatItDoes: Give each client its own installation, data store, security keys and picture and file storage, none of them shared with another client.
Refuse sign-in on one client's shop with an account that exists only on another client's shop.
Keep a client's retail and trade shops inside that client's own installation; separate shops are never used to separate two clients.
Give the platform operator a cross-client view that reads only monitoring information (proposed, to be confirmed).
clientRules: No customer, order or price of one client is shown by any page or connection of another client.
benefit: Protects every client's business data and makes data-protection compliance simpler.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether each client has its own installation or clients share one (architecture decision) (ref F-CAT-B)

name: Configuration packs
summary: Pre-packaged sets of settings, such as rules, roles, message wording and product categories, that are layered from global to country, industry and client. A transaction type or a single transaction can make a recorded exception to its client pack where justified.
description: Pre-packaged sets of settings (rules, roles, message wording, product categories and so on). A global pack applies to everyone, an industry pack adds sector settings, and a client pack adds that client's own choices. A single transaction type, or a single transaction, can override its client pack where justified; every override is recorded as a change from the pack.
whyItMatters: This is the main tool that lets a new client be set up by choosing options rather than by new development.
whoUsesIt: Platform team; client administrators; new clients
whatItDoes: Keep settings in packs at four layers: global, country, industry and client, plus entries for a single shop.
Apply a client's set of packs to a site in one step and record which packs and versions were applied, by whom and when.
Check a pack before it is applied and stop if it names an unknown setting, permission or shop.
Load roles, message wording, email templates, categories, feature switches, workflows and rules from the pack.
Let a client administrator set an exception for one transaction type, or one transaction, with a reason; each exception is recorded as a change from the pack.
Proposed, to be confirmed: list settings changed on the site since the last pack, so the platform team chooses to keep the site value or take the pack value.
clientRules: A client value wins over an industry value, an industry value over a country value, and a country value over a global value.
Passwords and secret keys are never held in a pack; a pack that contains one is refused.
An exception for a single transaction is refused without a reason.
Proposed, to be confirmed: applying a pack either fully succeeds or changes nothing; applying the same pack again changes nothing.
Proposed, to be confirmed: each pack set holds exactly one country pack (for example Kenya or Malawi).
benefit: This is the main tool that lets a new client be set up by choosing options rather than by new development.

name: Settings change control
summary: Changes to important settings are checked when saved, show in advance what they will affect, need approval, keep a history of old and new values, and can be undone. Two versions of the settings can be compared side by side.
description: Any change to important settings is checked when saved, shows in advance what it will affect, can be sent for approval, keeps a history of old and new values, and can be undone. Two versions of the settings can be compared side by side and changes copied between them.
whyItMatters: Stops accidental or unauthorised changes from breaking the live shop, and shows who changed what.
whoUsesIt: Client administrators; configuration approvers; auditors; platform team
whatItDoes: Check important settings when they are saved and refuse invalid values, leaving the live value unchanged.
Hold a change to an important setting for approval and preview what it affects, for example the number of open orders using a payment method.
Approve or reject a pending change; a rejection needs a reason and the requester is told.
Show a history of every settings change with who, when, old and new value, reason and approvers, and export a change report for a period.
Undo a change by returning selected settings to an earlier version, through the same checks and approval.
Show the settings as they were on a past date.
Compare two versions of the settings side by side and copy selected differences into a new change.
clientRules: A requester cannot approve their own change.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a high-impact change needs approval by two different approvers.
Proposed, to be confirmed: if a setting changed again after the request was made, the change is not applied and is marked out of date.
On the practice site, valid changes apply at once without approval and are still recorded.
benefit: Stops accidental or unauthorised changes from breaking the live shop, and shows who changed what.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)

name: Configuration export, import and promotion
summary: A site's settings can be saved to a file, loaded into another site, and moved from the practice site to the live site once checked.
description: Settings can be saved to a file, loaded into another site, and moved from the test site to the live site once checked.
whyItMatters: Changes are tried safely first and then copied to live without retyping them.
whatItDoes: Export a site's settings to a file with a summary of where and when it was made.
Load an exported file into another site, with the same checks as a pack.
Promote checked changes from the practice site to the live site; the differences become a change that follows normal approval.
Start a new client from a copy of another client's settings, with recorded permission (proposed, to be confirmed).
clientRules: Passwords and secret keys are never exported; they are listed by name only, to be entered on the target site.
Customer, order and product records are not part of a settings export.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a file from a newer product release cannot be loaded into a site on an older release.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a copy for a new client leaves out names, addresses, logos, email accounts and secrets of the original client.
benefit: Changes are tried safely first and then copied to live without retyping them.

name: Branding and theme
codeChange: None (or Theme/view override if no Pavilion licence)
summary: The client chooses its logo, colours, fonts and page layout so the shop looks like the client's own brand; each storefront can look different.
description: The client chooses its logo, colours, fonts and page layout so the shop looks like the client's own brand; each storefront can look different.
whyItMatters: Customers recognise and trust the brand, and no design code is needed per client.
whatItDoes: Set the logo for each storefront.
Apply the client's colours and fonts to every page of a storefront, with no change to product code.
Give each storefront of a client its own look.
Use the same branding on invoices and system emails.
clientRules: Shoppers can choose a look only if the client allows it.
benefit: Customers recognise and trust the brand, and no design code is needed per client.

name: Custom domain and SSL
clientName: Own web address and security certificate
summary: The shop runs on the client's own web address, for example shop.client.com, with the padlock security certificate in the browser.
description: The shop runs on the client's own web address (for example shop.client.com) with the padlock security certificate in the browser.
whyItMatters: Customers see a trusted, secure address that belongs to the client.
whatItDoes: Run each storefront on one or more of the client's own web addresses.
Move every visit to the secure (padlock) version of the address.
clientRules: Every client storefront uses the secure address.
benefit: Customers see a trusted, secure address that belongs to the client.

name: Email sender identity
summary: System emails, such as order confirmations, are sent from the client's own email address and set up so they are not marked as spam.
description: System emails (order confirmations and so on) are sent from the client's own email address, set up so they are not marked as spam.
whyItMatters: Customers receive and trust the emails.
whatItDoes: Send system emails from the client's own address and display name.
Send selected emails from a different client address where a template names one.
Send a test email to confirm delivery and spam checks as part of go-live.
clientRules: Email account passwords are never included in a settings export.
benefit: Customers receive and trust the emails.

name: Languages and language packs
summary: The shop can be shown in several languages, including right-to-left languages such as Arabic, and visitors pick their language. Countries, regions and districts used in addresses are maintained in the same admin area.
description: The shop can be shown in several languages, including right-to-left languages such as Arabic, and visitors pick their language. Countries, regions and districts used in addresses are maintained in the same admin area.
whyItMatters: People can shop in the language they understand best.
whatItDoes: Let shoppers choose from the languages published for that storefront.
Show the shop in Kiswahili, English, French, Arabic, Russian and Mandarin for KTDA, and in English and Chichewa for Malawi Post, once translations are loaded.
Lay out the shop right to left for languages such as Arabic.
Show the main language where a translation is missing, and report the gap.
Maintain countries and load the regions or districts each country uses in addresses.
benefit: People can shop in the language they understand best.

name: Currencies and exchange rates
summary: The shop can show and charge prices in more than one currency, with one main currency for accounting. Rates can be typed in, or come automatically from the exchange-rate connection.
description: The shop can show and charge prices in more than one currency, with one main (base) currency for accounting. Exchange rates can be typed in; automatic rates come from the exchange-rate connector (see 'Exchange-rate provider framework').
whyItMatters: International and local buyers see prices in a currency they understand.
whatItDoes: Let shoppers pick a currency and see prices and totals in it, formatted and rounded for that currency.
Keep one main currency for accounting; orders in other currencies also keep the currency and rate used.
Let staff type in a rate, which applies to prices shown after it is saved.
Take automatic rates from the exchange-rate connection (PRD-PLT-024).
clientRules: Where US dollars is the main currency, all reports and order totals use US dollars as the base.
benefit: International and local buyers see prices in a currency they understand.

name: Time zone and formats
summary: Sets the shop's local time zone and how dates, times and numbers are written.
description: Sets the shop's local time zone and how dates and times are written.
whyItMatters: Order times, deadlines and reports show the correct local time.
whatItDoes: Show order times and other times in the shop's time zone, or in the shopper's own time zone if the client allows it.
Write dates and numbers in the format of the chosen language.
benefit: Order times, deadlines and reports show the correct local time.

name: Fiscal calendar for reporting
summary: Lets the client set when its financial year starts so reports group figures by the client's own financial periods.
description: Lets the client set when its financial year starts so reports group figures by the client's own financial periods.
whyItMatters: Finance reports match the client's accounting year.
whatItDoes: Set the month and day the financial year starts.
Group report figures into financial periods that start on that date, in the shop's time zone.
Proposed, to be confirmed: regroup past figures when the start date changes, with the change kept in the settings history.
clientRules: Each order date falls in exactly one financial period.
benefit: Finance reports match the client's accounting year.

name: Multi-store (B2B and B2C storefronts)
clientName: Several shops for one client (trade and retail)
summary: One client can run several shops from the same system, for example a retail shop for the public and a trade shop for business buyers, each with its own products, prices, look, payment and delivery rules.
description: One client can run several shops from the same system, for example a retail shop for the public and a trade shop for business buyers, each with its own products, prices, look, payment and delivery rules.
whyItMatters: Serves business (B2B) and consumer (B2C) customers without running two systems.
whatItDoes: Run a retail shop and a trade shop from one installation, each on its own web address.
Show a product only in the shop it is assigned to.
Show business buyers the trade range and the prices for their role in the trade shop.
Offer retail, bulk, contract-packaging and forward-contract sales in the shops they are set up for.
Give each shop its own value for a setting, such as look, payment methods or delivery rules; other shops use the shared value.
benefit: Serves business (B2B) and retail (B2C) customers without running two systems.

name: Instance health and SLA monitoring
summary: Dashboards and alerts that show whether each client's site is up, how fast it is, and whether agreed service levels are met. The platform operator also has a staff-only view that compares health and usage across all clients.
description: Dashboards and alerts that show whether each client's site is up, how fast it is, and whether agreed service levels are met. The platform operator also has a view, for its own staff only, that compares health and usage across all clients.
whyItMatters: Problems are spotted and fixed before customers notice.
whatItDoes: Show page views, calls from other systems, error rates and response times per client site.
Show how fast key steps are, such as search, checkout and payment confirmation, over a chosen period.
Raise alerts to named people when a measure crosses a set limit.
Report the health of the site's main parts without any personal data (proposed, to be confirmed).
Give platform staff one view of health and usage across all clients.
clientRules: Client staff cannot open the cross-client view.
Alert limits are client settings.
benefit: Problems are spotted and fixed before customers notice.

name: Scalable, open architecture
summary: The system is built to grow: more servers can be added when traffic rises, it runs on Windows or Linux, it uses an open data store, and new modules are added without changing the core.
description: The system is built so it can grow: more servers can be added when traffic rises, it can run on Windows or Linux, it uses an open database, and new modules plug in without changing the core.
whyItMatters: The shop stays fast as it grows and is not locked to one vendor.
whatItDoes: Run a site on more than one web server, with shared storage, when traffic rises.
Add a new product module without changing the core product.
Run on Amazon Web Services or Microsoft Azure with no dependency on one cloud provider.
Keep the data store on a separate server from the application servers.
Run on open data stores (PostgreSQL, or MySQL version 8 or newer) as well as Microsoft SQL Server, and on Windows Server 2019 or newer with Microsoft .NET 10, which the current product base needs.
benefit: The shop stays fast as it grows and is not locked to one vendor.

name: Backup and disaster recovery
summary: Regular automatic backups, tested restores, and a plan to bring the shop back quickly if a server or data centre fails.
description: Regular automatic backups, tested restores, and a plan to bring the shop back quickly if a server or data centre fails.
whyItMatters: Orders and customer data are not lost, and downtime is kept short.
whatItDoes: Take scheduled backups of data and files while the shop keeps trading.
Restore the shop on a recovery site from the latest backup and record the time taken and any data lost.
Report each backup (time, size, success or failure) and the date and result of the last restore test.
Raise an alert when a backup fails.
clientRules: Where an open data store is used, backups come only from the outside backup service.
benefit: Orders and customer data are not lost, and downtime is kept short.

name: Responsive storefront
summary: The shop adjusts itself to work well on mobile phones, tablets and computers.
description: The shop adjusts itself to work well on mobile phones, tablets and computers.
whyItMatters: Both clients require the shop to work on phones, tablets and computers.
whatItDoes: Fit pages to phone, tablet and computer screens with no sideways scrolling.
Let shoppers browse, search, add to the basket and check out in current Android and iOS phone browsers.
Keep every menu, button and entry box usable at phone size.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: screen widths tested are 360, 768 and 1280 pixels.
benefit: Both clients require the shop to work on phones, tablets and computers.

name: Accessibility
summary: The shop and the staff screens follow the international accessibility standard (WCAG 2.1 AA), so people with disabilities, for example people using screen readers, can use them. Users can switch to high contrast and larger text.
description: The shop and the admin screens follow the international accessibility standard (WCAG 2.1 AA) so people with disabilities, for example people using screen readers, can use them. Users can switch to high contrast and larger text.
whyItMatters: Includes everyone and meets public-sector accessibility expectations.
whatItDoes: Check every new or changed screen against WCAG 2.1 AA, by tool and by hand with a keyboard and screen reader.
Let shoppers switch on high contrast or larger text on every page.
Remember the choice for a signed-in shopper, or for the visit for a guest.
clientRules: No level A or AA failure stays open at the end of a delivery increment.
benefit: Includes everyone and meets public-sector accessibility expectations.

name: Contextual help and guided tours
summary: Short help tips on each screen and step-by-step guided tours for new buyers, sellers and staff.
description: Short help tips on each screen and step-by-step guided tours for new buyers, sellers and staff.
whyItMatters: People learn the system without training sessions and make fewer mistakes.
whoUsesIt: New buyers, sellers and staff; client administrators
whatItDoes: Show help tips for a screen and role, in the user's language.
Start a guided tour once at a user's first sign-in; the user can skip it and replay it later.
Let administrators write tips, tour steps and links to training material per language, without a new release.
Keep the standard first-run steps and help links in the staff area.
benefit: People learn the system without training sessions and make fewer mistakes.

name: Data retention and archival
summary: Rules for how long each kind of record, such as orders, payments, support tickets and logs, is kept, when it is archived and when it is deleted or anonymised.
description: Rules for how long each kind of record (orders, payments, support tickets, logs) is kept, when it is archived and when it is deleted.
whyItMatters: Meets legal record-keeping and data-protection rules and keeps the system tidy.
whatItDoes: Set, per kind of record, how long it is kept and whether it is then archived, anonymised or deleted.
Run the rules on a schedule and log how many records were handled each time.
Archive records with a verified copy before removing them from the live system.
Set retention for tracking history: kept active, then archived and still searchable by staff, then deleted.
Proposed, to be confirmed: offer rules for every kind of record the product keeps, such as documents, support tickets, sign-in history, returns and disputes, chat transcripts and the audit trail.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: a record under legal hold, or linked to an open payment, refund, dispute or amount owed, is never removed.
Proposed, to be confirmed: audit history is only archived or removed in whole closed blocks, never entry by entry.
Retention periods are not yet set; each client sets them.
benefit: Meets legal record-keeping and data-protection rules and keeps the system tidy.

name: Product release and upgrade management
summary: A managed way to release new versions of the product and upgrade every client's site safely, including checks that each client's settings and add-on modules still work.
description: A managed way to release new versions of the product and upgrade every client's site safely, including checks that each client's settings and plugins still work.
whyItMatters: Keeps all clients on one product instead of each drifting into its own custom copy.
whatItDoes: Deploy a new release to the practice site first and to the live site only after the regression tests pass there.
Record the release version on each site.
Check after an upgrade that add-on modules and the client's settings still work, and show any problem as a warning and in the upgrade report.
Carry each client's existing settings forward automatically when moving to the current product base, and flag any setting name that changed.
Proposed, to be confirmed: roll back to the earlier release and backup if a check fails on the live site.
clientRules: Every add-on module, including those bought from outside suppliers, must have a version made for the current product base; one without it is not loaded and holds back the release of the features that need it.
benefit: Keeps all clients on one product instead of each drifting into its own custom copy.

name: Feature and module registry
summary: A master switchboard listing every product feature, with on and off switches per client and per shop.
description: A master switchboard listing every product feature, with on/off switches per client and per shop.
whyItMatters: Turning a feature on for a client is a setting, not a development job.
whatItDoes: List every product feature with its state for the client and for each shop.
Switch a feature on or off for the client or for one shop; every change is recorded.
Hide a switched-off feature's pages and actions in that shop (proposed, to be confirmed).
clientRules: A feature cannot be switched on while a feature it depends on is off.
Features of the platform core are always on.
A shop setting wins over the client setting; with neither set, the feature is off.
benefit: Turning a feature on for a client is a setting, not a development job.

name: Client data migration toolkit
summary: Tools to bring a new client's existing data, such as customers, addresses, open orders, order history, loyalty points and gift cards, into the system, with checks and a report showing nothing was lost.
description: Tools to bring a new client's existing data (customers, addresses, open orders, balances, loyalty points, gift cards, order history) into the system, with checks and a report showing nothing was lost.
whyItMatters: Clients can move from an old system without re-typing data or losing history.
whatItDoes: Run a trial load that checks every row and lists rejected rows with reasons, without saving anything.
Load customers, addresses, open orders, order history, loyalty-point balances and gift-card balances.
Load agreed customer and customer-group prices from a spreadsheet using the built-in price-list import.
Produce a check report per kind of record: source count, loaded count, rejected count, and money totals before and after, with differences highlighted.
Proposed, to be confirmed: run a load again without creating duplicates.
clientRules: Old passwords are kept only where the client allows it and the format matches; otherwise customers reset their password.
benefit: Clients can move from an old system without re-typing data or losing history.

name: Exchange-rate provider framework
summary: Connects to sources of official or commercial exchange rates for currencies such as the Kenyan shilling and Malawian kwacha, which the built-in rate source does not cover, and updates rates on a schedule.
description: Connects to sources of official or commercial exchange rates for currencies such as the Kenyan shilling and Malawian kwacha, which the built-in rate source does not cover, and updates rates on a schedule.
whyItMatters: Prices in other currencies stay accurate without manual updates.
whatItDoes: Choose a rate source and update rates automatically on a schedule.
Proposed, to be confirmed: leave rates unchanged and log the error when the source is unavailable.
Proposed, to be confirmed: hold back a new rate that moves more than a set tolerance and log it for finance staff.
benefit: Prices in other currencies stay accurate without manual updates.

name: Translation management
summary: Tools to send all screen text and product content out for translation, bring translations back in, and track which translations are checked.
description: Tools to send all screen text and product content out for translation, bring translations back in, and track which translations are checked.
whyItMatters: Makes running the shop in several languages manageable.
whatItDoes: Export one file per language with all screen text and product content, showing the source and current translation.
Import translated files; imported text is marked unchecked.
Show, per language, the share of text translated and checked.
Let a reviewer mark a translation as checked, with name and date.
Mark machine pre-translations (Google Translate or DeepL) as unchecked.
Proposed, to be confirmed: mark a checked translation unchecked again when its source text changes.
clientRules: Translation service keys are never included in a settings export.
benefit: Makes running the shop in several languages manageable.

name: Hosting profile and sizing NFR
summary: A written description of the server size each type of deployment needs. Malawi Post stated 4 processor cores, 8 GB memory and 2 TB storage for the first six months.
description: A written description of the server size each type of deployment needs. Malawi Post stated 4 processor cores, 8 GB memory and 2 TB storage for the first six months.
whyItMatters: Hosting is sized correctly, and conflicts with heavier components are visible early.
whatItDoes: List every hosted component and its resource needs for a single-server or multi-server deployment.
Compare the planned components with the Malawi Post figures (4 cores at 2.0 GHz, 8 GB memory, 2 TB storage, cloud hosting for the first six months).
Show the final sizing once it is decided whether the Malawi Post figures are a minimum or a maximum.
benefit: Hosting is sized correctly, and conflicts with heavier components are visible early.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the stated Malawi Post server size is a minimum or a maximum (Malawi Post) (ref C-SIZE)

name: Data consistency safeguards
summary: When two people or systems change the same record at the same time, the platform prevents one change from silently overwriting the other. A change sent twice, for example after a network drop, is carried out only once.
description: When two people or systems change the same record at the same time, the system detects it and prevents one change from silently overwriting the other; every request that changes data carries a unique key, so if it is sent twice (for example after a network drop) it is only carried out once.
whyItMatters: Data stays correct when many users and systems work at once, especially on unreliable networks.
whatItDoes: Refuse a save when someone else changed the same record after it was opened, and show the current values.
Carry out a repeated change request only once and return the first result.
Proposed, to be confirmed: refuse a repeated request key sent with different content.
Proposed, to be confirmed: refuse any change request from another system that does not carry a unique request key.
benefit: Data stays correct when many users and systems work at once, especially on unreliable networks.

name: Customer registration and login
summary: Customers create an account with their email address and a password and sign in. A guest who registers in the same visit keeps the basket and any guest order.
description: Customers can create an account with their email address and log in; guests can turn their guest order into an account later.
whyItMatters: Customers can track orders and reorder easily.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers; guest shoppers; members of the public; client administrators
whatItDoes: Register with an email address and a password that meets the password rules, and receive a welcome email.
Sign in with email and password; with a second sign-in check switched on, that step follows.
See saved addresses and earlier orders in My account when signing in again.
Keep the guest basket and guest order on the new account when registering in the same visit.
Let the client choose how new accounts start: at once, after email confirmation, after staff approval, or not at all.
Let members of the public register for the retail shop with name, email and password only, without any company details.
clientRules: An email address belongs to one account only; a second registration with it is refused.
Registration and sign-in from an email, phone number or network address on the block list are refused.
A wrong password is refused and counts towards the temporary lock (PRD-IAM-003).
benefit: Customers can track orders and reorder easily.

name: Mobile-number identity with OTP
codeChange: Custom plugin (ISmsProvider + DI override) + Theme/view override
summary: Customers can sign up and sign in with their mobile phone number, confirmed by a one-time code sent by SMS, and recover their account by SMS.
description: Customers can sign up and log in with their mobile phone number, confirmed by a one-time code sent by SMS, and recover their account by SMS.
whyItMatters: Malawi Post requires sign-up with a mobile number; customers without email can still have an account.
whatItDoes: Sign up with a mobile number and a one-time code sent by SMS, with no email address needed.
Sign in with the mobile number and a one-time code; this sign-in comes ready-made with the current product base, and an outside text-message service chosen by the client sends the codes.
Reach the same account by email and password or by mobile number and code, where the customer has both.
Recover access by SMS code when unable to sign in.
Let the client choose which sign-in methods buyers are offered: password, SMS code or either.
clientRules: A number already in use cannot be registered again; the visitor is offered the sign-in link.
Numbers are stored in international format.
Too many wrong sign-in codes lock that code; a customer locked out for wrong passwords, or staff who must use a second check, cannot get in with a code alone (proposed, to be confirmed).
A code expires after its validity period, and too many wrong entries or too many code requests stop further codes until a waiting time has passed; the client sets these values once for all codes.
Numbers should be entered with the country code (for example +254 or +265); the product adds it where a local number is typed (proposed, to be confirmed).
Which text-message service is used, and whether the ready-made Twilio option is acceptable and reaches Kenyan and Malawian networks, is still to be confirmed by each client.
Proposed, to be confirmed: for staff in sensitive roles, an SMS code alone does not restore access.
benefit: Malawi Post requires sign-up with a mobile number, and customers without email can still have an account.

name: Password policy, lockout and recovery
clientName: Password rules, temporary lock and recovery
summary: Rules for password strength and expiry, a temporary lock after too many wrong attempts, and password reset by email. Recovery of sensitive accounts needs extra checks such as security questions or confirmation by a manager.
description: Rules for password strength and expiry, temporary lock after too many wrong attempts, and password reset by email. For sensitive accounts, recovery needs extra checks such as security questions or confirmation by a manager.
whyItMatters: Protects accounts from being guessed or stolen.
whatItDoes: Set password length, character rules, how many old passwords cannot be reused, and how long a password lasts.
Lock an account for a set time after a set number of wrong passwords, and email the owner about failed attempts if the client chooses.
Let a user reset their password through a one-time email link that expires.
Sign out other sessions after a password change, if the client chooses.
Require security questions or a manager's confirmation before a sensitive account can be recovered.
clientRules: A reset link works only once and only for a set number of days.
Sensitive accounts get no reset link by email alone; the same neutral message is shown as for other accounts.
The reset page never reveals whether an email address is registered.
A person cannot confirm their own recovery request.
benefit: Protects accounts from being guessed or stolen.

name: Multi-factor authentication by role
summary: Staff in sensitive roles must pass a second check when signing in: a code from an authenticator app, a code sent by email or SMS, or a hardware security key. Buyers can also switch on a second check for their own account.
description: Staff in sensitive roles must use a second check when logging in: a code from an authenticator app, a code sent by email or SMS, or a hardware security key. Buyers can also switch on a second login check for their own accounts and choose the factor (SMS, email or authenticator app).
whyItMatters: Protects admin and finance accounts even if a password is stolen.
whatItDoes: Name the roles that must use a second check; members cannot continue until they set one up.
Use an authenticator app, an email code, an SMS code or a hardware security key as the second check.
Let buyers switch on a second check in My account and choose the method.
Make a staff member set up the second check again after an administrator removes it; the removal is recorded.
clientRules: The second check is required by role, not for every shopper.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a member of a role that requires the second check cannot switch it off.
benefit: Protects admin and finance accounts even if a password is stolen.

name: Single sign-on for staff and B2B buyers
clientName: Single sign-on for staff and business buyers
summary: Staff and business buyers sign in with the account they already use at work, for example Microsoft or Google, instead of a separate password. Accounts are created and disabled automatically when people join or leave.
description: Staff and business buyers can log in with the account they already use at work (for example Microsoft or Google) instead of a separate password. Accounts are created and disabled automatically when a person joins or leaves the organisation.
whyItMatters: Fewer passwords, and the client's IT team controls access centrally.
whoUsesIt: Client staff; client IT administrators; business buyers
whatItDoes: Sign staff in through the organisation's sign-in service (OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0) and match them to their existing account.
Create accounts with roles matched to directory groups when the organisation adds a person.
Disable an account and end its open sessions when the organisation removes a person.
Record sign-in errors from the work sign-in service, if the client chooses.
Proposed, to be confirmed: let a company buyer sign in through their own company's sign-in service and link them to that company.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: staff accounts are not created by signing in alone.
Proposed, to be confirmed: where a role requires a second check, the platform asks for one unless the work sign-in service already did one.
benefit: Fewer passwords, and the client's IT team controls access centrally.

name: Session management
summary: Automatic sign-out after inactivity, limits on signing in from many places at once, and the ability to force someone off the system.
description: Automatic logout after inactivity, limits on logging in from many places at once, and the ability to force someone off the system.
whyItMatters: Reduces the risk of someone using an unattended or stolen session.
whoUsesIt: All users; client administrators; security officers
whatItDoes: Sign users out after a set idle time, with different times for staff and buyers.
Keep an active session going while the user keeps working.
Let a security officer force a user off at once, ending all of their sessions; this is recorded.
Start a new session after a password change, a second-check change or a new role.
Proposed, to be confirmed: limit how many sessions one user can have, either ending the oldest or refusing the new sign-in.
Proposed, to be confirmed: end one chosen session while the user's other sessions continue.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: "remember me" does not keep a session alive past the idle time.
benefit: Reduces the risk of someone using an unattended or stolen session.

name: Roles and permissions
summary: Defines what each type of user, such as customer, seller, staff and administrator, can see and do, including custom roles and which products each group can see.
description: Defines what each type of user (customer, seller, staff, administrator) can see and do, including custom roles and which products each group can see.
whyItMatters: People only see and do what their job needs.
whatItDoes: Create roles and tick exactly the permissions each role has, without code.
Give staff access by role only, with separate rights to view and to change each area.
Limit which products, categories, brands, content pages and menus each role can see.
Give one user several roles; the user gets the combined access of those roles.
Set up one role per KTDA stakeholder group once those groups are confirmed.
Proposed, to be confirmed: keep the roles that product modules rely on, such as Finance, Risk and Agent, in place with fixed names.
clientRules: Only users with the right to manage permissions can change a role's permissions.
A role with view rights only cannot save changes in that area.
Proposed, to be confirmed: some permissions are never given to certain roles, for example sellers never see return requests.
benefit: People only see and do what their job needs.

name: Scoped permissions
summary: Limits a person's permissions to a part of the business, for example one shop, one region, one category, orders up to a certain value, or a time window.
description: Limits a person's permissions to a part of the business, for example one store, one region, one category or orders up to a certain value.
whyItMatters: Large organisations with branches or factories can delegate safely.
whoUsesIt: Client administrators; branch, factory and regional staff; agents
whatItDoes: Limit a person to the orders of one shop.
Limit a person to the records of one region, for example a KTDA factory or regional unit.
Limit product editing to one category.
Limit approvals to items up to a set value.
Limit a permission to a time window.
Proposed, to be confirmed: limit an agent to the orders of their own outlet.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: an attempt to open a record outside the person's scope is refused and recorded.
benefit: Large organisations with branches or factories can delegate safely.

name: Permission delegation
summary: A manager can hand over approval rights to someone else for a fixed period, for example while on leave, with a record kept.
description: A manager can hand over approval rights to someone else for a fixed period (for example while on leave), with a record kept.
whyItMatters: Work keeps moving when people are away, with accountability.
whatItDoes: Hand over a permission to a colleague from a start date to an end date.
End the handover automatically on the end date, with no manual step.
Show the colleague the approver's waiting items during the period.
Record every handover when it is created, cancelled or ends.
Proposed, to be confirmed: record actions taken under a handover with both the person acting and the person they act for.
clientRules: Only permissions marked as transferable can be handed over.
A person cannot approve an item they requested themselves, even under a handover.
benefit: Work keeps moving when people are away, with accountability.

name: User administration console
summary: A screen for staff to find users, view their details, activate or deactivate them and, when helping them, see the shop as they see it, with every action recorded. Customers can deactivate their own account and later reactivate it.
description: A screen for staff to find users, view their details, activate or deactivate them and, when helping them, see the shop as they see it, with every action recorded. Customers can deactivate their own account and later reactivate it.
whyItMatters: Support staff can solve customer problems quickly and safely.
whoUsesIt: Support staff; user administrators; shoppers; auditors
whatItDoes: Search users by email, name, phone, company, role, registration date or last activity, and open their details.
Deactivate and reactivate accounts without deleting data; a deactivated user cannot sign in.
Let an administrator see the shop as a customer sees it, with the start recorded for both people.
Let shoppers deactivate their own account after confirming with a password or code, and reactivate it later with a code.
Record staff changes to customer records, roles and addresses with old and new values.
Proposed, to be confirmed: record each time staff open a customer's record, order or address.
clientRules: Staff who are not administrators cannot view the shop as an administrator.
Self-deactivation deletes no data and stops marketing messages.
Proposed, to be confirmed: an account deactivated by staff cannot be reactivated by its owner, who is asked to contact support.
benefit: Support staff can solve customer problems quickly and safely.

name: Staff invitation and access reviews
summary: Staff are invited by email, and managers regularly confirm that each person still needs their access. Administrators can run access reports showing role assignments, privileged accounts and each user's second-check status.
description: Staff are invited by email, and managers regularly confirm that each person still needs their access. Administrators can also run access audit reports showing role assignments, privileged accounts and each user's MFA status.
whyItMatters: Removes access that is no longer needed, a common audit requirement.
whatItDoes: Invite staff by email with chosen roles; the invitee sets a password, sets up the second check where required and accepts the terms before first use.
Run an access review in which each reviewer marks every member of their roles as keep or remove.
Run an access report showing each user's roles, whether they hold privileged access, second-check status, last sign-in and whether active.
Show only privileged accounts in the report, and export it to a spreadsheet (CSV or Excel).
clientRules: An invitation link works once and only for a set number of days.
Every review decision is recorded.
Proposed, to be confirmed: undecided review items become overdue and are listed to administrators; no role is removed automatically.
benefit: Removes access that is no longer needed, a common audit requirement.

name: Authentication audit and suspicious-login detection
clientName: Sign-in records and suspicious sign-in alerts
summary: Records every sign-in and failed sign-in and flags unusual patterns, such as many failed attempts or sign-ins from unexpected countries. The records can feed a security monitoring system.
description: Records every login and failed login and flags unusual patterns, such as many failed attempts or logins from unexpected places; can feed a security monitoring system.
whyItMatters: Detects account takeover attempts early.
whatItDoes: Record sign-ins, failed sign-ins, sign-outs, second checks, password changes, role changes and refused access, with time, network address and outcome.
Flag an account or network address with more than a set number of failures in a set time, and notify the security officer.
Flag a sign-in from a country not seen for that customer recently, and tell the customer if the client chooses.
Search the records by date, customer, network address and outcome, and export them.
Send the records to the client's security monitoring system (PRD-SEC-005).
Proposed, to be confirmed: let the security officer confirm a flag and force the user off, or dismiss it with a reason.
clientRules: No one, including administrators, can change or delete a sign-in record.
benefit: Detects account takeover attempts early.

name: Passwordless and biometric login
clientName: Passwordless and fingerprint or face sign-in
summary: Users sign in with a fingerprint, face recognition or device security key (a passkey) instead of a password.
description: Log in with a fingerprint, face recognition or device security key instead of a password.
whyItMatters: Faster and safer logins.
whatItDoes: Register a passkey on a supported device, and see or remove it in My account.
Sign in with the passkey without a password.
Proposed, to be confirmed: keep password and one-time code sign-in available on devices without passkey support.
Proposed, to be confirmed: count a passkey that checks the person on the device as the second sign-in check.
benefit: Faster and safer sign-ins.

name: Customer profile and address book
summary: Customers manage their personal details and save several delivery addresses, choosing a default.
description: Customers manage their personal details and save several delivery addresses, choosing a default.
whyItMatters: Faster checkout and fewer delivery mistakes.
whatItDoes: Update name, phone and email; an email change is confirmed again where the client uses email confirmation.
Add, edit and delete delivery addresses.
Mark one address as the default, shown first and pre-selected at checkout.
Reuse saved addresses at checkout without retyping.
Proposed, to be confirmed: change a sign-in mobile number only after confirming a code sent to the new number.
benefit: Faster checkout and fewer delivery mistakes.

name: Pickup preference and preferred channel
clientName: Preferred pickup point and contact method
summary: Customers save a preferred pickup point, such as a post office, and how they want to be contacted: SMS, email or app.
description: Customers can save a preferred pickup point (such as a post office) and how they want to be contacted (SMS, email, app).
whyItMatters: Orders go where the customer wants and messages arrive the way they prefer.
whatItDoes: Save a preferred pickup point, which checkout then pre-selects.
Choose a preferred contact method from the methods the client has set up.
Use that contact method for every message that has no message-specific choice.
Proposed, to be confirmed: clear the preference and ask for a new choice when the pickup point closes.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: the app is offered as a contact method only where the shop has an app.
benefit: Orders go where the customer wants and messages arrive the way they prefer.

name: Terms acceptance with versioning
summary: Records when each customer accepted the terms of use and privacy policy, and asks them to accept again when a new version needs it.
description: Records when each customer accepted the terms and privacy policy, and asks them to accept again when a new version is published.
whyItMatters: Provides proof of consent for legal purposes.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers; sellers; support staff; clients; regulators
whatItDoes: Require acceptance of the current terms and privacy policy at registration by web, mobile number or agent.
Record the policy, version, time, channel, network address and any agent for each acceptance.
Ask users to accept again when a new version that requires it is published; they can still sign out and read the policies.
Let authorised support staff see, read-only and in time order, when a customer accepted each version and gave or withdrew each consent.
Proposed, to be confirmed: ask approved sellers to accept new seller terms before using the seller portal.
clientRules: Registration cannot be completed without acceptance.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a user who declines a new version is signed out and can only sign in again by accepting.
benefit: Provides proof of consent for legal purposes.

name: Privacy rights
summary: Customers can give or withdraw consent, download their personal data, ask for it to be corrected, or ask for their account to be deleted.
description: Customers can give or withdraw consent, download their personal data, ask for it to be corrected, or ask for their account to be deleted.
whyItMatters: Meets data-protection law and builds trust.
whatItDoes: Give or withdraw consent to marketing and other uses; withdrawn marketing consent stops marketing from the next send.
Download the personal data held about the customer.
Request a correction of personal details used for orders and deliveries, with a due date set by the country's rules.
Request deletion of the account; once approved, personal details are removed, while orders and invoices are kept under the record-keeping rules.
Mark open privacy requests as overdue after the due date and notify the privacy officer.
Show staff a full privacy history per customer: consents, downloads, corrections and deletions.
Show no analytics and build no analytics profile for a visitor who has not accepted analytics cookies.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: corrections are approved or rejected by staff with a reason, and do not change addresses already on placed orders.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a deletion is complete only when every part of the product holding that person's data has removed it.
benefit: Meets data-protection law and builds trust.

name: Account activity history
summary: Customers see a list of recent sign-ins, profile changes and payment attempts on their account, and when staff accessed their data.
description: Customers can see a list of recent logins, profile changes and payment attempts on their account. It also shows which staff members accessed their data.
whyItMatters: Customers can spot suspicious activity themselves.
whatItDoes: List sign-ins and failed sign-ins, newest first, for a set look-back period.
List changes to name, email, phone, password, second check and addresses, showing what changed but not the values.
List payment attempts with time, method and status.
Show when staff opened or changed the customer's data, with the staff name or role as the client chooses.
Show the same history to authorised administrators.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: network addresses are partly hidden when shown to the customer.
benefit: Customers can spot suspicious activity themselves.

name: Account synchronisation with core systems
clientName: Account sync with Malawi Post systems
summary: Keeps customer accounts in step with Malawi Post's other internal systems through the Integration Layer.
description: Keeps customer accounts in step with Malawi Post's other internal systems.
whyItMatters: Avoids duplicate or conflicting customer records across Malawi Post systems.
whatItDoes: Send new, changed, deactivated and deleted customer accounts to the Integration Layer for the chosen details.
Retry failed sends and list those that still fail for staff follow-up.
Proposed, to be confirmed: accept changes from Malawi Post systems for chosen details, with the agreed system of record winning conflicts.
Proposed, to be confirmed: tell the other systems when a customer is deleted.
benefit: Avoids duplicate or conflicting customer records across Malawi Post systems.

name: Identity verification adapter framework
summary: A common connection that checks identity details, such as national ID, tax number or mobile-money registration, against official or mobile-network sources, with a separate connection for each country.
description: A common connector that checks identity details (national ID, tax number, mobile-money registration) against official or telecom sources, with a separate adapter for each country.
whyItMatters: Confirms buyers and sellers are who they say they are, and adds new countries without rebuilding.
whatItDoes: Check an identity type and number where a process requires identity checks, and record the result as verified, not verified, inconclusive or unavailable.
Check a person against their mobile-money registration.
Check sellers for the seller onboarding process (PRD-SEL-004).
Add a new country by adding its own connection, without changing the common part.
Proposed, to be confirmed: send inconclusive or unavailable results to staff for manual review with a reason.
clientRules: Identity document images are not stored by this feature.
Proposed, to be confirmed: suggestions from automated document reading are shown to the reviewer only; they never decide the result alone.
benefit: Confirms buyers and sellers are who they say they are, and adds new countries without rebuilding.

name: Customer transaction history
summary: Customers see all their past orders, invoices, quotes and returns, and can download or export them.
description: Customers see all their past orders, invoices, quotes and returns, and can download or export them.
whyItMatters: Customers keep their own records and need less help from support.
whatItDoes: List past orders with number, date, status and total, and open details with items, totals and tracking numbers.
Download a PDF invoice for an order.
See quotes and return requests on their own pages, and download a quote as a PDF where the client allows it.
Narrow the history by type, dates, status and value, and export it to a spreadsheet (CSV or Excel).
Re-order a past order in one step, where the client allows it.
benefit: Customers keep their own records and need less help from support.

name: B2B company accounts
summary: A company account with several staff users who share addresses and order history, each with a role such as buyer, approver or company administrator.
description: A company account with several staff users who share addresses and order history, each with a role such as buyer, approver or company administrator.
whyItMatters: Lets organisations buy as a team with proper control.
whatItDoes: Link orders placed by members to the company, visible to members with the right to view.
Offer the company's shared addresses at checkout.
Let a company administrator invite members by email and give each a company role: buyer, approver or company administrator.
Send orders above a role's limit for approval within the company (approval limits are set in checkout, PRD-CHK-018).
Proposed, to be confirmed: remove a member's access to company data while orders they placed stay with the company.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: people outside the company cannot open its orders.
benefit: Lets organisations buy as a team with proper control.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: B2B buyer registration and approval
summary: Businesses apply for a trade account by giving company details, VAT or tax number and documents; the client approves them before trade prices are shown.
description: Businesses apply for a trade account by giving company details, VAT or tax number and documents; the client approves them before trade prices are shown.
whyItMatters: Trade prices and terms go only to verified businesses.
whatItDoes: Apply with company name, registration number, tax or VAT number and the required documents.
Approve an application, which gives the trade buyer role, creates a company account, shows trade prices and notifies the applicant.
Proposed, to be confirmed: reject an application or ask for more information, with the reason sent to the applicant.
clientRules: Trade prices are not shown while an application is still waiting.
Proposed, to be confirmed: uploaded documents must meet the platform's file type and size rules.
benefit: Trade prices and terms go only to verified businesses.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: Tax-exempt and VAT-registered buyers
summary: Marks certain customers or groups as tax-exempt or VAT-registered and records their VAT number.
description: Marks certain customers or groups as tax-exempt or VAT-registered and records their VAT number.
whyItMatters: Correct tax is charged on business sales.
whatItDoes: Mark a customer or a customer group as tax-exempt, so no tax is added to their orders.
Apply an exemption approved on evidence from the next calculation, with the change recorded.
Let a business buyer record a VAT number.
Let staff mark a VAT number as valid or invalid.
clientRules: Settings for VAT numbers are checked for every country so that no buyer is exempted by mistake.
benefit: Correct tax is charged on business sales.

name: Customer home dashboard
summary: A personal home page after sign-in showing open orders, quotes, things waiting for the customer and recent messages, a quick-action menu on every page, and the customer's own figures.
description: A personal home page after login showing open orders, quotes, things waiting for the customer and recent messages. It also has a quick-action menu on every screen (for example place an order, raise a complaint, contact support) and the user's own activity figures (for example orders, response times and spending over time).
whyItMatters: Customers see what needs their attention at a glance.
whatItDoes: Show open orders, open quotes, items waiting for the customer (such as quotes to answer or deliveries to confirm) and the latest messages.
Offer a quick-action menu on every page, such as place an order, raise a complaint or contact support.
Show orders and spending per month for a chosen period.
benefit: Customers see what needs their attention at a glance.

name: Assisted service by agents
summary: Named agents at outlets, such as post offices, register customers and place orders for them, with the agent and outlet recorded.
description: Named agents at outlets (such as post offices) register customers and place orders for them, with the agent and outlet recorded.
whyItMatters: People without internet access or skills can still buy online through a helper.
whoUsesIt: Outlet agents; walk-in customers; client administrators
whatItDoes: Let each agent sign in with their own named account.
Register a walk-in customer with a mobile number or email, confirmed by a code the customer receives.
Record the agent and outlet on the customer account and on the terms acceptance.
Let the agent act for a customer and place orders, with the agent named on each order.
Assign agents to outlets; the assignment limits what each agent can see.
clientRules: An agent account is never shared.
A second sign-in check applies if the agent role requires it.
Proposed, to be confirmed: agents act only for customers registered at their own outlets, and never for staff or administrators.
Proposed, to be confirmed: an agent with no assigned outlet cannot register or act for customers.
benefit: People without internet access or skills can still buy online through a helper.

name: Company cost centres and budgets
summary: Business customers set up cost centres and spending budgets for their staff users.
description: Business customers set up cost centres and spending budgets for their staff users.
whyItMatters: Companies control spending by department.
whatItDoes: Set up cost centres with a budget for a period.
Charge an order to a cost centre and add its total to the amount spent.
Proposed, to be confirmed: refuse an order that would exceed the remaining budget, or send it for approval, as the client chooses.
Proposed, to be confirmed: reduce the amount spent when a charged order is cancelled or refunded.
benefit: Companies control spending by department.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: Seller application and profile
summary: Businesses apply to sell on the platform and create a seller profile with name, description, logo and contact details. The marketplace can be switched on or off per client.
description: Businesses apply to sell on the platform and create a seller profile with name, description, logo and contact details. The marketplace can be switched on or off per client.
whyItMatters: Lets a client run a marketplace with many sellers if it wants to.
whatItDoes: Let a registered customer apply to sell with name, email, description, an optional logo and any details the client requires.
Notify the client when an application is submitted.
Ask guests to sign in or register before they apply.
Show the applicant the status of the application and the next step (proposed, to be confirmed).
Switch the marketplace on or off for a client.
clientRules: A new seller stays inactive until approved.
An application missing a required detail is not accepted.
Where a client has not confirmed it runs a marketplace, seller applications are switched off.
benefit: Lets a client run a marketplace with many sellers if it wants to.

name: Seller KYC documents
summary: Sellers upload required documents, such as registration certificates and licences; the platform stores them, tracks expiry dates and lets staff review them.
description: Sellers upload required documents (registration, licences and so on); the system stores them, tracks expiry dates and lets staff review them.
whyItMatters: Only properly documented businesses can sell.
whoUsesIt: Applicants; sellers; compliance staff; client administrators
whatItDoes: List the documents each seller type and level requires, and let sellers upload them with issue and expiry dates.
Capture identity and business registration details, such as registration number, with the application.
Let compliance staff accept a document, ask for it again, or reject it; asking again and rejecting need a reason shown to the seller.
Keep earlier versions when a seller uploads a replacement.
Let administrators change the required details and documents per seller type and level without a new release.
Alert the seller and compliance staff before a document expires, and mark it expired on the date.
Proposed, to be confirmed: accept a valid document the seller already holds in their document store, without a new upload.
clientRules: If the client chooses, a seller's listings are paused when a required document expires.
Proposed, to be confirmed: only the seller, its staff, compliance staff and administrators can open seller documents; other attempts are refused and logged.
Proposed, to be confirmed: files must meet the platform's file type and size rules.
benefit: Only properly documented businesses can sell.

name: Seller verification workflow and tiers
summary: Seller applications move through clear stages (submitted, under review, approved, rejected, suspended), with verification levels and the ability to request an upgrade or appeal. Sellers see their current level, what it allows and what unlocks the next level.
description: Seller applications move through clear stages (submitted, under review, approved, rejected, suspended), with verification levels and the ability to request an upgrade or appeal. Participants see their current verification level, what it allows and what to do to reach the next level.
whyItMatters: A fair, transparent and auditable onboarding process.
whatItDoes: Move applications through submitted, under review, approved, rejected and suspended, recording the reviewer.
Approve a seller, activating the seller account and notifying the seller.
Reject an application with a reason shown and sent to the applicant.
Suspend a seller with a reason, which pauses all its listings, and reinstate it later.
Define verification levels, each with its own checks, documents and limits, without code.
Show sellers their level, what it allows and what the next level needs, and let them request an upgrade or appeal a decision.
Proposed, to be confirmed: share applications among reviewers by turn, or by seller type, level or country.
clientRules: A seller is approved only when every required document is accepted, the seller agreement is accepted and the block-list check passes.
Proposed, to be confirmed: an approved seller can be taken off the marketplace only by suspension or blacklisting, not by switching it off or deleting it.
Proposed, to be confirmed: an appeal is never decided by the reviewer who made the original decision.
Proposed, to be confirmed: sellers already approved keep their level until checked again after a level changes.
benefit: A fair, transparent and auditable onboarding process.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)

name: Identity and registry verification adapters
summary: Uses the identity check connection (PRD-IAM-020) to check a seller's ID, tax number, business registration and mobile-money registration against official sources.
description: Uses the identity verification connector to check a seller's ID, tax number, business registration and mobile-money registration against official sources.
whyItMatters: Reduces fraud by fake sellers.
whatItDoes: Check a seller's identity details where the seller's level requires it, and record the result.
Check the name registered for a seller's mobile-money number against the seller or owner name, where the provider supports this.
Fall back to document checks (PRD-SEL-002) where no mobile-money check is available.
Proposed, to be confirmed: retry a check when the source is unavailable; a reviewer may decide by hand with a reason.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: a failed check blocks approval until a second authorised person records a reason to proceed, or the seller corrects the details and the check is run again.
Proposed, to be confirmed: an inconclusive check blocks approval until an authorised reviewer records a decision with a reason and evidence.
benefit: Reduces fraud by fake sellers.

name: Payout accounts and verification
summary: Sellers register the bank or mobile-money account where they will be paid; the account is checked, and any change needs a second person to approve it.
description: Sellers register the bank or mobile-money account where they will be paid; the account is verified, and any change needs a second person to approve it.
whyItMatters: Stops payouts being diverted to fraudulent accounts.
whatItDoes: Let an approved seller add one or more mobile-money or bank accounts.
Hold the account number securely and show it partly hidden.
Proposed, to be confirmed: check each account with the bank, against the mobile-money registered name, or by finance staff with evidence, before it is used.
Proposed, to be confirmed: let a seller mark one checked account as the default for payouts.
Send a change to account details for approval and tell the seller's owner by email and phone.
Keep paying to the current details until a change is approved; a rejected change keeps the old details.
clientRules: The person who requested a change, or a seller's staff user, cannot approve it.
Every approved or rejected change is recorded with old and new details.
benefit: Stops payouts being diverted to fraudulent accounts.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)

name: Seller terms acceptance
summary: Sellers must accept the seller agreement before they can start selling.
description: Sellers must accept the seller agreement before they can start selling.
whyItMatters: Gives a clear legal basis for the selling relationship.
whatItDoes: Require applicants to tick acceptance of the published seller agreement when they apply.
Record the acceptance with the person, seller, agreement version, channel and network address.
Proposed, to be confirmed: ask approved sellers to accept a new version that requires it before they use the seller portal.
clientRules: An application without acceptance is refused.
A seller cannot be activated until the current agreement is accepted.
benefit: Gives a clear legal basis for the selling relationship.

name: Marketplace rules and listing eligibility
summary: Rules the client sets for what can be sold and by whom, checked before a listing goes live.
description: Rules the client sets for what can be sold and by whom, checked before a listing goes live.
whyItMatters: Keeps the marketplace within the client's policies.
whoUsesIt: Clients; client administrators; sellers; compliance staff
whatItDoes: Publish marketplace rules for sellers, including prohibited items, listing standards and delivery service levels.
Proposed, to be confirmed: set rules such as which seller types may sell in a category, the minimum number of pictures, and the listing limit per level, with each version kept.
Check every listing against the rules before it is published, however it was added, and name each rule it breaks.
Stop sellers adding products to categories closed to sellers, or beyond the maximum number of products.
Proposed, to be confirmed: list published products that break a changed rule for compliance staff, without unpublishing them automatically.
benefit: Keeps the marketplace within the client's policies.

name: Seller dashboard and onboarding checklist
clientName: Seller home page and onboarding checklist
summary: A seller home page with a step-by-step onboarding checklist, tasks to do, orders and payouts.
description: A seller home page with a step-by-step onboarding checklist, tasks to do, orders and payouts.
whyItMatters: Sellers get started quickly and know what to do next.
whatItDoes: Show applicants a checklist: profile complete, agreement accepted, documents accepted, identity checks passed, payout account checked; each open item links to where it is done (proposed, to be confirmed).
Show approved sellers the remaining checklist items, actions needed (such as expiring documents or an open appeal) and the next payout date and amount.
Proposed, to be confirmed: collapse the checklist once every item is done.
benefit: Sellers get started quickly and know what to do next.

name: Seller staff accounts
summary: Sellers add their own staff users with limited permissions.
description: Sellers add their own staff users with limited permissions.
whyItMatters: Seller businesses can share the work safely.
whatItDoes: Let the client define seller staff profiles, such as orders only or catalogue only.
Let the seller owner invite a staff user by email with a chosen profile.
Limit staff to the actions their profile allows and to the seller's own orders.
Remove a staff user, who then loses seller access.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: staff cannot change payout accounts, staff or the agreement unless their profile allows it.
Staff of a suspended seller cannot use the seller area.
Adding and removing staff is recorded.
benefit: Seller businesses can share the work safely.

name: Seller categorisation
summary: Groups sellers into types or tiers, each with its own terms and processes.
description: Groups sellers into types or tiers, each with its own terms and processes.
whyItMatters: Different seller groups can be treated appropriately without custom code.
whatItDoes: Set up seller types, such as manufacturer, distributor or service provider, and seller sizes.
Use the seller type to decide the verification level, required documents, commission rules, payout cycle and agreement version.
Proposed, to be confirmed: apply a new type's rules from the time compliance staff change it, with the change recorded.
benefit: Different seller groups can be treated appropriately without custom code.

name: Seller performance monitoring
summary: Tracks each seller's performance, such as on-time delivery, cancellations, returns and complaints, and triggers warnings or action when set limits are crossed.
description: Tracks each seller's performance (on-time fulfilment, cancellations, returns, complaints) and triggers warnings or action when thresholds are crossed.
whyItMatters: Keeps marketplace quality high for buyers.
whoUsesIt: Clients; client administrators; compliance staff; sellers
whatItDoes: Calculate each seller's orders fulfilled, cancellation rate, return rate, complaints and on-time delivery rate every day.
Show these figures per seller and period to authorised staff, with export; each seller sees only its own.
Send a warning and record an intervention when a seller crosses a set limit, including the delivery service level.
Proposed, to be confirmed: pause a seller's listings when a limit set to "pause" is crossed, and tell compliance staff.
Proposed, to be confirmed: propose a suspension to compliance staff when a limit set to "suspend" is crossed.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: a seller is suspended only when compliance staff confirm.
benefit: Keeps marketplace quality high for buyers.

name: Seller ratings
summary: Buyers rate sellers after an order; ratings are moderated.
description: Buyers rate sellers after an order; ratings are moderated.
whyItMatters: Helps buyers choose reliable sellers and motivates good service.
whatItDoes: Let the buyer rate the seller with a score and comment once the order is complete.
Hold ratings for approval before they show, if the client chooses.
Let sellers and users report an abusive rating, and hide it if a moderator agrees.
Show the average score and number of ratings on the seller's page.
clientRules: One rating per order and seller, by the buyer of a completed order only.
benefit: Helps buyers choose reliable sellers and motivates good service.

name: Block and watch lists
summary: Lists of blocked, watched and allowed users, sellers, internet addresses and devices, with reasons, time limits and history; sign-ups, sign-ins, checkouts and seller applications are checked against them.
description: Lists of blocked or watched users, internet addresses and devices, with reasons, time limits and history; transactions are checked against them.
whyItMatters: Stops known fraudsters and abusers.
whatItDoes: Add entries for a customer, seller, email, phone, internet address or device, as block, watch or allow, with a reason, start and optional end date.
Apply an entry to registration, sign-in, checkout, seller applications or all of these.
End an entry automatically on its end date.
Stop a blocked person registering, applying to sell or checking out, without telling them the reason.
Let a watched person continue and raise a flag for review.

Proposed, to be confirmed: stop a blocked person signing in, by password or by a code sent to their mobile phone, and refuse every shop page for a blocked internet address where the entry covers all actions.
clientRules: Every new entry, change and removal is recorded with old and new values.
Proposed, to be confirmed: an allow entry stops a watch flag being raised.
benefit: Stops known fraudsters and abusers.

name: Approved supplier panels
summary: The client approves a set of suppliers for each category; only they are invited to quote for requests in that category. Each approval has a validity period, and suppliers are asked to renew before it expires.
description: The client approves a set of suppliers for each category; only they are invited to quote for requests in that category. Each approval has a validity period, and suppliers are asked to renew before it expires.
whyItMatters: Requests for quotation go only to vetted suppliers.
whatItDoes: Add an approved seller to a category's supplier panel with an end date.
Invite only current panel members of a category to quote for requests in that category.
Tell a supplier when renewal is due.
End panel membership on the end date if it is not renewed.
benefit: Requests for quotation go only to vetted suppliers.

name: Bulk participant import and invitation
clientName: Bulk import and invitation of customers and sellers
summary: Staff upload a spreadsheet of customers or sellers and invite them with their details already filled in. Every row is checked, duplicates are found, and a result is shown for every row.
