description: Upload a spreadsheet of customers or sellers and invite them with their details already filled in. Each upload is checked field by field, duplicates are detected, and a result is shown for every row.
whyItMatters: Brings many participants on board quickly.
whatItDoes: Upload a file in the published template; every value in each row is checked.
Create an invitation with the given details for each valid row.
Send invitations by email or SMS; the person completes the profile and sets a password, and sellers go on to the seller application.
Mark rows that match an existing customer or another row as duplicates.
Show and download the result of every row: created, duplicate or error, with the reason.
Proposed, to be confirmed: expire unaccepted invitations after a set time and let staff send them again.
benefit: Brings many participants on board quickly.

name: Commission and fee rules
summary: The client sets commission and fee rates by category, service or listing type, seller type and delivery service, with dates from which they apply.
description: The client sets commission and fee rates by category, service or seller type, with dates from which they apply.
whyItMatters: The marketplace earns revenue correctly and fees change without code changes.
whatItDoes: Set commission as a percentage or a fixed fee by category, service or listing type, seller type or delivery service.
Record commission and fees on each paid order line with the rule version used.
Schedule a rate change from a future date; orders keep the rate in force when they were placed.
Change rules without a new release, with every change recorded.
Proposed, to be confirmed: charge fees such as a listing fee and deduct them in the next settlement.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: the most specific rule wins, in the order seller, seller type or level, listing or service type, category, then default.
Proposed, to be confirmed: where no rule and no default apply, the line is flagged for finance staff and no commission is assumed.
Builds on an add-on bought from an outside supplier; a version for the current product base must still be confirmed by that supplier.
benefit: The marketplace earns revenue correctly and fees change without code changes.

name: Seller settlements and payouts
summary: Calculates what each seller is owed, produces settlement statements and pays sellers on a regular cycle.
description: Calculates what each seller is owed, produces settlement statements and pays sellers on a regular cycle.
whyItMatters: Sellers are paid correctly and on time.
whatItDoes: Calculate each seller's settlement: their share, less refunds, fees, penalties, loan repayment deductions and other seller charges, plus adjustments.
Run settlements on each seller's own cycle, such as daily or weekly.
Let authorised finance staff release a payout to the seller's checked default account.
Record the payout as paid or failed, and retry a failed payout.
Let sellers view and download a monthly statement (PDF and CSV) showing, per order line, what was earned, deducted and paid.
Proposed, to be confirmed: carry a zero or negative balance forward to the next settlement.
clientRules: Each amount is included in exactly one settlement.
A seller cannot see another seller's statement.
Proposed, to be confirmed: no payout is released without a checked payout account.
Proposed, to be confirmed: service lines are paid only once the service is accepted.
benefit: Sellers are paid correctly and on time.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG); the payment model for paying sellers directly, and whether a payment-service or e-money licence is needed (Product Owner and legal advice) (ref PAY-DIRECT)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision WF-ENG, PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 / WF-ENG / PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 pending

name: Seller locations and fulfilment opt-in
clientName: Seller locations and delivery by the client
summary: Sellers record their business locations, choose pickup or drop-off options, and can choose to let the client handle delivery for them.
description: Sellers record their business locations, choose pickup or drop-off options, and can choose to let the client handle delivery for them.
whyItMatters: Delivery can be organised from the right place.
whatItDoes: Add business locations, pickup points and drop-off points with a pickup or drop-off preference.
Use the location as the starting point for collection, or for drop-off at an outlet.
Let sellers opt in to the client's delivery services where the client offers them in that area.
Proposed, to be confirmed: stop a seller closing a location still used by open shipments.
benefit: Delivery can be organised from the right place.

name: Seller vacation mode
summary: Sellers can temporarily pause their listings with a message, for example during holidays.
description: Sellers can temporarily pause their listings with a message, for example during holidays.
whyItMatters: Avoids orders the seller cannot fulfil.
whatItDoes: Schedule a pause with start, end and a message in each language.
Pause all listings at the start time while seller staff keep access to the seller area.
Show the seller's message and return date on the seller page and on paused product pages.
Stop paused items in a shopper's basket from being checked out.
End the pause at the end time or earlier at the seller's choice.
clientRules: Listings resume only when no other pause reason remains.
benefit: Avoids orders the seller cannot fulfil.

name: Seller notifications
summary: Sellers receive notifications about verification, new and changed orders and complaints on the channels the client has set up.
description: Sellers receive notifications about their verification, new orders and complaints on the channels the client has set up.
whyItMatters: Sellers react quickly.
whatItDoes: Notify sellers by email of orders placed, paid and cancelled, and of low stock, plus SMS or app where set up, in the seller's language.
Notify sellers of approval decisions, document requests and expiry, and payout account decisions, with the action needed and a link.
Notify sellers of a complaint with the reference and the date a response is due.
Respect the seller's contact preferences and opt-outs.
Proposed, to be confirmed: use a fallback channel when one fails, and log the failure.
benefit: Sellers react quickly.

name: Seller onboarding funnel report
summary: A report showing how many sellers registered, submitted, were approved or rejected, and how long each step took.
description: A report showing how many sellers registered, submitted, were approved or rejected, and how long each step took.
whyItMatters: Shows where seller onboarding gets stuck.
whatItDoes: Count sellers registered, submitted, approved and rejected for a period.
Show the typical and longest time from submission to decision and between each step.
Narrow the report by seller type and level, and export it.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: "registered" counts people who started a seller sign-up, and "submitted" counts applications made.
benefit: Shows where seller onboarding gets stuck.

name: Seller diversity tracking
summary: Records seller characteristics such as women-owned or youth-owned business and reports their share.
description: Records seller characteristics such as women-owned or youth-owned business and reports their share.
whyItMatters: Supports inclusion targets in development programmes.
whatItDoes: Let sellers declare characteristics, such as women-owned or youth-owned, at application or in their profile.
Show these to compliance staff.
Report the share of approved sellers, active listings and sales value for each characteristic.
benefit: Supports inclusion targets in development programmes.

name: Seller training content
summary: Help pages, templates and guides for sellers.
description: Help pages, templates and guides for sellers.
whyItMatters: Sellers learn to use the platform without one-to-one training.
whatItDoes: Publish training pages and downloadable templates that only sellers can open.
Show links to onboarding content next to the applicant's checklist.
Send changes to content for approval where the client uses content approval.
benefit: Sellers learn to use the platform without one-to-one training.

name: Seller blacklisting
summary: A blocked list and watch list for sellers and suppliers with a history of fraud or abuse. Each entry has a period and an appeal route, and applies automatically.
description: A blocked list and watch list specifically for sellers and suppliers with a history of fraud or abuse. Each entry has a period and an appeal route, and is applied automatically to all transactions.
whyItMatters: Keeps bad sellers off the marketplace.
whatItDoes: Blacklist a seller with a reason and period, which suspends the seller and pauses its listings.
Block the seller's linked details too: owner and staff email and phone, registration number and payout accounts.
Refuse new seller applications that use any of those details.
Put a seller on a watch list so that its listings and orders are flagged for review.
Let a blacklisted seller appeal from its account page; a different reviewer decides, and the seller is told the outcome.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: when a blacklist period ends, the seller stays suspended until compliance staff reinstate it.
benefit: Keeps bad sellers off the marketplace.

name: Commission invoicing to sellers
onHold: PH-INF, PO-REC-v8, PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01, E-INV, PAID-STUB, DOC-LIB
summary: When buyers pay sellers directly, the client cannot deduct commission and fees from the payment, so the platform invoices each seller regularly for them, tracks payment, and can restrict sellers with overdue amounts.
description: When buyers pay sellers directly, the client cannot deduct its commission and fees from the payment, so the platform issues each seller a regular invoice for commission and fees (as a fiscal invoice where electronic invoicing applies), records it in accounts receivable with statements and payment tracking, and can restrict sellers with overdue amounts.
whyItMatters: The client still earns its commission under the direct-payment model.
whatItDoes: Record the commission due on each directly paid order line, using the rules in force when the order was placed.
Issue a commission invoice per period with lines per order, commission, fees and tax, and let the seller download it.
Record the invoice as an amount owed by the seller, with statements and payment tracking.
Submit the invoice as a fiscal invoice where electronic invoicing applies.
Mark unpaid invoices overdue after the due date and grace days, notify the seller and, if the client chooses, pause the seller's listings until paid.
Proposed, to be confirmed: reduce the commission due when a line is refunded before invoicing.
benefit: The client still earns its commission under the direct-payment model.

name: Category taxonomy
summary: The tree of product categories, for example Tea > Black tea > Bulk, with names in each language, web addresses, pictures, display order and limits on who can see them.
description: The tree of product categories (for example Tea > Black tea > Bulk) with names in each language, web-friendly links, pictures, display order and restrictions on who can see them.
whyItMatters: Customers find products easily, and the shop stays organised.
whatItDoes: Create categories under a parent category, with names in each language, web addresses, pictures and display order.
Let shoppers browse categories and subcategories, with their products in display order.
Show the main-language name where a translation is missing.
Limit a category to certain customer groups or shops.
Hide unpublished categories from shoppers.
clientRules: Each category gets a unique web address.
Only staff with catalogue rights can create or change categories; sellers cannot.
benefit: Customers find products easily, and the shop stays organised.

name: Product master record
summary: The main product record: name, short and full description, product code (SKU), barcode, price, weight, size, pictures and whether it is published. Staff and sellers can edit it, with required information and upload limits.
description: The main product record: name, short and full description, product code (SKU), barcode, price, weight, size, pictures and whether it is published. Staff and sellers can edit it, with required fields and upload limits.
whyItMatters: Every product has complete, consistent information.
whoUsesIt: Catalogue staff; sellers; client administrators; shoppers
whatItDoes: Create and edit products with name, descriptions, product code, barcode, price, weight, dimensions and pictures; new products start as drafts.
Let sellers create and manage only their own products.
Record weight and dimensions for delivery pricing and planning.
Hide parts of the product form that a client does not use.
Let the client set which file types and sizes can be uploaded as product pictures and documents.
clientRules: A listing cannot be submitted or published without a name, full description, price (unless "call for price"), stock quantity where stock is managed, and at least one picture.
Sellers cannot exceed the client's limit on number of products or pictures.
Uploads of the wrong type or size are refused.
benefit: Every product has complete, consistent information.

name: Identifier patterns
summary: Product codes are created automatically from a pattern the client sets, for example KTDA-2026-00045, unique within each shop.
description: Product codes are created automatically from a pattern the client sets (for example KTDA-2026-00045), unique within each shop.
whyItMatters: No duplicate or inconsistent codes, without typing them by hand.
whatItDoes: Create a product code from the client's pattern whenever a product is added without one, however it is added.
Take the next number in the sequence if a generated code already exists.
Proposed, to be confirmed: patterns made of a fixed prefix, the year and a sequence number with a set number of digits.
clientRules: A typed code that already exists is refused.
Proposed, to be confirmed: two products added at the same moment always get different codes, and numbers of deleted products are not reused.
Proposed, to be confirmed: changing the pattern does not change existing codes, and the change is recorded.
benefit: No duplicate or inconsistent codes, without typing them by hand.

name: Product and specification attributes
summary: Product options, such as pack size, and descriptive details, such as grade, origin or "fragile", which can be translated and used to narrow search results.
description: Product options (such as pack size) and descriptive details (such as grade, origin or 'fragile'), which can be translated and used as search filters.
whyItMatters: Customers can compare and filter products by what matters to them.
whatItDoes: Add descriptive details, such as size or grade, that shoppers can use to narrow category and search results.
Add options, such as pack size, that change the price and weight when chosen.
Show option and detail names in the shopper's language.
Proposed, to be confirmed: let sellers record "fragile" and handling notes, shown on the product page and passed to delivery documents.
benefit: Customers can compare and narrow down products by what matters to them.

name: Category attribute schema and listing quality rules
clientName: Required details per category and listing quality checks
summary: For each category, the client decides which details must be filled in before a product can be published, and the platform checks this.
description: For each category, the client decides which details must be filled in before a product can be published, and the system checks this.
whyItMatters: Product information is complete and consistent.
whatItDoes: Set, per category, which details are required before publishing.
Let sellers run a quality check that lists every missing detail before they submit.
Warn sellers when a picture is smaller than the set minimum size, while still allowing submission.
Record who changed the required details, when, and what changed.
Proposed, to be confirmed: send changes to required details for approval by a different person before they take effect.
Proposed, to be confirmed: list published products that miss a newly required detail for their owners, without unpublishing them.
clientRules: A listing missing a required detail cannot be submitted or published.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a subcategory follows its parent's requirements, and a product in two categories must meet both.
benefit: Product information is complete and consistent.

name: Variants and attribute combinations
summary: One product can have versions, for example 250 g, 500 g and 1 kg, each with its own code, price, stock and picture.
description: One product can have versions (for example 250 g, 500 g, 1 kg), each with its own code, price, stock and picture.
whyItMatters: Customers choose the exact version they want.
whatItDoes: Create all versions of a product in one step from its options.
Give each version its own code, barcode, price, stock and picture.
Show the chosen version's code, price, stock and picture on the product page.
Warn the shopper and not add a version that is out of stock, unless back-orders are allowed.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: a version code that duplicates another code is refused.
benefit: Customers choose the exact version they want.

name: Bundles and kits
summary: Several products sold together as one bundle or kit with a bundle price.
description: Several products sold together as one bundle or kit with a bundle price.
whyItMatters: Supports gift packs and combined offers.
whatItDoes: Create a bundle from several products with quantities and one bundle price.
Show the bundle's contents with names, quantities and pictures on its page.
Reduce the stock of each item in the bundle when it is sold.
Refuse to add a bundle to the basket when any item in it is unavailable.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: a seller can bundle only their own products.
benefit: Supports gift packs and combined offers.

name: Product cloning and listing templates
summary: Copy an existing product to create a new one with the same settings and pictures. Frequently used set-ups can be saved as named listing templates.
description: Copy an existing product to create a new one with the same settings and pictures. Frequently used set-ups can also be saved as named listing templates for reuse.
whyItMatters: Speeds up adding similar products.
whatItDoes: Copy a product with its settings and pictures; the copy starts as an unpublished draft.
Save a product's set-up as a named template, visible only to that seller, or to all staff for a staff template.
Start a new draft listing from a template, with a new product code.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a template holds descriptions, category, options, tax category, dimensions and delivery settings, but not code, stock or pictures.
clientRules: A seller cannot copy another seller's product.
benefit: Speeds up adding similar products.

name: Bulk import/export and PDF catalogue
clientName: Bulk upload, export and PDF catalogue
summary: Add or update many products at once from Excel, CSV or XML files, export the catalogue and print a PDF catalogue. Sellers can upload too, within limits. Columns are matched by name automatically.
description: Add or update many products at once from Excel or XML files, export the catalogue, and print a PDF catalogue; sellers can upload too, within limits. Files can be Excel, CSV or XML, and columns are matched to product fields automatically.
whyItMatters: Saves hours of manual typing.
whatItDoes: Upload Excel, CSV or XML files in the standard template; new products start as drafts and existing ones are updated by product code.
Let sellers upload their own products where the client allows it.
Export all or selected products to Excel or XML.
Produce a PDF catalogue for offline use and tenders.
Process very large Excel files in parts, if the client chooses.
clientRules: Sellers can upload only their own products and within their product limit.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a file never publishes a product; changes to published products follow the same re-approval as form changes.
Proposed, to be confirmed: files in other formats are refused.
benefit: Saves hours of manual typing.

name: Import validation report
summary: Before a bulk upload is saved, the platform checks every row and lists any errors to fix. Very large files trigger a warning before the upload starts.
description: Before a bulk upload is saved, the system checks every row and lists any errors to fix. Very large files trigger a warning before the import starts.
whyItMatters: Prevents bad data from going live.
whatItDoes: Check every row for required columns, correct values, existing categories and brands, unique codes, required details and prohibited words.
List each error with row number, column and message, for download.
Ask for confirmation before checking a very large file, with the option to cancel.
Record the result of each upload: created, updated and unchanged counts.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: nothing is uploaded while the report shows any error.
benefit: Prevents bad data from going live.

name: Catalogue API
summary: A secure connection that lets other systems, such as an ERP, create, update and read product information automatically.
description: A secure technical connection that lets other systems (such as an ERP) create, update and read product information automatically.
whyItMatters: Keeps the shop in step with the client's other systems without retyping.
whatItDoes: Let an approved partner system read products changed since a date, with prices, stock availability, categories and options, for its permitted shop.
Let an approved ERP create and update products, with the same checks as the staff form.
Refuse and log requests from systems without valid permission.
Limit how many requests each partner system can make in a period, without affecting others.
Keep each published version of the connection working for a notice period before it is retired.
clientRules: Products created this way start as drafts and are never published by the connection.
Unpublished products are shared only with systems specifically allowed to see them.
benefit: Keeps the shop in step with the client's other systems without retyping.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: which connection product is used for other systems to read and update the catalogue (technical decision) (ref API-01); whether a licensed add-on is bought or the capability is built (technical and Product Owner decision) (ref PAID-STUB); which integration gateway product is used and who runs secure sign-in for partners (technical decision) (ref API-GW)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision API-01, PAID-STUB, API-GW / API-01 / PAID-STUB / API-GW pending

name: Price tiers by customer group and quantity
clientName: Prices by customer group and quantity

description: Different prices for different customer groups and quantities, for example a lower price when buying 100 units, with start and end dates.
whyItMatters: Supports retail, dealer, bulk and institutional pricing.
whatItDoes: Set prices per customer group and quantity, with start and end dates and, if needed, per shop.
Show the quantity prices on the product page and apply the right price in the basket.
Let sellers change the base price and add dated prices for their own products; changes are kept in the version history.
clientRules: A price outside its dates, or for another shop, is not used.

benefit: Supports retail, dealer, bulk and institutional pricing.

name: Call-for-price / negotiable flag
summary: Hides the price on chosen products and shows a "request a quote" button instead of "add to basket".
description: Hides the price on chosen products and shows a 'request a quote' button instead of 'add to cart'.
whyItMatters: Bulk and negotiated items are sold by quote instead of a fixed price.
whatItDoes: Hide the price and the "add to basket" button on chosen products and show "request a quote".
Let a buyer send quantity, options and notes from the product page to start a quote request.
Use the quoted price once the buyer accepts the quote and moves it to the basket.
Proposed, to be confirmed: ask guests to sign in before requesting a quote.
clientRules: The quote button shows only on "call for price" products; the basket-level quote request is unchanged.
benefit: Bulk and negotiated items are sold by quote instead of a fixed price.

name: Product tax category
summary: Assigns each product a tax category, or marks it exempt, so the right tax is calculated.
description: Assigns each product a tax category so the right tax is calculated.
whyItMatters: Correct tax on every sale.
whatItDoes: Pre-select the client's default tax category for new products.
Apply the rate set for the product's tax category on every sale.
Mark a product as tax-exempt so no tax is charged on it.
benefit: Correct tax on every sale.

name: Cross-border trade fields
summary: Extra product details needed for export: customs (HS) code, country of origin and duty information.
description: Extra product details needed for export: customs (HS) code, country of origin and duty information.
whyItMatters: Supports international shipping and customs paperwork.
whatItDoes: Record an HS code, country of origin and duty note on each product, where the shop uses them.
Print these details on export documents for each order line.
Proposed, to be confirmed: refuse an HS code in the wrong format, and accept only countries from the country list.
Proposed, to be confirmed: require these details before a product offered for international delivery can be submitted.
benefit: Supports international shipping and customs paperwork.

name: Product media
summary: Several pictures per product, videos, 360-degree views, PDF brochures and zoom, with configurable image sizes and quality.
description: Several pictures per product, videos, 360-degree views, PDF brochures and zoom, with configurable image sizes and quality.
whyItMatters: Customers can see what they are buying.
whatItDoes: Show several pictures with thumbnails and an embedded video on the product page.
Let shoppers zoom into a full-size picture.
Show a 3D model of the product that shoppers can turn, zoom and let rotate (ready-made); a separate 360-degree photo view only if the client does not accept the 3D model for this.
Offer a PDF brochure for download.
Resize pictures above the set maximum size.
clientRules: Files of the wrong type or size are refused.
Sellers can add 3D models to their own products only if the client allows it.
benefit: Customers can see what they are buying.

name: Localised product content
summary: Product names, descriptions and details written in each language the shop offers.
description: Product names, descriptions and details written in each language the shop offers.
whyItMatters: Customers read product information in their own language.
whatItDoes: Enter name, short and full description and search-engine text in each language, for example the six languages KTDA requires.
Show the shopper's language, or the main language where a translation is missing.
Pre-translate empty text by machine and mark the listing for review before publication.
Offer a generated product description for staff to edit; it is saved only when staff save the product.
benefit: Customers read product information in their own language.

name: Product questions and answers
summary: Shoppers ask questions on a product page; the seller or staff answer; questions and answers are published after moderation.
description: Shoppers ask questions on a product page; the seller or staff answer; answers are published after moderation.
whyItMatters: Answers common questions once for everyone and builds confidence to buy.
whatItDoes: Let registered shoppers ask a question on a product page.
Let sellers answer questions about their products.
Let staff approve or reject questions and answers; approved ones show to all shoppers, and authors of rejected ones are told.
Proposed, to be confirmed: tell the person who asked when an answer is published.
clientRules: Nothing is published before moderation, and every decision is recorded.
Proposed, to be confirmed: guests must sign in to ask.
benefit: Answers common questions once for everyone and builds confidence to buy.

name: Regulatory metadata and certificates
summary: For regulated products, required legal details and certificates with validity dates are stored; the platform warns before a certificate expires and can hide the product when it does. Each product shows its compliance review status.
description: For regulated products, required legal details and certificates (with validity dates) are stored; the system warns before a certificate expires and can hide the product when it does. Each product shows its compliance review status (pending, validated, flagged, escalated or barred).
whyItMatters: Avoids selling products without valid certification.
whatItDoes: Mark categories as regulated with the legal details they require.
Store certificates with type, number, issuer, validity dates and the file.
Warn the seller and compliance staff once before a certificate expires.
Pause and hide a listing when its certificate expires, where the category is set to do so.
Set a review status on each regulated listing: pending, validated, flagged, escalated or barred.
clientRules: A regulated listing cannot be submitted without its legal details and a valid certificate.
A barred listing cannot be submitted or published.
benefit: Avoids selling products without valid certification.

name: Origin and provenance content
summary: Shows where a product comes from, for example the factory, farm or region, using producer pages, product details and content pages. Certificates and ownership-chain documents can be attached as proof of origin.
description: Shows where a product comes from (for example the factory, farm or region) using producer records, product details and content pages. Certificates and ownership-chain documents can be attached as proof of origin.
whyItMatters: Buyers value knowing the origin and story of the product.
whatItDoes: Link a product to its producer page with description, picture and other products.
Link a factory or farmer story page from the producer page.
Attach proof-of-origin documents for shoppers to download; documents marked internal are not shown.
clientRules: Attached documents must meet the file type and size rules.
benefit: Buyers value knowing the origin and story of the product.

name: Listing policy enforcement
summary: Blocks prohibited items and words, lets shoppers report a listing, and handles takedown requests with evidence.
description: Blocks prohibited items and words, lets anyone report a listing, and handles takedown requests with evidence.
whyItMatters: Keeps illegal or harmful items off the shop.
whoUsesIt: Clients; client administrators; shoppers; compliance staff
whatItDoes: Refuse listings, by any route, whose text in any language contains a prohibited word.
Refuse listings placed in a prohibited category.
Let shoppers report a listing from the product page or search results, and notify compliance staff.
Record takedown requests with requester, basis and evidence.
Withdraw a listing when a report or takedown is upheld, notify the seller and keep the evidence.
Proposed, to be confirmed: send listings matching a "flag" rule to review with the reason shown.
clientRules: An upheld decision needs a reason and is recorded.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a dismissed report leaves the listing unchanged and the reporter is told.
benefit: Keeps illegal or harmful items off the shop.

name: Listing lifecycle and operator approval
summary: Products move through stages (draft, in review, approved, published, paused, archived), with approval by one or more approvers in sequence, for example catalogue staff then a manager, before publishing.
description: Products move through stages (draft, in review, approved, published, paused, archived), with approval by one or more configured approvers in sequence (for example catalogue staff, then a manager) before publishing.
whyItMatters: Only checked products go live.
whatItDoes: Move a listing from draft to review once its checks pass.
Approve in one or more steps in sequence; the listing is approved after the last step.
Reject or ask for changes with a reason, and tell the owner.
Send listings to review queues by category, seller, seller level and shop, with a default queue.
Pause, resume and archive published listings, with every change recorded.
Pause all of a seller's listings when the seller may not sell (for example suspended or on holiday) and resume them only when no reason remains (proposed, to be confirmed).
clientRules: A listing is shown to shoppers only in the published stage; no route can publish it otherwise.
A reason is required to reject or ask for changes.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a person cannot approve a listing they submitted.
Proposed, to be confirmed: editing a listing under review sends it back to draft.
benefit: Only checked products go live.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)

name: Listing version history and autosave
summary: Keeps every saved version of a product so changes can be compared or undone, and saves drafts automatically.
description: Keeps every saved version of a product so changes can be compared or undone, and saves drafts automatically.
whyItMatters: No work is lost, and mistakes can be reversed.
whatItDoes: Keep a version each time a product is saved, with who, when and how it was saved.
Compare two versions, showing old and new values.
Restore an earlier version as a new version, following the normal approval rules.
Offer to restore or discard an unsaved draft when the user reopens the product.
Proposed, to be confirmed: save unsaved edits automatically at set intervals without changing the live product.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: a save is refused if someone else saved the product after it was opened.
benefit: No work is lost, and mistakes can be reversed.

name: Listing availability and withdrawal
summary: Show or hide a product, set when it is available, allow pre-orders, and withdraw it with a reason. Customers watching the product are told, and linked items such as held stock, payments held in escrow and open disputes are passed to the right staff.
description: Show or hide a product, set when it is available, allow pre-orders, and withdraw it with a reason. Customers watching the product are told, and anything linked to it (held stock, payments in escrow, open disputes) is dealt with automatically.
whyItMatters: Control over what customers can buy and when.
whatItDoes: Set the dates between which a product can be bought.
Allow pre-orders with a start date shown to shoppers.
Withdraw a product with a reason; it is hidden and the withdrawal is recorded.
Stop a withdrawn product in a basket from being checked out.
Release basket stock holds and list escrow orders and open cases for staff after a withdrawal.
Proposed, to be confirmed: tell shoppers who are watching the product or have it in a wish list.
clientRules: A withdrawal needs a reason.
Withdrawal does not change orders or payments itself.
benefit: Control over what customers can buy and when.

name: Stale listing detection
summary: Flags products not updated for a set number of days, reminds the seller and can pause them automatically.
description: Flags products not updated for a set number of days, reminds the seller and can pause them automatically.
whyItMatters: Keeps information and prices current.
whatItDoes: Set the number of days per category after which a listing counts as out of date.
Flag out-of-date listings daily and remind the seller once.
Clear the flag when the seller confirms or edits the listing.
Pause the listing after a grace period, if the client chooses, and tell the seller.
benefit: Keeps information and prices current.

name: Service listings
summary: Lets the shop list services, not physical goods, with service details and the area covered. How a booked service is confirmed as delivered is handled by service order completion.
description: Lets the shop list services (not physical goods), with service details and the area covered; how a booked service is confirmed as delivered is handled by 'Service order lifecycle and completion sign-off'.
whyItMatters: The same shop can sell services as well as products.
whatItDoes: Let sellers create a service listing from a service template, where the client switches services on.
Record service type, delivery method, areas covered and qualifications (proposed, to be confirmed).
Refuse a service for an address outside the areas it covers.
Show the service description, delivery method, areas covered and price.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: services are not shipped and are not offered for return; a failed service follows the service completion process.
benefit: The same shop can sell services as well as products.

name: Service booking
summary: A calendar of available time slots where customers book a service.
description: A calendar of available time slots where customers book a service.
whyItMatters: Customers pick a time that suits them, and providers are not double-booked.
whatItDoes: Show free time slots by day with the places left; full slots cannot be chosen.
Confirm the booking when the order is placed, and free the place if the order is cancelled.
Proposed, to be confirmed: let staff add slots with start, end, number of places and an optional outlet.
Proposed, to be confirmed: hold a chosen slot for the shopper until a time limit passes.
Proposed, to be confirmed: let citizens book a slot at an outlet for the in-person step of an e-government service, without a basket.
Proposed, to be confirmed: let service providers move, cancel and close bookings so the number of places stays right.
clientRules: Two shoppers can never take the last place at the same time.
benefit: Customers pick a time that suits them, and providers are not double-booked.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether postal operations, e-Government services and Malawi Post financial services are part of the product (Malawi Post to decide) (ref FG-06)

name: Listing geo-location
summary: Records a listing's map location and shows it on a map. An area, for example a farm plot, can be drawn as a shape.
description: Records a listing's map location and shows it on a map. An area, for example a farm plot, can be drawn as a shape on the map.
whyItMatters: Customers can see where a product or service is located.
whatItDoes: Record a listing's map position.
Show the point or shape on a map on the product page, where a map service is set up.
Proposed, to be confirmed: draw an area as a closed shape on the map.
clientRules: Positions outside valid map ranges are refused.
benefit: Customers can see where a product or service is located.

name: Product reviews and ratings
summary: Customers write reviews and give star ratings, which are moderated; others can mark reviews helpful; reviews can be limited to people who bought the product.
description: Customers write reviews and give star ratings, which are moderated; others can mark reviews helpful; reviews can be limited to people who bought the product.
whyItMatters: Honest feedback helps others decide.
whatItDoes: Let customers write a review with title, text and star rating.
Limit reviews to people who bought the product, and to one review per product, if the client chooses.
Hold reviews for approval before they show, if the client chooses.
Let other customers mark reviews helpful or not helpful.
Let staff reply under a review and notify the reviewer, if the client chooses.
Use a "prove you are human" check on reviews, if the client chooses.
benefit: Honest feedback helps others decide.

name: Product returnability flag
summary: Marks products that cannot be returned, in line with the returns policy.
description: Marks products that cannot be returned, in line with the returns policy.
whyItMatters: Avoids disputes about non-returnable items.
whatItDoes: Let sellers mark a product as not returnable, so it is not offered on the return request page.
Proposed, to be confirmed: show a "cannot be returned" label near the price.
Proposed, to be confirmed: mark products in categories the returns policy excludes as not returnable automatically, without the seller being able to change it.
benefit: Avoids disputes about non-returnable items.

name: Product page delivery promise
clientName: Delivery promise on the product page
summary: The product page shows price, seller, delivery options, estimated delivery time and a returns summary. It also explains how disputes are resolved; the returns and disputes summaries also appear on the order page.
description: The product page shows how long delivery will take, who sells it, delivery options and a returns summary. The page also explains how disputes are resolved, and the same explanation appears on the order page; the returns-policy summary also appears on the order page.
whyItMatters: Customers know what to expect before buying.
whatItDoes: Show the seller's name with a link to the seller page.
List delivery options and fees for the shopper's location.
Show the estimated delivery window, or the product's standard delivery time where no location is known.
Show when pickup is available.
Show summaries of the returns policy and the disputes process, with links, on the product page and the order page.
State when an item cannot be returned.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: a summary is not shown, and no broken link appears, if its policy page is not published.
benefit: Customers know what to expect before buying.

name: Catalogue audit log
summary: Records who viewed or changed what on a product, from which internet address, with old and new values.
description: Records who viewed or changed what on a product, from which internet address, with old and new values.
whyItMatters: Accountability for product and price changes.
whatItDoes: Show, per listing, every change, stage change and approval decision with time, user, internet address, and old and new values.
Record each time staff open a product for editing.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: only users with audit rights can open the record.
benefit: Accountability for product and price changes.

name: Promoted listings with fees
summary: Sellers can pay to feature their products in prominent places, under rules, schedules and fees the client sets.
description: Sellers can pay to feature their products in prominent places, under rules and schedules the client sets.
whyItMatters: An extra revenue stream for the client.
whatItDoes: Set up placement types, such as home page, featured in category, search boost and banner, with fees per period.
Let sellers request a placement for a published product and dates.
Let marketing staff approve requests; placements start and end automatically on their dates.
Proposed, to be confirmed: suspend a placement if its product stops being published.
Proposed, to be confirmed: charge the fee to the seller in the seller settlement.
clientRules: A request is refused if it would exceed the number of places available for any day.
benefit: An extra revenue stream for the client.

name: Catalogue analytics
summary: Reports on product views, how often views turn into sales, out-of-stock rates and why listings were rejected. It also shows wish list and basket additions, how shoppers narrow results, and how many visitors leave at once.
description: Reports on product views, how often views turn into sales, out-of-stock rates and why listings were rejected. It also shows watchlist and cart additions, which filters people use, and how many visitors leave at once.
whyItMatters: Shows which products work and what to improve.
whatItDoes: Count listings by stage and category, the out-of-stock rate and rejections by reason.
Show views, basket and wish list additions, orders and conversion per product and category.
Show how often listed products are clicked from category pages and search results.
Show how shoppers narrow results and how many leave at once, where web analytics is connected; otherwise show "not available".
benefit: Shows which products work and what to improve.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether a licensed add-on is bought or the capability is built (technical and Product Owner decision) (ref PAID-STUB)

name: Listing syndication and product feeds
summary: Sends product information to other marketplaces and shopping comparison sites.
description: Sends product information to other marketplaces and shopping comparison sites.
whyItMatters: Reaches more buyers outside the shop.
whatItDoes: Set up a feed target with format, product selection and schedule.
Send published products that are in stock or can be back-ordered.
Remove withdrawn or paused products at the next run.
Proposed, to be confirmed: mark a failed run and tell staff.
benefit: Reaches more buyers outside the shop.

name: Catalogue segmentation by buyer channel
summary: Shows different product ranges to different customer groups, for example bulk tea for traders and packaged tea for retail shoppers.
description: Shows different product ranges to different customer groups, for example bulk tea for traders and packaged tea for consumers.
whyItMatters: Each audience sees what is relevant to them.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers; business buyers; client administrators; sales staff
whatItDoes: List ranges, such as bulk tea and packaged tea, separately in navigation and category pages.
Hide a range and its category from customers outside the group it is meant for.
Show a range only in the storefront for its business model.
benefit: Each audience sees what is relevant to them.

name: Order quantity rules
summary: Sets minimum, maximum and allowed multiples of quantity per product, for example sold only in cartons of 12. Orders above the maximum can be sent for approval instead of being refused.
description: Sets minimum, maximum and allowed multiples of quantity per product (for example sold only in cartons of 12). Orders above the maximum can be sent for approval instead of being refused.
whyItMatters: Prevents orders in quantities that cannot be supplied.
whatItDoes: Set a minimum and maximum quantity per product, with a warning when a quantity is outside them.
Set a quantity multiple, for example 12, and refuse quantities that are not a multiple.
Proposed, to be confirmed: let a buyer send a quantity above the maximum for approval, and add it to the basket once approved.
benefit: Prevents orders in quantities that cannot be supplied.

name: Guided seller listing wizard
summary: A step-by-step form that guides sellers through creating a listing, adapted to the category.
description: A step-by-step form that guides sellers through creating a listing, adapted to the category.
whyItMatters: Sellers create complete listings without training.
whatItDoes: Show steps for identification, options, pricing, media, compliance and tax, with the category's required details marked.
Stop the seller moving on while a required detail is missing, naming it.
Submit the finished listing for review with the same checks as the staff form.
Proposed, to be confirmed: keep a part-finished listing as a draft and resume at the first incomplete step.
benefit: Sellers create complete listings without training.

name: Customer and company price lists
summary: Special price lists for a particular company, customer or customer group, including contract prices with validity dates, which take priority over standard prices. Price lists come ready-made with the current product base.
description: Special price lists for a particular company or customer, including contract prices with validity dates, which override standard prices.
whyItMatters: Supports negotiated prices for key customers.
whatItDoes: Set a price list with product prices, or a percentage or amount up or down, with validity dates and a priority, and give it to customers or customer groups; a company gets it through its own group.
Show and charge the list price to those buyers within the dates, instead of the standard price.
Choose whether a buyer in several price lists gets the lowest price or the list with the highest priority.
Load and download price lists as spreadsheets.
Use an accepted quote price before the price list.
Record every change to a price list.
Proposed, to be confirmed: list every product where a quantity price and a price list both apply, so staff can resolve it.
clientRules: Where a quantity price also applies to the same buyer, the quantity price is charged; contract products should therefore carry no quantity price for the same buyers.
Price lists apply in every shop of the client and are set in the main currency; a fixed price in another currency does not replace a contract price.
Where any price list is given to a single customer, the shop does not keep ready-calculated prices, so each customer always sees their own price.
benefit: Supports negotiated prices for key customers.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: Company-specific assortment
summary: Controls exactly which products each company can see, beyond the standard customer-group rules.
description: Controls exactly which products each company can see, beyond the standard customer-group rules.
whyItMatters: Companies see only the products agreed for them.
whatItDoes: Proposed, to be confirmed: list the products agreed for a company, so its buyers see them and products agreed only for other companies are hidden.
Proposed, to be confirmed: apply the company range in browsing, search and product pages.
Proposed, to be confirmed: give a new company member the company range at once, and remove it when they leave.
clientRules: Proposed, to be confirmed: products in no company range follow the normal visibility rules.
benefit: Companies see only the products agreed for them.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: Units of measure and pack selling
codeChange: Custom plugin; Core modification (conditional, decision UOM-01)
clientName: Units of measure and pack selling
summary: Sell by kilogram, chest or carton, with pack sizes and prices based on weight.
description: Sell by kilogram, chest or carton, with pack sizes and prices based on weight.
whyItMatters: Matches how bulk goods such as tea are really traded.
whatItDoes: Define pack sizes, such as 1 kg or a chest, and price them from a price per base unit, showing the price per kilogram.
Accept part quantities such as 2.5 kg, if the client decides to sell in part quantities (decision pending).
Proposed, to be confirmed: define units with a code, name, base unit and conversion factor.
clientRules: Whether quantities are whole packs or part quantities is still to be decided.
Proposed, to be confirmed: a conversion factor of zero or below is refused.
benefit: Matches how bulk goods such as tea are really traded.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF); whether products must be sold in fractional quantities such as 2.5 kg (KTDA and Product Owner) (ref UOM-01)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PH-INF, UOM-01 / PH-INF / UOM-01 pending

name: Fixed prices per currency
summary: Set a fixed price in each currency instead of converting from the main currency.
description: Set a fixed price in each currency instead of converting from the base currency.
whyItMatters: Prices in foreign currencies stay stable and round.
whoUsesIt: International buyers; sales staff; finance staff
whatItDoes: Set a fixed price for a product in a currency, which shoppers in that currency see and pay exactly.
Record on the order that fixed prices were used.
Show each shopper the price for their own currency.
Show deductions or charges from other parts of the product, such as wallet use, as separate lines in the order total, and record them on the order.
Proposed, to be confirmed: show the converted price where no fixed price is set.
Proposed, to be confirmed: record every change to a fixed price.
clientRules: An order total is never below zero.
benefit: Prices in foreign currencies stay stable and round.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: Seller listing moderation
summary: Client staff review products submitted by sellers and approve, reject or request changes, with reasons.
description: Client staff review products submitted by sellers and approve, reject or request changes, with reasons.
whyItMatters: Keeps the quality of marketplace listings high.
whoUsesIt: Client staff; approvers; sellers; client administrators
whatItDoes: Show approvers each seller listing with seller, category, submission time, quality-check result and policy flags.
Approve, reject or ask for changes, choosing a reason from a list or writing one.
Show the seller the decision, reason and time, and notify them.
Send listings to review queues by seller level and other rules.
clientRules: A reason is required to reject or ask for changes, and every decision is recorded.
Listings submitted by staff follow the staff review queues, not the seller queues.
benefit: Keeps the quality of marketplace listings high.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)

name: Stock tracking
summary: The platform keeps count of how many of each product, and each version of it, are in stock. It shows shoppers whether an item is available and keeps a history of every stock change.
description: Keeps count of how many of each product (and each version of it) are in stock, shows customers whether it is available, optionally allows orders when out of stock, and keeps a history of stock changes.
whyItMatters: Customers do not buy items that are not there, and staff know what to restock.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers; stock staff; client administrators; sellers
whatItDoes: Shoppers see whether a product is in stock, low in stock or out of stock before they order.
Stock goes down automatically when an order is placed and goes back up when an order is cancelled.
Stock can be kept for each version of a product, for example each size or pack.
Shoppers see the lowered stock straight away after another order; figures are not updated in batches.
Administrators decide per product whether orders are allowed when stock runs out.
Stock staff open a full history of every stock change, with date, quantity, warehouse and reason.
clientRules: When a product does not allow orders below zero stock, the cart refuses more than is in stock.
Sellers can change stock only on their own products, and only through a recorded stock adjustment (PRD-INV-005).
benefit: Shoppers do not buy items that are not there, and staff know what to restock.

name: Multi-warehouse stock
summary: The platform tracks stock separately in each warehouse or store and adds it up to show total availability. Each warehouse or postal facility has its own code and map position.
description: Tracks stock separately in each warehouse or store and adds it up to show total availability. Each warehouse or postal facility has a code and map coordinates.
whyItMatters: Clients with several warehouses or factories see where stock is.
whatItDoes: Stock staff see, for each warehouse, the stock held, the stock reserved for orders, the stock available and the stock on the way from another warehouse.
Shoppers see total availability across all warehouses.
Administrators give each warehouse or postal facility a code and map coordinates.
Warehouse locations are used for nearby searches and for choosing the nearest warehouse for delivery.
clientRules: Proposed: each warehouse code must be unique and map coordinates must be valid, to be confirmed.
Stock on the way between warehouses shows as zero until warehouse transfers (PRD-INV-007) are in use.
benefit: Clients with several warehouses, factories or post offices see where their stock is.

name: Low-stock thresholds and alerts
summary: The client sets a minimum stock level for each product. When stock falls below it, staff or the seller receive an alert and the product appears on a low-stock report.
description: The client sets a minimum stock level per product; when stock falls below it, staff or the seller are alerted and it appears on a low-stock report.
whyItMatters: Popular items are restocked before they run out.
whatItDoes: Stock staff set a minimum stock level and an alert level for each product.
Staff receive an email when stock falls below the alert level.
Sellers set the levels for their own products and receive the alerts themselves.
Staff open a low-stock report listing everything that needs restocking, and download it as a spreadsheet; sellers see only their own products.
The client can choose to switch off the buy button when stock reaches the minimum level.
clientRules: The alert is sent only when stock goes down and ends below the alert level.
Proposed: stock corrections, receipts, transfers and counts trigger the same alerts as orders, to be confirmed.
benefit: Popular items are restocked before they run out.

name: Stock reservation and hold
clientName: Stock hold while the customer pays
summary: Stock is held for a shopper when they start checkout and, if the client chooses, when they add it to the cart. Unpaid orders get reminders, and the client decides what happens when the time to pay runs out.
description: Stock is held for a customer when they add it to the cart (optional, per client), start checkout or place an unpaid order; reminders are sent, and the hold is released automatically if they do not pay in time.
whyItMatters: Prevents two people buying the last item, without locking stock forever.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers; stock staff; finance staff; client administrators
whatItDoes: Items are held for a set time when a shopper starts checkout, and optionally when they add items to the cart.
Other shoppers cannot take stock that is held, and see a message when the item is held by someone else.
A hold ends on its own when its time runs out; the item stays in the shopper's cart and is checked again when they order.
Shoppers with an unpaid order receive reminders to pay, with a link to pay again.
For each payment method, the client sets the time allowed to pay and what happens after it: remind again, flag for follow-up, or cancel the order and return the stock.
Stock staff see all active holds on a product.
Proposed: finance staff see a list of flagged unpaid orders and can release the order or dismiss the flag with a reason, to be confirmed.
clientRules: An order is never cancelled if a payment has succeeded or the order has been shipped.
Payment methods with no time limit (for example cash on delivery, letter of credit or buying on account) are never reminded or cancelled.
No reminder is sent once an order is paid or cancelled, and reminders stop at the number the client sets.
Products that do not track stock, or that allow orders when out of stock, are not held.

Proposed, to be confirmed: the simpler ready-made automatic cancellation and email reminders of the current product base stay switched off, because they use one time limit for all payment methods, send emails only and do not check for a payment arriving at the same moment.
benefit: Two people cannot buy the last item, and stock is not locked forever by orders that will never be paid.

name: Stock adjustments with reason codes
summary: Staff correct stock levels, for example after damage or loss, by choosing a reason. Large corrections need approval by a second person, and every change is recorded.
description: Staff correct stock levels (for example after damage or loss) by choosing a reason; large adjustments need approval; every change is recorded.
whyItMatters: Stock figures stay accurate and losses are explained.
whatItDoes: Stock staff correct the stock of a product in a chosen warehouse and choose a reason such as damage or loss.
Corrections above an approval limit wait for approval and do not change stock until approved.
Approvers approve or reject a correction; a rejection needs a reason.
Auditors see who made each change, why and when.
Stock can no longer be changed directly on the product page; all changes go through a recorded correction.
Returned goods that are put back on the shelf are added to stock with the reason "Return".
clientRules: A reason is required for every correction.
Proposed: a person cannot approve their own correction, to be confirmed.
Proposed: a correction cannot take available stock below zero unless the product allows it, to be confirmed.
Corrections backed by a document (receipt, transfer, count, ERP update, return) do not need a separate approval.
benefit: Stock figures stay accurate and every loss is explained.

name: Goods receiving
summary: Warehouse staff record goods arriving against the purchase order, note any shortage or damage, and record where the goods are stored.
description: Records goods arriving at the warehouse against the purchase order, notes any shortages or damage, and records where the goods are stored.
whyItMatters: Stock levels are right from the moment goods arrive.
whatItDoes: Staff record the goods received for some or all lines of a purchase order.
Accepted goods are added to stock straight away.
Shortages and damaged units are recorded as differences, and the purchase order stays open for the rest.
Staff record the storage location (zone, aisle, rack, shelf, bin) so goods can be found for picking.
Proposed: goods that need inspection are added to stock only after quality staff pass them, to be confirmed.
For batch- or serial-tracked products, staff record the batch details or one serial number per unit.
clientRules: Damaged units are not added to stock.
Proposed: receipts without a purchase order are refused unless the client allows them, to be confirmed.
Proposed: receiving more than ordered, beyond a set tolerance, is refused, to be confirmed.
benefit: Stock levels are right from the moment goods arrive.

name: Warehouse transfers
summary: Staff move stock between warehouses. While on the way, the stock shows as "in transit".
description: Moves stock between warehouses, showing it as 'in transit' while on the way.
whyItMatters: Stock is not lost or counted twice during transfers.
whatItDoes: Staff create a transfer and dispatch it; stock leaves the sending warehouse.
The receiving warehouse records the goods that arrive, and its stock goes up.
Stock in transit is not available for sale anywhere.
Proposed: if fewer units arrive than were sent, the missing units become a stock correction for approval, to be confirmed.
Every change to a transfer is recorded with the user, time and quantities.
clientRules: Proposed: a transfer cannot be dispatched if the sending warehouse does not have enough stock, to be confirmed.
Only products that are stocked in more than one warehouse can be transferred.
benefit: Stock is not lost or counted twice during transfers.

name: Cycle counts
summary: Regular partial stock counts run on a schedule. Differences are investigated and corrected.
description: Regular partial stock counts on a schedule, with differences investigated and corrected.
whyItMatters: Keeps stock records accurate without closing for a full count.
whatItDoes: Staff set up count plans by warehouse, category, product importance or product list, with a frequency.
Counts are created automatically when a plan is due.
Staff can also plan full counts of high-value or controlled stock.
Differences between counted and recorded stock are shown and posted as stock corrections.
Proposed: counters can count without seeing the recorded quantity, to be confirmed.
Proposed: large differences are sent for a recount before posting, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Count differences follow the same approval limit as other stock corrections (PRD-INV-005).
Proposed: the difference takes into account stock movements made after the count started, to be confirmed.
benefit: Stock records stay accurate without closing for a full count.

name: Batch and lot tracking
summary: The platform records the batch (lot) number of goods with manufacture and expiry dates, and which customers received each batch. Quality test results and the chain of custody are recorded too.
description: Records the batch (lot) number with manufacture and expiry dates, and which customers received each batch. Batch quality test results and the chain of custody (who held the batch and when) are recorded.
whyItMatters: If a batch has a problem, affected customers can be found and the batch recalled.
whatItDoes: Staff record the batch number, manufacture date and expiry date when goods are received.
Quality staff record test results for each batch; a failed batch is blocked from sale.
Staff record who held the batch and when; earlier custody records cannot be changed.
Staff choose the batch for each item when it is shipped.
Quality staff recall a batch; its remaining stock stops being sold and a list of every order, customer, quantity and shipment date for that batch is produced.
Proposed: the platform regularly checks batch quantities against stock and lists any differences, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Batch tracking is available only for products whose stock is tracked as a whole, not by product version.
Blocked, expired, recalled and quarantined batches are not available for sale.
benefit: If a batch has a problem, affected customers can be found and the batch recalled.

name: Serial number tracking
summary: The platform records the unique serial number of each unit, from arrival to sale, and who bought it.
description: Records the unique serial number of each unit sold and who bought it.
whyItMatters: Supports warranties and tracing of high-value items.
whatItDoes: Warehouse staff record one serial number per unit when goods are received.
Staff record the serial numbers of the units in each shipment.
Support staff search a serial number and see the product, order, customer, shipment date and its history.
Proposed: a returned unit that is put back on the shelf becomes available again, to be confirmed.
Proposed: differences between serial numbers in stock and recorded stock are listed for checking, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Each unit needs exactly one serial number, and a serial number is used once per product.
Proposed: an unknown serial number, or one not in stock, cannot be shipped, to be confirmed.
benefit: Supports warranties and tracing of high-value items.

name: Expiry management
summary: The platform tracks expiry dates per batch, picks the batches that expire soonest first, flags items close to expiry and stops expired items from being sold.
description: Tracks expiry dates per batch, picks items that expire soonest first, flags items close to expiry and can hide expired items from sale.
whyItMatters: Reduces waste and stops expired goods being sold.
whatItDoes: When a shipment is prepared, the batch that expires first is suggested; staff may choose only another sellable batch.
Batches that reach their expiry date are taken out of sale automatically.
Batches close to expiry appear on a near-expiry list and stock staff are notified once.
Staff record the disposal of expired stock as a stock correction with the reason "Expiry".
clientRules: The client sets how many days before expiry an item counts as close to expiry.
benefit: Less waste, and shoppers are not sold expired goods.

name: WMS/ERP stock synchronisation
clientName: Stock link with the warehouse or ERP system
summary: Stock levels and stock movements are kept in step, in both directions, with the client's warehouse or ERP (business management) system. Stock values and purchase triggers are also passed to the ERP.
description: Keeps stock and stock movements in step, in both directions, with the client's warehouse or ERP system. Stock values for accounting and purchase triggers are also passed to the ERP.
whyItMatters: One set of stock figures across all systems.
whoUsesIt: Stock staff; finance staff; IT team
whatItDoes: Proposed: stock levels sent by the ERP update the platform for each warehouse, to be confirmed.
Proposed: every stock movement on the platform (orders, cancellations, shipments, corrections, receipts, transfers, counts) is sent to the ERP, to be confirmed.
Proposed: stock quantity and value per product and warehouse are sent to the ERP on a schedule, to be confirmed.
Purchase triggers are sent to the ERP when stock reaches the minimum level.
Proposed: failed messages are retried and, if they still fail, are listed for the IT team, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: the same message is never applied twice, to be confirmed.
Proposed: when both systems changed the same stock, the system the client names as the master wins and the conflict is listed for review, to be confirmed.
benefit: One set of stock figures across all systems.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether a licensed add-on is bought or the capability is built (technical and Product Owner decision) (ref PAID-STUB)

name: Inventory analytics
summary: Reports show how fast stock sells, how many days of stock are left, items that never sell and which items matter most.
description: Reports on how fast stock sells, how many days of stock are left, items that never sell and which items matter most.
whyItMatters: Better buying decisions and less money tied up in stock.
whatItDoes: Proposed: managers see units sold, average daily sales and days of stock left per product for a chosen period, to be confirmed.
Proposed: a report shows on how many days each product was out of stock, to be confirmed.
Proposed: planners see items that have not sold within a set period, with their stock value, to be confirmed.
Planners see products grouped into classes A, B and C by their share of sales value.
The management dashboard of fast and slow movers uses the same stock figures as these reports.
Proposed: sellers see only their own products, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Cancelled orders are not counted as sales.
benefit: Better buying decisions and less money tied up in stock.

name: Keyword search
codeChange: None (configuration of bundled plugin + external Google Cloud Retail account)
summary: Shoppers type words and the shop finds matching products by name, description, product code or tags. Products can also carry tags with their own tag pages.
description: Customers type words and the shop finds matching products by name, description, product code or tags. Customers can also type questions in everyday language (for example 'black tea in 1 kg packs'), and products can carry tags with their own tag pages.
whyItMatters: Lets customers find products by typing what they want.
whatItDoes: Shoppers use a search box that is on every page.
Shoppers use an advanced search form, for example by category with sub-categories, brand or seller.
Products are found by name, description, tags, or the exact product code of a product or one of its versions.
Shoppers search in the language they are using on the site.
Shoppers open a tag page to see all products with the same tag.
Shoppers type a request in everyday language, such as "black tea in 1 kg packs", and the best matches come first, when the client chooses the Google search service that comes with the platform.
If the enhanced search engine fails or finds nothing, the standard search answers instead.
clientRules: A search term must reach a minimum length set by the client.
The Google search service is used only if the client agrees to send its product list and visitor identifiers to Google; this data-protection approval is to be confirmed for Kenya and Malawi.
By default the Google search service answers signed-in shoppers only; the client can extend it to guests.
If the client does not use the Google search service, everyday-language search is built into the product search engine instead.
benefit: Shoppers find products by typing what they want.

name: Search-as-you-type
summary: Product suggestions with pictures appear while the shopper is still typing.
description: Suggestions with pictures appear while the customer is still typing.
whyItMatters: Faster searching and fewer spelling problems.
whatItDoes: Shoppers see a set number of product suggestions with pictures as they type.
A "view all results" link appears when more products match than are shown.
When the shopper has chosen a category in the search box, suggestions come only from that category.
clientRules: Suggestions start only after a minimum number of characters is typed.
benefit: Faster searching and fewer spelling problems.

name: Faceted filters
summary: Shoppers narrow search results and category pages by price range, grade, size, brand, seller and "in stock".
description: Filters beside search results and category pages, for example price range, grade, brand, seller and 'in stock'.
whyItMatters: Customers narrow a long list down to what they want.
whatItDoes: Shoppers set a price range.
Shoppers tick product characteristics such as grade or size.
Shoppers choose a brand or a seller.
Shoppers show only items that can be bought now.
Shoppers limit search results to a category and its sub-categories.
Proposed: the same choices are offered on category pages and on the search page, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Choices within one characteristic widen the list (either option); choices across different characteristics narrow it (both).
benefit: Shoppers narrow a long list down to what they want.

name: Location and delivery-option discovery
clientName: Finding items by location and delivery option
summary: Shoppers browse by district, distance or delivery option, or find items available for pickup at a nearby outlet.
description: Customers browse or filter by district, distance or delivery option, or find items available for pickup at a nearby outlet.
whyItMatters: Customers see what they can actually get where they are.
whatItDoes: Proposed: shoppers choose a district and see only products in stock in that district, to be confirmed.
Proposed: shoppers give their location, with consent, and see products within a chosen distance, to be confirmed.
Proposed: shoppers choose a delivery option, such as home delivery or pickup, and see only products that can be delivered that way to their district, to be confirmed.
Shoppers choose an outlet or a district and see the products available for pickup there, with the outlets that have them.
clientRules: Proposed: if the shopper gives no location, the platform asks for a district instead, to be confirmed.
Each client defines what a district is in its own addresses.
benefit: Shoppers see what they can actually get where they are.

name: Sorting options
summary: Shoppers sort results by relevance, name, price, newest, popularity or place of origin.
description: Customers sort results by name, price, newest, popularity or origin.
whyItMatters: Helps customers compare quickly.
whatItDoes: Shoppers sort by name, price or newest.
Search results can be shown with the best matches first.
Proposed: shoppers sort by popularity, based on units sold in a set period, to be confirmed.
Proposed: shoppers sort by place of origin, to be confirmed.
benefit: Shoppers compare products quickly.

name: Category browse
summary: Category pages show a "you are here" trail, sub-categories, featured items and a grid or list view.
description: Category pages with a 'you are here' trail, sub-categories, featured items and grid or list views.
whyItMatters: Easy browsing for customers who do not search.
whatItDoes: Shoppers see the path from the home page to the current category.
Shoppers see sub-categories with pictures and, if the client chooses, their products.
Shoppers see featured products in their own block on a category page.
Shoppers switch between grid and list views.
Shoppers reach categories from the main menu, the category pages and the "you are here" trail.
benefit: Easy browsing for shoppers who do not search.

name: Merchandising widgets and landing pages
summary: Marketing staff build menus, sliders, product carousels, curated collections and campaign pages without developers. Labels such as "New" or "Sale" can be shown on product pictures.
description: Tools for marketing staff to build menus, sliders, product carousels, curated collections and campaign pages scheduled to appear on set dates. Labels ('ribbons') such as 'New' or 'Sale' can be shown on product pictures.
whyItMatters: Promotions and seasonal campaigns without developers.
whatItDoes: Marketing staff build the main and footer menus from categories, brands, sellers, products, pages or links.
Marketing staff set up rotating home-page slides.
Marketing staff create product carousels and collections from a chosen list or a rule, such as a category, tag, new or on sale.
Banners and featured categories appear and disappear on set dates.
Marketing staff build campaign landing pages from blocks such as text, carousels and banners.
Shoppers see a "New" or "Sale" label on product pictures.
benefit: Promotions and seasonal campaigns run on time without developers.

name: Rules-based recommendations
summary: The shop shows related products, "customers also bought", recently viewed items and new arrivals using simple rules.
description: Shows related products, 'customers also bought', recently viewed and new arrivals using simple rules.
whyItMatters: Customers discover more products and spend more.
whatItDoes: Shoppers see related products on a product page.
Shoppers see suggested add-on products in the cart.
Shoppers see products bought in the same orders as the one they are viewing.
Shoppers see the products they viewed recently.
Shoppers open a page of new arrivals.
clientRules: Proposed: products that cannot be bought are not suggested, to be confirmed.
benefit: Shoppers discover more products and spend more.

name: Personalised recommendations and ranking
summary: Suggestions and search results are ordered by what each shopper has browsed and bought, only with their consent.
description: Recommends products and orders search results based on what each customer has browsed and bought, only with their consent.
whyItMatters: More relevant suggestions for each customer.
whatItDoes: Shoppers who give consent receive suggestions based on their browsing and buying.
Search results for shoppers who give consent can be ordered by what is most relevant to them.
Shoppers who do not give consent see only rule-based suggestions (PRD-SRC-008).
Proposed: when a shopper withdraws consent, use of their behaviour stops at once and their data is deleted from the suggestion service, to be confirmed.
