Proposed: if the suggestion service is not available, rule-based suggestions are shown instead, to be confirmed.
clientRules: No personal data is used for suggestions without the shopper's consent.

If the client uses the Google search service, Google receives a visitor identifier with each search and may order results for that visitor; the client must confirm this is acceptable under its data-protection law.
benefit: More relevant suggestions for each shopper, with their choice respected.

name: Wishlist
summary: Shoppers save products to a wish list, share it by email and move items to the cart later.
description: Customers save products to a wish list, share it by email and move items to the cart later.
whyItMatters: Customers can come back and buy later.
whatItDoes: Shoppers save products to a wish list, as registered or guest shoppers.
Shoppers send their wish list to a friend by email.
Shoppers move chosen items from the wish list to the cart.
If the client allows it, shoppers keep several named wish lists.
clientRules: The client sets the maximum number of items and of wish lists.
benefit: Shoppers can come back and buy later.

name: Saved searches and watch alerts
summary: Shoppers save a search or watch a product and are told when new matches appear, the price drops or it is back in stock.
description: Customers save a search or watch a product and are told when new matches appear, the price drops or it is back in stock.
whyItMatters: Brings customers back at the right moment.
whatItDoes: Proposed: registered shoppers save a search with its choices, up to a set number, to be confirmed.
Proposed: shoppers receive one alert listing new products that match a saved search, to be confirmed.
Proposed: shoppers watching a product receive an alert when its price drops, to be confirmed.
Shoppers ask to be told when an out-of-stock product is back in stock.
Proposed: shoppers stop an alert using the unsubscribe link in it, to be confirmed.
benefit: Brings shoppers back at the right moment.

name: Search history
summary: Shoppers see their recent searches and recently viewed products and repeat a search with one tap.
description: Shows the customer's recent searches and recently viewed products so they can repeat them with one tap.
whyItMatters: Saves time for returning customers.
whatItDoes: The platform remembers each shopper's search terms, as a standard part of the platform.
Shoppers see their recent searches when they click in the empty search box and repeat one with a tap.
Shoppers remove searches from their history one at a time.
The client switches the history on or off and sets how many recent searches are shown.
clientRules: Shoppers see only their own searches.
Proposed: search history is deleted when the shopper's account is deleted under data-protection rules, to be confirmed.
A single button to clear the whole history is not included; to be confirmed if a client needs it.
benefit: Saves time for returning shoppers.

name: Product comparison
summary: Shoppers put chosen products side by side to compare their details.
description: Customers put chosen products side by side to compare their details.
whyItMatters: Easier, better-informed choices.
whatItDoes: Shoppers add products to a comparison list.
Shoppers see name, price and each product characteristic side by side.
clientRules: The client sets how many products can be compared; adding one more removes the oldest.
benefit: Easier, better-informed choices.

name: Search engine: relevance, synonyms, multilingual
clientName: Enhanced search engine: relevance, synonyms and languages
summary: A more powerful search engine ranks the best matches first, understands synonyms and word forms, tolerates typing mistakes and works across languages. Administrators set rules to promote results, and every change is recorded.
description: A more powerful search engine that ranks the best matches first, understands synonyms and word forms, tolerates typing mistakes and works across languages. Administrators can set boosting rules (for example by category, featured items or location), and every change to these rules is recorded.
whyItMatters: Customers find what they mean, not only exact words.
whatItDoes: Shoppers see the best matches first.
Catalogue managers set groups of words that mean the same, per language, so a search for one finds the others.
Shoppers find a product when they type another form of a word, such as the plural.
Proposed: shoppers find the intended product despite small typing mistakes, ranked below exact matches, to be confirmed.
Shoppers search in the language they are using, with a fallback when nothing matches.
Catalogue managers promote results by category, featured status or stock in the shopper's district.
Every change to promotion rules and word groups is kept as a new version with who made it and when.
clientRules: Products that cannot be bought are never shown, even if the search engine has not yet caught up.
A client that uses the Google search service gets its ranking from Google; promotion rules and searching in several languages are still built into the product.
Staff searches in the back office use the standard search.
benefit: Shoppers find what they mean, not only exact words.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether a licensed add-on is bought or the capability is built (technical and Product Owner decision) (ref PAID-STUB)

name: Trending and bestsellers
summary: Lists of best sellers, most viewed and trending products by region or category.
description: Lists of best sellers, most viewed and trending products by region or category.
whyItMatters: Shows customers what is popular.
whatItDoes: Shoppers see best sellers on the home page.
Shoppers see most viewed and trending products for a category or for their region.
Proposed: the lists refresh by themselves at a set interval, with trending based on growth in views and sales, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: products that cannot be bought are not listed, to be confirmed.
benefit: Shows shoppers what is popular, without staff maintaining lists by hand.

name: Taxonomy governance
summary: A controlled process to propose, approve and retire product categories, with a record of every change.
description: A controlled process to propose, approve and retire product categories, with a record of changes.
whyItMatters: Keeps the category structure tidy as the catalogue grows.
whatItDoes: Catalogue managers propose a new category, a change or the retirement of a category, with a reason.
Another person approves or rejects the proposal; a rejection needs a reason.
Nothing changes in the shop until a proposal is approved.
When a category is retired, it is hidden, no new products can be added to it, and a list of its products that need another category is produced.
Every step is recorded with user, time, old and new values.
clientRules: While this process is on, categories cannot be created, changed or deleted directly.
benefit: The category structure stays tidy and controlled as the catalogue grows.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)

name: Seller badges and featured sellers
summary: Badges such as "verified" or "top rated" for sellers, and featured sellers for set dates.
description: Badges such as 'verified' or 'top rated' for sellers, and featured sellers for set dates.
whyItMatters: Builds buyer trust and rewards good sellers.
whatItDoes: Marketing staff create badge types with a name and icon and give them to sellers.
Shoppers see a seller's badges on the seller page and on the seller's product pages.
Marketing staff feature sellers on the home page between set dates.
Proposed: a badge with an end date stops showing after that date, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: badges and featured places of a deactivated seller are not shown, to be confirmed.
benefit: Builds buyer trust and rewards good sellers.

name: Delivery promise on listing cards
summary: Product cards in search results and lists show the expected delivery time and whether pickup is available.
description: Product tiles in search results show the expected delivery time and whether pickup is available.
whyItMatters: Customers can choose by delivery speed before opening the product.
whatItDoes: Shoppers see the expected delivery time for their district on each product card.
Shoppers see the same delivery time on the product page.
Shoppers see "Pickup available" when the product can be collected at an outlet in their district.
Proposed: when no delivery time can be worked out, no delivery text is shown, to be confirmed.
benefit: Shoppers choose by delivery speed before opening the product.

name: Search result eligibility
summary: Rules hide unpublished, suspended or out-of-stock products from search results.
description: Rules that hide unpublished, suspended or out-of-stock products from search results.
whyItMatters: Customers do not see things they cannot buy.
whatItDoes: Unpublished, deleted or out-of-date products never appear in search results.
Products of a suspended seller are hidden from search and category pages.
Proposed: products return to search when the seller is reinstated, to be confirmed.
The client chooses whether out-of-stock items are hidden from search; if not hidden, the product page says it is out of stock.
Products set to be hidden at a minimum stock level disappear from results when they reach it.
clientRules: Proposed: these rules do not apply to staff searches in the back office, to be confirmed.
benefit: Shoppers do not see things they cannot buy.

name: Services browsing area
summary: A separate area of the shop for the operator's own services, such as postal, logistics or financial services.
description: A separate area of the shop for the operator's own services, such as postal, logistics or financial services.
whyItMatters: Services are easy to find apart from goods.
whatItDoes: Shoppers open a services entry in the main menu and see a services landing page and service categories.
Shoppers read a description of each service and order it through the service ordering process (PRD-SVC-005).
The client can show the services area only to chosen shoppers or shops.
benefit: Services are easy to find apart from goods.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether postal operations, e-Government services and Malawi Post financial services are part of the product (Malawi Post to decide) (ref FG-06)

name: Web analytics
summary: The shop connects to web analytics to measure what people click and buy after searching or browsing.
description: Connects to web analytics to measure what people click and buy after searching or browsing.
whyItMatters: Shows what works so the shop can be improved.
whatItDoes: Product views, cart additions and purchases are sent to Google Analytics.
Page views can be sent to Facebook Pixel.
Marketing staff see a report of the most popular search terms.
clientRules: Proposed: analytics do not run unless the shopper accepts cookies where data-protection rules require it, to be confirmed.
benefit: Shows what works so the shop can be improved.

name: Accessible search and navigation
summary: Search, suggestions, result choices and menus can be used with a keyboard only and are labelled for screen readers.
description: Search and menus can be used with a keyboard only and are labelled for screen readers.
whyItMatters: People with disabilities can find products.
whatItDoes: Shoppers use the search box and suggestions with the keyboard only.
Shoppers reach and use every result choice and menu item with the keyboard.
Screen readers read a label for each part and announce the number of suggestions.
Proposed: an accessibility check confirms that search and menus meet the WCAG 2.1 AA standard, to be confirmed.
benefit: People with disabilities can find products.

name: Low-connectivity resilience
summary: When the internet connection is weak, search shows clear messages and lets the shopper retry instead of failing.
description: When the internet connection is weak, search shows clear messages and retries instead of failing.
whyItMatters: Works for customers on slow mobile networks.
whatItDoes: Shoppers see a "search is slow" message with a retry button, and their typed text is kept.
When the device is offline, shoppers see a message and the search is sent automatically once the connection returns.
Proposed: if suggestions fail, pressing Enter still runs the normal search, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: automatic retries stop after a set number of attempts; the retry button stays, to be confirmed.
benefit: Search works for shoppers on slow mobile networks.

name: Search API for channels
summary: A search service that other channels, such as USSD, SMS or kiosks, can use through a secure connection.
description: A technical search service that other channels (USSD, SMS, kiosks) can use.
whyItMatters: Customers without smartphones can still search.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers on basic phones; channel systems
whatItDoes: Proposed: registered channel systems search products by keyword, to be confirmed.
Proposed: results can be returned in a short form (name and price) that fits SMS or USSD screens, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: only registered and authorised channel systems can use the service, to be confirmed.
Proposed: each channel system has a usage limit, to be confirmed.
benefit: Shoppers without smartphones can still search.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether a licensed add-on is bought or the capability is built (technical and Product Owner decision) (ref PAID-STUB)

name: Unified search
summary: One search box finds products, the user's own orders, quotes and their own records.
description: One search box that finds products, the user's orders, quotes and their own records.
whyItMatters: Users find anything from one place.
whatItDoes: Signed-in buyers see results grouped into products, their own orders, and their own quote requests and quotes.
Proposed: guests see only products, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: a buyer never sees another customer's orders in the results, to be confirmed.
benefit: Users find anything from one place.

name: Search performance and freshness
summary: Search answers within a target time, and new or changed products appear in results without delay.
description: Search answers within a target time, and new or changed products appear in results immediately.
whyItMatters: Customers see current stock and prices in search results without delay.
whatItDoes: With the standard search, a newly published product or a price change shows in the next search.
Proposed: with the enhanced search engine, changed products are updated within a set time, to be confirmed.
Proposed: search response times are measured against an approved target in load tests, to be confirmed.
benefit: Shoppers see current stock and prices in search results without delay.

name: Storefront conveniences
summary: Handy shop features: quick product preview, a "buy now" button, "email a friend", a delivery-cost estimate on the product page, and links to the previous and next product.
description: Handy shop features: quick product preview, a 'buy now' button, 'email a friend' and a delivery-cost estimate on the product page. Also links to the previous and next product in the same category.
whyItMatters: Faster, easier buying.
whatItDoes: Shoppers preview a product without leaving the list.
Shoppers press "buy now" to add a product to the cart and go straight to checkout.
Shoppers send a product to a friend by email.
Shoppers enter a destination on the product page and see delivery options and costs.
Shoppers move to the previous or next product in the same category.
benefit: Faster, easier buying.

name: Shopping cart
summary: Shoppers add, change and remove items in a cart that is remembered between visits, see a mini cart and can save items for later.
description: Customers add, change and remove items in a cart that is remembered between visits, see a mini cart and can save items for later.
whyItMatters: Customers can collect several items, review them and buy in one go.
whatItDoes: Shoppers add items, change quantities and remove items; totals update straight away.
Shoppers see a mini cart with the number of items and the subtotal.
Registered shoppers find the same cart when they sign in on another device.
A guest's cart is kept when the guest signs in or registers.
If the client enables it, shoppers move a cart item to a "saved for later" list and back.
clientRules: An item moved back from "saved for later" is checked again for stock and price.
benefit: Shoppers collect several items, review them and buy in one go.

name: Checkout
summary: The steps to complete a purchase: address, delivery, payment and review. Each client chooses whether guests can buy without an account or must sign in first.
description: The steps to complete a purchase: address, delivery, payment and review. Each client chooses whether guests can buy without an account or must log in first; customers accept the terms and see a correct, secure total.
whyItMatters: A clear checkout means fewer abandoned purchases. (KTDA allows guest buying; Malawi Post requires login.)
whatItDoes: Shoppers go through billing address, delivery address, delivery method, payment method and review steps, on one page or several, as the client chooses.
The client decides whether guests may buy without an account (KTDA) or must sign in or register first (Malawi Post).
Before paying, shoppers see every item with quantity and price, the subtotal, discounts, tax, payment fee, delivery or pickup fee and the total.
Shoppers accept the terms of service before ordering, where the client requires it.
Proposed: a registered shopper's default delivery address is filled in for them, to be confirmed.
Proposed: on a multi-step checkout, shoppers see which step they are on and which details are missing, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Checkout is always secure, and prices and totals are always worked out again by the platform, so they cannot be changed from the shopper's browser.
Where sign-in is required, no order or payment can be made by a guest.
benefit: A clear, secure checkout means fewer abandoned purchases and correct totals.

name: Checkout validation
summary: Just before an order is placed, the platform checks again stock, prices, whether the shopper may buy the items, whether the chosen payment method is valid, and any fraud warning signs.
description: Just before the order is placed, the system rechecks stock, prices, whether the customer may buy the items, whether the chosen payment method is valid, and any fraud warning signs.
whyItMatters: Prevents orders for items that are gone or wrongly priced.
whatItDoes: The order is refused if stock has run out since the item was added.
Proposed: if a price has changed, the review page is shown again with the new total, to be confirmed.
The order is refused if an item has been withdrawn or the shopper is no longer allowed to buy it.
The order is refused if the payment method is no longer offered for this order.
Orders that match a fraud rule are blocked or flagged for staff, as the client sets.
The order is refused if the delivery address is no longer covered by the seller's delivery area.
Checks from all other parts of the product, such as stock holds, quotas and discounts, run together at this point, so none is missed.
clientRules: Proposed: if a check cannot be completed because of an error, the item is refused rather than allowed, to be confirmed.
No payment is started for an order that fails a check.
benefit: Prevents orders for items that are gone, wrongly priced or not allowed.

name: Multi-seller split checkout
summary: When a cart holds items from several sellers, one checkout and one payment create a separate sub-order and task list for each seller.
description: When a cart holds items from several sellers, one checkout creates a separate sub-order and task list for each seller.
whyItMatters: Customers pay once while each seller handles their own part.
whatItDoes: Shoppers check out and pay once for items from many sellers.
Each seller gets their own sub-order and task list, and an order notification for their part only.
Sellers see only the sub-orders that contain their products.
Proposed: delivery fees, payment fees, discounts and similar order-level amounts are shared out exactly between sub-orders, to be confirmed.
A cart from a single seller creates a single order.
clientRules: Proposed: the payment is taken once for the whole checkout total, to be confirmed.
Proposed: rounding differences go to the sub-order with the largest subtotal, so the parts always add up to the total, to be confirmed.
Proposed: if no payment method can handle a multi-seller payment, shoppers are told before paying, to be confirmed.

The shop keeps one cart for all sellers. The newer platform option of a separate cart for each seller, paid one seller at a time, stays switched off, because it would stop a mixed cart before it is split.
benefit: Shoppers pay once while each seller handles their own part.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG); the payment model for paying sellers directly, and whether a payment-service or e-money licence is needed (Product Owner and legal advice) (ref PAY-DIRECT)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision WF-ENG, PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 / WF-ENG / PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 pending

name: Fulfilment method per line
clientName: Delivery or pickup for each item
summary: For each item in the order, the shopper chooses home delivery or pickup at an outlet.
description: For each item in the order, the customer chooses home delivery or pickup.
whyItMatters: Flexibility when items come from different places.
whatItDoes: Shoppers choose delivery or pickup at a chosen outlet for each item.
Delivery fees and pickup fees are worked out for each group of items.
Outlets that do not serve an item, or are closed on the expected collection date, are not offered.
Pickup-only items are offered for pickup only.
Proposed: the shopper's preferred pickup point is chosen for them when it is open and serves the item, to be confirmed.
Proposed: items are grouped into separate sub-orders by seller and by delivery or pickup choice, to be confirmed.
benefit: Flexibility when items come from different places.

name: Delivery slot and instructions
summary: Shoppers choose a preferred delivery time window, where the delivery service supports it, and add delivery instructions.
description: Customers choose a preferred delivery time window and add delivery instructions.
whyItMatters: Fewer failed deliveries.
whatItDoes: Administrators set delivery windows (day, start, end, number of places) for each delivery service and area.
Shoppers pick a preferred delivery date from a list the platform offers as standard, then see the windows of that date that still have places and choose one.
Where no windows are set for a service, checkout continues without this choice.
Shoppers add delivery instructions, which are shown on the order.
Proposed: when an order is cancelled, its window place is released, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: if the last place in a window is taken first by another order, the shopper is asked to choose another window, to be confirmed.
Every change to delivery windows is recorded.
When one checkout becomes several seller orders, each of them keeps the chosen delivery date.
The client can switch off the choice of delivery date where it does not offer one.
benefit: Fewer failed deliveries.

name: Structured address capture
summary: Address forms suit places without formal street addresses: landmarks, a map pin and a name for the address. A post-office box option, including a virtual post box, can be switched on by the client.
description: Address forms that suit places without formal street addresses: landmarks, map pin, a nickname for the address, with checks. A post-office box field (including virtual post box) can be enabled by the client.
whyItMatters: Couriers can find customers in areas with no street numbers.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers; couriers; staff; sellers; client administrators
whatItDoes: Shoppers add a landmark and a name for the address; the client decides which are required.
Proposed: shoppers place a pin on a map to mark their location, to be confirmed.
The client switches on a post-office box option, including a virtual post box.
County and region choices follow each country's setup.
Proposed: staff, sellers and couriers see the pin with a map link and the landmark on the order, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: the client can require at least one way to find the address (street address, landmark or pin), to be confirmed.
benefit: Couriers can find customers in areas with no street numbers.

name: Checkout resilience and idempotency
summary: An order reference is created as soon as checkout starts and kept through payment and delivery. If payment is interrupted the shopper can resume, and pressing "pay" twice never creates two orders.
description: An order number is created as soon as checkout starts and kept through payment and delivery; if payment is interrupted the customer can resume, and pressing 'pay' twice never creates two orders.
whyItMatters: No lost or duplicate orders when networks are unreliable.
whatItDoes: Proposed: shoppers receive one reference when checkout starts and see it on the order, invoice and tracking pages, to be confirmed.
Shoppers whose payment was interrupted complete payment later from the order page.
Proposed: shoppers who left checkout before ordering find their cart, addresses, delivery and payment choices kept, to be confirmed.
Pressing "pay" twice creates only one order.
A retried payment uses the same reference, so the payment provider recognises it.
clientRules: Proposed: until protection across several servers is delivered, the shop may go live only with checkout on a single server, to be confirmed.
benefit: No lost or duplicate orders when networks are unreliable.

name: E-transactions consumer controls
summary: Checkout shows the confirmations and policy notices that e-commerce law requires, at the required points. Each country's rules are set up as configuration.
description: Shows the confirmations and policy notices that e-commerce law requires, at the required points in checkout. Each country's rules are set as configuration.
whyItMatters: Keeps online sales legal in each country.
whatItDoes: Proposed: administrators set the notices each country requires at each checkout point, to be confirmed.
Where an item or service needs it, shoppers read and tick a returns and refund policy before paying.
Proposed: the platform records each shopper's acceptance with the policy version, to be confirmed.
Proposed: the order confirmation is sent within the time limit the country sets, to be confirmed.
The country's data-protection and e-commerce notices are shown at checkout.
clientRules: An order needing a policy acknowledgement cannot be placed until it is ticked.
No acknowledgement is shown when no item needs one.
benefit: Keeps online sales legal in each country.

name: Minimum order and fee thresholds
clientName: Minimum order and free delivery thresholds
summary: The client sets a minimum order value, and a value above which delivery or pickup is free.
description: Set a minimum order value and fee thresholds, for example free pickup above a certain amount.
whyItMatters: Avoids unprofitable small orders and encourages bigger baskets.
whatItDoes: The client sets a minimum order value; shoppers below it cannot complete checkout and see a message.
The client sets a value above which delivery and pickup are free.
Each shop can have its own values.
clientRules: One free threshold applies to both delivery and pickup.
benefit: Avoids unprofitable small orders and encourages bigger baskets.

name: Cart restriction rules
summary: Rules stop certain combinations of items, make some items pickup-only, limit where items can be delivered, or stop restricted accounts from buying.
description: Rules that stop certain combinations, make some items pickup-only, or restrict items to certain accounts.
whyItMatters: Prevents orders that cannot or must not be fulfilled.
whatItDoes: Administrators block items that must not be in the same cart; shoppers see the reason.
Administrators make items pickup-only.
Items that cannot be delivered to the shopper's area are flagged at the delivery step.
Shoppers whose account has been restricted for suspected fraud cannot complete checkout.
Proposed: every change to a rule is recorded with who, when and the old and new values, to be confirmed.
clientRules: A rule switched on after items were added still stops the order at checkout.
benefit: Prevents orders that cannot or must not be fulfilled.

name: Pickup code / QR
summary: After ordering, the shopper receives a code or QR code to show when collecting the parcel.
description: After ordering, the customer receives a code or QR code to show when collecting the parcel.
whyItMatters: Only the right person collects the order.
whatItDoes: Shoppers choose an order code or a QR code, from the methods the client has enabled.
The code is sent when the order is ready for pickup, by SMS or email as the client sets.
Outlet staff enter or scan the code at collection, and it is checked before the parcel is handed over.
clientRules: Proposed: codes cannot be guessed, to be confirmed.
Proposed: a code works only at the outlet chosen for the order, and only once, to be confirmed.
Proposed: after a set number of wrong attempts, the code is blocked, to be confirmed.
benefit: Only the right person collects the order.

name: Assisted checkout
summary: An agent at an outlet places an order for a customer and records how the customer paid.
description: An agent at an outlet places an order for a customer and records how the customer paid.
whyItMatters: Serves customers who cannot order online themselves.
whatItDoes: Proposed: agents find or register a walk-in customer and place an order on their behalf, to be confirmed.
Each order records the agent and the outlet that placed it.
Agents see only the payment methods allowed for agent orders and record the payment taken.
Supervisors list agent orders by agent, outlet and date; agents see only their own outlet.
clientRules: An agent must be assigned to an outlet before they can place orders for customers.
benefit: Serves customers who cannot order online themselves, with every agent order traceable.

name: Estimated delivery at checkout
summary: Checkout shows the expected delivery date, or when the order can be collected.
description: Checkout shows the expected delivery date or when the order can be collected.
whyItMatters: Customers know when to expect their order.
whatItDoes: Shoppers see the earliest and latest delivery date for each delivery option.
Shoppers see, for each outlet, the date from which the order can be collected.
Proposed: where no estimate is available, a simpler transit-time estimate is shown if one exists, otherwise no date, to be confirmed.
Proposed: the estimate shown is kept with the order and shown again on the review step and in tracking, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: where shoppers can also choose a preferred delivery date, that list is shown as a choice and is not presented as the expected date, to be confirmed.
benefit: Shoppers know when to expect their order.

name: Checkout attributes
summary: Extra details can be asked for at checkout, such as a purchase-order number, special instructions or a gift message, optionally with a fee.
description: Extra fields at checkout such as a purchase-order number, special instructions or a gift message, optionally with a fee.
whyItMatters: Captures information business buyers and gift senders need.
whatItDoes: Business buyers enter their purchase-order number, which the client can make required.
Shoppers add a gift message or special instructions.
The client can charge a fee, with tax, for an option.
An option can show or hide depending on another choice.
benefit: Captures information business buyers and gift senders need.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: B2B on-account payment and credit limits
clientName: Business buying on account with credit limits
summary: Approved business customers buy now and pay later against an invoice, within a credit limit and agreed payment terms.
description: Approved business customers buy now and pay later against an invoice, within a credit limit and agreed payment terms (for example 30 days).
whyItMatters: Normal practice in business-to-business trade.
whatItDoes: Finance staff approve a company's credit account and set the limit, currency and payment terms.
Buyers of approved companies see "On account" as a payment method.
Orders above the available credit cannot be paid on account.
Proposed: when a credit account is suspended, "On account" is not offered, to be confirmed.
Proposed: the client can stop buying on account while a company has overdue amounts, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Available credit is the limit less amounts owed and unpaid orders on account.
Proposed: two orders from the same company at the same time cannot together exceed the limit, to be confirmed.
Every change to a credit account is recorded.
Standard reminder emails about unpaid orders follow the client's reminder setting, so buyers on account are not chased before their payment is due.
benefit: Supports normal business-to-business trade on credit, with credit risk controlled.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF); whether a licensed add-on is bought or the capability is built (technical and Product Owner decision) (ref PAID-STUB)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PH-INF, PAID-STUB / PH-INF / PAID-STUB pending

name: B2B quick order and bulk add
clientName: Quick and bulk ordering for businesses
summary: Business buyers order quickly by typing product codes, uploading a spreadsheet or using saved order lists.
description: Business buyers order quickly by typing product codes, uploading a spreadsheet or using saved order lists.
whyItMatters: Large repeat orders take minutes, not hours.
whatItDoes: Buyers type product codes and quantities; unknown codes are listed.
Proposed: buyers upload a spreadsheet of codes and quantities and see which lines were added or refused, to be confirmed.
Buyers add a whole saved order list to the cart.
clientRules: Every line is checked for stock and price as if added one by one.
benefit: Large repeat orders take minutes, not hours.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: B2B purchase approval
summary: Orders by company staff above a set amount must be approved by someone else in the company before they are placed.
description: Orders by company staff above a set amount must be approved by someone else in the company before they are placed.
whyItMatters: Companies keep control of spending.
whoUsesIt: Business buyers; company approvers; company administrators
whatItDoes: Company administrators set approval limits for each company role.
Buyers send orders above their limit to an approver.
Approvers approve or reject; a rejection needs a reason, and the buyer is told.
Once approved, the buyer places the order.
clientRules: The approver cannot be the person who asked for approval.
Proposed: if the cart changes after approval, approval is needed again, to be confirmed.
Changes to approval limits are recorded.
benefit: Companies keep control of spending.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF); whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PH-INF, WF-ENG / PH-INF / WF-ENG pending

name: Order confirmation
summary: After ordering, the shopper sees a confirmation page and receives a message with the order number.
description: After ordering, the customer sees a confirmation page and receives a message with the order number.
whyItMatters: Reassures the customer that the order went through.
whatItDoes: Shoppers see a confirmation page with the order number and the checkout reference.
Shoppers receive a confirmation email with the order number, with the invoice attached if the client chooses.
Proposed: for a checkout with several sellers, shoppers receive one confirmation listing all sub-orders, to be confirmed.
benefit: Reassures shoppers that the order went through.

name: Payment method framework and routing
clientName: Choosing which payment methods to offer
summary: The client switches payment methods on or off and decides where each is offered, for example by shop, country, customer type, rural or urban location, pickup or type of service.
description: The client switches payment methods on or off and decides where each is offered, for example by shop, country, customer type, rural or urban location, pickup or type of service.
whyItMatters: The right payment options appear for each situation.
whatItDoes: Administrators switch each payment method on or off; past orders keep their payment records.
Administrators limit a method by shop, country, customer type, rural or urban location, pickup or delivery, and type of service.
Shoppers see the methods available to them, with name, logo and any fee.
Clients with several card gateways can offer each one as a separate method under the same rules.
Proposed: if no method is available, checkout stops with a message and support contact, and no order is placed, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: when several rules apply to one method, it is shown only if every rule allows it, to be confirmed.
Proposed: rural or urban location is taken from the delivery area of the address or pickup point, to be confirmed.
benefit: The right payment options appear for each situation.

name: Card payments (framework)
summary: Shoppers pay by debit or credit card on the bank's secure payment page. Card details never reach the shop, and refunds go back to the card.
description: Customers pay by debit or credit card on the bank's secure payment page. Card details never touch the shop, and refunds go back to the card. Each bank or gateway is connected as a separate adapter.
whyItMatters: Safe card payments that stay within card-security rules.
whatItDoes: Shoppers are taken to the bank's secure page to enter card details.
Successful payments mark the order as paid; failed or cancelled payments leave the order unpaid, and the shopper can retry.
Where the gateway supports it, extra card security checks (3-D Secure) are used.
Finance staff refund all or part of a card payment back to the same card.
Each bank or gateway is connected separately, so a new gateway needs no change to checkout.
clientRules: The shop never receives or stores card details. The current platform version no longer stores card details at all.
Any ready-made card gateway connector must be confirmed as available for the current platform version; otherwise it is built.
benefit: Safe card payments that stay within card-security rules.

name: PayPal
summary: Shoppers can pay with PayPal.
description: Customers can pay with PayPal.
whyItMatters: Convenient for international buyers.
whatItDoes: Shoppers choose PayPal and pay with their PayPal account.
Finance staff refund all or part of a PayPal payment.
benefit: Convenient for international buyers.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether PayPal and global payment processors are acceptable under the rule that gateways are operated by a Central Bank of Kenya-regulated bank (KTDA to decide) (ref K-08)

name: Mobile money (framework)
summary: Shoppers pay from their mobile-money wallet: a payment request appears on their phone and they confirm with their PIN. Each provider (M-Pesa, Mpamba, Airtel Money) connects separately.
description: Customers pay from their mobile-money wallet: a payment request pops up on their phone, they confirm with their PIN, and the shop is told the result. Includes reversals, refunds and matching payments to orders. Each provider (M-Pesa, Mpamba, Airtel Money) connects as an adapter. Customers can also pay by scanning a QR code where the provider supports it.
whyItMatters: Both clients require mobile money: KTDA names M-Pesa; Malawi Post names TNM Mpamba and Airtel Money.
whatItDoes: Shoppers enter their mobile number and confirm the request on their phone with their PIN.
Where the provider supports it, shoppers pay by scanning a QR code.
The order is marked paid when the provider confirms success; if the payment fails, the shopper can retry within the time allowed.
Proposed: if no answer arrives in time, the platform asks the provider for the status, to be confirmed.
Reversals made by the provider are recorded against the order.
Where the provider supports it, refunds go back to the shopper's wallet.
New providers can be added without changing how mobile money works for shoppers.
clientRules: Proposed: a payment that succeeds after the order was cancelled for non-payment is flagged for finance staff, to be confirmed.
benefit: Both clients require mobile money: KTDA names M-Pesa; Malawi Post names TNM Mpamba and Airtel Money.

name: Bank transfer
summary: Buyers pay by bank transfer using a unique reference, and incoming payments are matched to orders.
description: Customers pay by bank transfer using a unique reference, and incoming payments are matched to orders.
whyItMatters: Suits large business payments.
whatItDoes: Buyers receive a unique payment reference with the client's bank details on the confirmation page and email.
Bank statement lines with a valid reference and the exact amount are matched and the order is marked paid.
Payments with a different amount or an unknown reference go to a list for finance staff; the order is not marked paid.
Proposed: banks can send payment notices directly to the platform for matching, to be confirmed.
Proposed: each shop can show its own bank account, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: unpaid bank-transfer orders follow the client's reminder, flag or cancel rules (PRD-INV-004), to be confirmed.
Proposed: the platform's standard reminder emails for unpaid orders are switched off, so buyers waiting for a bank transfer to arrive are not chased, to be confirmed.
benefit: Suits large business payments, with orders released without manual searching.

name: Letters of credit
summary: Buyers pay using a letter of credit from their bank. The client checks the letter of credit before shipping.
description: Buyers pay using a letter of credit from their bank; the client checks the letter of credit before shipping.
whyItMatters: A standard, secure way to pay for international trade.
whoUsesIt: International buyers; export staff; finance staff; client administrators
whatItDoes: Business buyers choose letter of credit at payment; the order is created as unpaid with a letter-of-credit record.
Finance staff record that the letter of credit is verified, which releases the order for shipping.
Proposed: when a letter of credit is rejected or expires, the buyer and export staff are told, to be confirmed.
Proposed: letters of credit and escrow are offered only to bulk buyers, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Goods cannot be shipped until the letter of credit is verified.
What counts as a bulk buyer is not stated in the source and requires confirmation.
benefit: A standard, secure way to pay for international trade.

name: Escrow and staged release
summary: The buyer's money is held safely and released to the seller in stages, for example on dispatch, on delivery or when the buyer accepts the goods.
description: The buyer's money is held safely and released to the seller in stages, for example on dispatch, on delivery or when the buyer accepts the goods.
whyItMatters: Both sides are protected in large transactions.
whatItDoes: Bulk buyers pay into an escrow account held with a bank or payment provider.
Money is released to the seller in stages when goods are dispatched, delivered or accepted.
Proposed: no further release is made while a dispute is open, to be confirmed.
Proposed: if a release fails, finance staff are alerted and can retry, to be confirmed.
Proposed: buyers or finance staff can raise a payment dispute on an escrow order, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Every escrow action is recorded.
benefit: Both sides are protected in large transactions.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: the payment model for paying sellers directly, and whether a payment-service or e-money licence is needed (Product Owner and legal advice) (ref PAY-DIRECT)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 pending

name: Cash on delivery and cash at outlet
clientName: Cash on delivery and cash at an outlet
summary: Shoppers pay in cash on delivery or at an outlet, using a secure reference. Banker's cheques and payment slips paid to the client are also accepted and matched by staff.
description: Customers pay in cash on delivery or at an outlet, using a secure reference; the client decides which sellers, items or areas allow it. Banker's cheques and payment slips paid to the client (local instruments to be confirmed per client) are also accepted and matched by staff.
whyItMatters: Serves customers without cards or mobile money.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers; outlet staff; couriers; finance staff; client administrators
whatItDoes: Shoppers choose cash on delivery where every item, seller and the delivery area allow it.
Shoppers choose cash at an outlet and receive a secure payment reference.
Outlet staff take the cash against the reference, mark the order paid and print a receipt.
Proposed: couriers record the cash collected at delivery and the order is marked paid, to be confirmed.
Finance staff record banker's cheques and payment slips against orders.
Outlet cash payments are reconciled against closed shifts.
clientRules: The client decides which sellers, items and areas allow cash on delivery.
Which local instruments are accepted is to be confirmed for each client.
benefit: Serves customers without cards or mobile money.

name: Wallet and store credit
summary: Shoppers hold a balance in the shop, top it up and spend from it.
description: Customers hold a balance in the shop, top it up and spend from it.
whyItMatters: Faster repeat payments, and refunds can go to the wallet.
whatItDoes: Shoppers top up their wallet with any active payment method; the balance rises only after the top-up succeeds.
Shoppers pay for orders from their wallet.
Shoppers see their balance and wallet history in their account.
Refunds can be credited to the wallet when the shopper chooses.
clientRules: How a wallet is used when the balance is lower than the order total is still to be decided.
benefit: Faster repeat payments and instant refunds.
status: On hold: FG-06, PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01, WAL-01
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether postal operations, e-Government services and Malawi Post financial services are part of the product (Malawi Post to decide) (ref FG-06); the payment model for paying sellers directly, and whether a payment-service or e-money licence is needed (Product Owner and legal advice) (ref PAY-DIRECT); how a wallet balance is spent at checkout (Malawi Post and Product Owner) (ref WAL-01)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision FG-06, PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01, WAL-01 / FG-06 / PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 / WAL-01 pending

name: Split payments
summary: Each customer payment is automatically split into the seller's share, the delivery fee and the client's commission.
description: Each customer payment is automatically split into the seller's share, the delivery fee and the client's commission.
whyItMatters: Everyone gets their correct share without manual calculation.
whatItDoes: Each paid order item is split into seller share, delivery fee and platform commission.
Where the provider can split payments itself, the split is passed to it; otherwise it is used for seller payouts.
On a partial refund, split amounts are reduced in proportion.
Proposed: if no commission rule applies to an item, finance staff are alerted, to be confirmed.
clientRules: No split is made for orders paid directly to the seller (PRD-PAY-035); commission is invoiced instead.
benefit: Everyone gets their correct share without manual calculation.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: the payment model for paying sellers directly, and whether a payment-service or e-money licence is needed (Product Owner and legal advice) (ref PAY-DIRECT)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 pending

name: Payment status lifecycle
summary: Every payment has a clear status (started, pending, successful, failed, reversed) linked to its order. Shoppers see the status and can try again.
description: Every payment has a clear status (started, pending, successful, failed, reversed) linked to its order; customers see the status and can try again.
whyItMatters: Fewer 'did my payment go through?' calls.
whatItDoes: Every payment attempt is recorded with its status and linked to its order.
Shoppers see the payment status and what to do next.
Shoppers retry a failed or pending payment.
Proposed: shoppers pay once for a checkout split into one order per seller, and every seller's order is marked paid, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Every status change is time-stamped and recorded.
Proposed: retry is not offered once the order has been cancelled for non-payment, to be confirmed.
An unpaid order is never cancelled while a payment for it has succeeded.

Proposed: the platform's standard reminder emails and automatic cancelling of unpaid orders stay switched off unless the client asks for them, because orders paid on account, by letter of credit or by bank transfer are unpaid for a long time by design, to be confirmed.
benefit: Fewer "did my payment go through?" calls.

name: Payment idempotency
summary: If a shopper or the network retries a payment, the shopper is charged only once.
description: Ensures that if a customer or the network retries a payment, they are only charged once.
whyItMatters: Prevents double charges.
whatItDoes: A repeated payment request does not start a second charge.
A repeated confirmation from a provider is recognised and ignored.
Placing the same order twice in quick succession does not create a duplicate order.
A retried checkout uses the same order reference with the provider.
benefit: Prevents double charges.

name: Payment receipts
summary: Payment receipts are sent by email and SMS.
description: Payment receipts are sent by email and SMS.
whyItMatters: Customers have proof of payment.
whatItDoes: Shoppers receive a receipt when their payment succeeds, on the channels the client sets.
Proposed: shoppers without a mobile number receive the receipt by email only, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: a failed SMS does not stop the email receipt, to be confirmed.
The text-message service that comes with the platform (Twilio) must be confirmed for coverage, cost and data protection in Kenya and Malawi; a local text-message company can be connected instead.
benefit: Customers have proof of payment.

name: Payment reconciliation
summary: The platform automatically matches the shop's payments against statements from payment providers and produces a daily file for finance.
description: Automatically matches the shop's payments against statements from payment providers and produces a daily file for finance.
whyItMatters: Finance can trust the numbers and find gaps quickly.
whatItDoes: Provider statements are collected or uploaded and each line is classed as matched or unmatched.
Finance staff work through unmatched items and resolve each one with a required note.
A daily reconciliation file is produced for download.
Proposed: where a provider has no direct link, finance staff upload its file and the same matching runs, to be confirmed.
Amounts settled by providers are compared with seller settlement totals.
clientRules: Every resolution is recorded.
benefit: Finance can trust the numbers and find gaps quickly.

name: Payment fees
summary: The client adds a fee for particular payment methods and keeps dated versions of provider and platform fees.
description: Add a fee for particular payment methods and keep versioned schedules of provider and platform fees.
whyItMatters: Covers payment costs transparently.
whatItDoes: Finance staff set a fixed or percentage fee for a payment method; shoppers see it before paying.
Finance staff save new fee schedules with a start date; orders keep the fee that applied when placed.
Cash on delivery fees can differ by rural or urban location and by service level, such as express or standard.
Proposed: the fee charged on each item is kept with the schedule version, so refunds adjust it correctly, to be confirmed.
clientRules: Proposed: every change to a fee schedule is recorded with who, when and the old and new values, to be confirmed.
benefit: Covers payment costs transparently.

name: Refunds
summary: Full or partial refunds go back to the original payment method, with status tracking. Large refunds need approval, and fees are adjusted in proportion on partial refunds.
description: Full or partial refunds back to the original payment method, with status tracking; large refunds need approval. When part of an order is refunded, related fees are adjusted in proportion, and customers are shown the expected refund time for each payment method.
whyItMatters: Customers get their money back properly and fraud is controlled.
whatItDoes: Finance staff refund all or part of an order to the original payment method.
Proposed: where the method cannot refund, the refund is recorded as made outside the platform, or to the wallet if chosen, to be confirmed.
On a partial refund, fees, commission and seller shares are adjusted in proportion.
Shoppers see the refund status and the expected time for their payment method.
Shoppers receive one refund notification when the refund completes.
Refunds from returns and other order changes go through the same controlled process.
clientRules: Refunds above a set amount need approval, and the requester cannot approve their own refund.
benefit: Customers get their money back properly and fraud is controlled.

name: Chargebacks
summary: The platform tracks card payments that customers dispute with their bank (chargebacks).
description: Tracks card payments that customers dispute with their bank (chargebacks).
whyItMatters: Clients can respond in time and reduce losses.
whatItDoes: A chargeback case is opened, from the gateway or by staff, with reason, amount and response deadline.
Proposed: finance staff are reminded before the response deadline, to be confirmed.
Proposed: when a case is lost, the payment is shown as reversed and the order as refunded, to be confirmed.
Proposed: when a case is won, the case is closed with no change to the payment, to be confirmed.
benefit: Clients can respond in time and reduce losses.

name: Payment and order risk controls
summary: Checks that the client sets flag suspicious behaviour, such as many payments in a short time or many accounts on one device.
description: Configurable checks that flag suspicious behaviour, such as many payments in a short time, many accounts on one device or other warning signs.
whyItMatters: Reduces fraud losses.
whatItDoes: Fraud staff set rules on how many payment attempts are allowed in a period; breaches are flagged or blocked.
Accounts are flagged when too many use the same device.
Fraud staff switch rules on or off and change limits; every change is recorded.
Customers with an account restriction, or on a block list, cannot complete checkout.
Proposed: a flagged order can be put on hold before shipping, to be confirmed.
Proposed: a score from an optional fraud-scoring service can trigger a rule, to be confirmed.
clientRules: The message shown to a blocked customer does not give the reason.
benefit: Reduces fraud losses.

name: Payments operations console
summary: A screen for finance staff to see payment records and problem payments and to step in manually, with every action recorded.
description: A screen for finance staff to see payment logs and problem payments and to step in manually, with every action recorded.
whyItMatters: Payment problems are fixed quickly and transparently.
whatItDoes: Finance staff search payments by date, method, status, order or provider reference.
Finance staff see problem payments in one view.
Finance staff check a status again, mark a payment paid with evidence, or cancel a payment attempt.
clientRules: A reason is required for every manual action, and only staff with permission can take one.
benefit: Payment problems are fixed quickly and transparently.

name: Tax calculation
summary: The platform calculates tax using tax categories and rates per country or region, and shows prices including or excluding tax as the client chooses.
description: Calculates tax using tax categories and rates per country or region, and shows prices including or excluding tax as configured.
whyItMatters: Correct tax on every sale.
whatItDoes: Finance staff set tax categories and rates by country or region.
Tax is calculated on each order item.
Shoppers see items, taxes, payment fees and delivery fees before paying.
benefit: Correct tax on every sale.

name: Tax on fees and tax reporting
clientName: Tax on fees and tax reports
summary: The platform calculates tax on the client's own commissions and fees, and produces tax reports and files for tax returns.
description: Calculates tax on the client's own commissions and fees, and produces tax reports and files for tax filing.
whyItMatters: Supports the client's tax returns.
whatItDoes: Tax on platform commission is calculated and kept with each seller share.
Finance staff run tax reports by tax category, rate and type of transaction for a period, and export them.
Administrators change commission, fee and tax rules with a start date, without developers.
clientRules: The old rule applies until a new rule's start date; every change is recorded.
benefit: Supports the client's tax returns.

name: Bulk disbursements
summary: The platform pays many recipients at once, for example farmers or beneficiaries, after approval, then tracks each payment.
description: Pays many recipients at once (for example farmers or beneficiaries) after approval, then matches the payments. Each payment's status (succeeded, failed, reversed) is shown with a reason, and failed payments are retried automatically.
whyItMatters: Large payout runs become efficient and controlled.
whatItDoes: Finance staff upload a list of recipients; invalid rows are reported and must be fixed first.
A second authorised person approves the batch before money is sent.
Each payment shows its status (succeeded, failed, reversed) with a reason.
Payments that fail for temporary reasons are retried automatically.
Proposed: where the bank offers it, account numbers and holder names are checked before payment, to be confirmed.
benefit: Large payout runs become efficient and controlled.

name: Multi-currency settlement
summary: The customer pays in their own currency while the client receives money in its base currency, with the exchange rate shown to the customer.
description: The customer pays in their own currency while the client receives money in its base currency, with the exchange rate shown to the customer.
whyItMatters: Clear, fair cross-currency payments.
whatItDoes: Shoppers choose their currency and see prices and totals in it.
Where the gateway supports it, the customer is charged in their own currency, with the rate and any conversion fee shown before paying.
Proposed: where the gateway settles only in the base currency, the customer is charged in it and sees the converted amount first, to be confirmed.
clientRules: The currency rules for each client are still to be decided.
benefit: Clear, fair cross-currency payments.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: how a US dollar base currency works with M-Pesa settlement in Kenya shillings (KTDA to decide) (ref C-FX)

name: Payment connector SDK
summary: A standard way for every payment provider to connect to the platform: start a payment, receive the result, check status, reverse, refund, get the statement and pay out.
description: A standard technical 'plug' that every payment provider connects to: start a payment, receive the result, check status, reverse, refund, get the reconciliation file and pay out.
whyItMatters: A new payment provider is added by building one adapter, not by changing the shop.
whatItDoes: Each provider connection states which actions it supports.
Proposed: where a provider does not support an action, finance staff are offered a manual way instead, to be confirmed.
Messages from providers are checked as genuine before any payment status changes.
Administrators enter each provider's login details for their own installation.
clientRules: Provider login details are stored encrypted and are never copied into client setup packages.
benefit: A new payment provider is added by building one connection, not by changing the shop.

name: Fiscal e-invoicing framework
summary: Each invoice is sent to the tax authority's electronic invoicing system, and the official fiscal number or QR code is printed on it. Credit notes are handled the same way, and each country connects separately.
description: Sends each invoice to the tax authority's electronic invoicing system, retries if it fails, prints the official fiscal number or QR code on the invoice, and also handles credit notes (corrections and refunds on invoices); each country connects as an adapter.
whyItMatters: Kenya (KRA eTIMS) and Malawi (MRA EIS) operate electronic invoicing; the clients must confirm how it applies to them (decision E-INV).
whatItDoes: Invoices are sent to the tax authority when issued.
Failed sends are retried; persistent failures alert finance staff.
Shoppers receive invoices that carry the official fiscal number or QR code.
Credit notes for corrections and refunds are sent the same way.
Tax on each fiscal invoice is the tax calculated for the order.
clientRules: Whether electronic invoicing applies to each client is to be confirmed.
benefit: Kenya (KRA eTIMS) and Malawi (MRA EIS) operate electronic invoicing; the platform is ready once each client confirms how it applies.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF); whether statutory electronic invoicing (KRA eTIMS in Kenya, MRA EIS in Malawi) is required (both clients to confirm) (ref E-INV); which document and QR-code generation product is used (technical decision) (ref DOC-LIB)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PH-INF, E-INV, DOC-LIB / PH-INF / E-INV / DOC-LIB pending

name: KRA eTIMS adapter
summary: Connects invoices to the Kenya Revenue Authority's electronic invoicing system (eTIMS).
description: Connects invoices to the Kenya Revenue Authority's electronic invoicing system (eTIMS).
whyItMatters: Legal invoicing in Kenya (to be confirmed with KTDA).
whatItDoes: Invoices and credit notes are sent to KRA eTIMS using KTDA's own credentials.
Sending, retries and printing of the fiscal number or QR code work as described for electronic tax invoicing (PRD-PAY-025).
clientRules: Expected to apply to KTDA; to be confirmed with KTDA, and the eTIMS specification is still to be received.
benefit: Legal invoicing in Kenya, to be confirmed with KTDA.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF); whether statutory electronic invoicing (KRA eTIMS in Kenya, MRA EIS in Malawi) is required (both clients to confirm) (ref E-INV); which document and QR-code generation product is used (technical decision) (ref DOC-LIB)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PH-INF, E-INV, DOC-LIB / PH-INF / E-INV / DOC-LIB pending

summary: Connects invoices to the Malawi Revenue Authority's electronic invoicing system (EIS).
