whyItMatters: Legal invoicing in Malawi (to be confirmed with Malawi Post).
whatItDoes: Invoices and credit notes are sent to MRA EIS using Malawi Post's own credentials.
Sending, retries and printing of the fiscal number or QR code work as described for electronic tax invoicing (PRD-PAY-025).
clientRules: Expected to apply to Malawi Post; to be confirmed with Malawi Post, and the EIS specification is still to be received.
benefit: Legal invoicing in Malawi, to be confirmed with Malawi Post.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF); whether statutory electronic invoicing (KRA eTIMS in Kenya, MRA EIS in Malawi) is required (both clients to confirm) (ref E-INV); which document and QR-code generation product is used (technical decision) (ref DOC-LIB)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PH-INF, E-INV, DOC-LIB / PH-INF / E-INV / DOC-LIB pending

name: M-Pesa (Kenya) adapter
summary: Connects the shop to Safaricom M-Pesa in Kenya: a payment request appears on the shopper's phone, with confirmations and reversals.
description: Connects the shop to Safaricom M-Pesa in Kenya: a payment request appears on the customer's phone, with confirmations and reversals.
whyItMatters: KTDA requires M-Pesa payments.
whatItDoes: Shoppers pay with M-Pesa through a request on their phone.
Confirmations, status checks and reversals work as for all mobile money (PRD-PAY-004).
KTDA sets its own till or paybill number.
clientRules: The settlement currency for M-Pesa payments is still to be decided.
benefit: Meets KTDA's requirement for M-Pesa payments.

name: TNM Mpamba adapter
summary: Connects the shop to TNM Mpamba mobile money in Malawi.
description: Connects the shop to TNM Mpamba mobile money in Malawi.
whyItMatters: Malawi Post requires TNM Mpamba payments.
whoUsesIt: Malawian shoppers; Malawi Post finance staff
whatItDoes: Shoppers pay with TNM Mpamba from their wallet.
Payments and refunds work as for all mobile money (PRD-PAY-004), over a secure connection.
benefit: Meets Malawi Post's requirement for TNM Mpamba payments.

name: Airtel Money adapter
summary: Connects the shop to Airtel Money in Malawi, and in Kenya if needed.
description: Connects the shop to Airtel Money (Malawi, and Kenya if needed).
whyItMatters: Malawi Post requires Airtel Money payments; the same adapter can serve Kenya if a client asks.
whatItDoes: Shoppers pay with Airtel Money from their wallet.
Payments and refunds work as for all mobile money (PRD-PAY-004), set up per country.
benefit: Meets Malawi Post's requirement for Airtel Money, and can serve Kenya if a client asks.

name: KTDA bank card gateway adapter
summary: Connects card payments to the Central Bank of Kenya-regulated bank gateway that KTDA chooses.
description: Connects card payments to the Central Bank of Kenya-regulated bank gateway that KTDA chooses.
whyItMatters: Meets KTDA's requirement for a regulated bank gateway.
whatItDoes: Shoppers pay by debit or credit card through the bank KTDA names, as described for card payments (PRD-PAY-002).
Each card payment records the bank's reference.
clientRules: KTDA must name the bank gateway; the KTDA role that manages it is to be confirmed.
benefit: Meets KTDA's requirement for a regulated bank gateway.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: the name of the KTDA bank (KTDA to provide) (ref KG-04)

name: MPC card gateway adapter
summary: Connects card payments to the gateway Malawi Post chooses.
description: Connects card payments to the gateway Malawi Post chooses.
whyItMatters: Enables card payments for Malawi Post.
whatItDoes: Shoppers pay by card through the gateway Malawi Post names, as described for card payments (PRD-PAY-002).
Card details never reach the shop; where cards are saved, only a secure stand-in from the gateway is kept.
clientRules: Malawi Post must name the gateway; the Malawi Post role that manages it is to be confirmed.
benefit: Enables card payments for Malawi Post.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: the name of the Malawi Post card payment provider (Malawi Post to provide) (ref MG-03)

name: Accounts receivable
summary: For customers who buy on credit: account statements, credit notes, matching payments to invoices and lists of overdue amounts by age.
description: For customers who buy on credit: account statements, credit notes, matching payments to invoices and lists of overdue amounts by age.
whyItMatters: The client gets paid and tracks who owes what.
whatItDoes: Each invoice to a credit customer becomes an amount owed, with a due date from the agreed payment terms.
Finance staff match payments received to one or more invoices; part-payments are allowed.
Finance staff see overdue amounts grouped by age.
Business buyers see their statement, open invoices and overdue amounts in their account.
Proposed: where an invoice has been passed to a lender, the buyer is shown the lender as the party to pay, to be confirmed.
clientRules: The client sets the age groups.
benefit: The client gets paid and tracks who owes what.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether a licensed add-on is bought or the capability is built (technical and Product Owner decision) (ref PAID-STUB)

name: Outlet receipt printing and cash-up
summary: Outlet counters print small (80 mm) receipts and pickup slips, and each outlet closes its cash at the end of a shift.
description: Prints small (80 mm) receipts and pickup slips at outlet counters, and lets each outlet close its cash at the end of a shift.
whyItMatters: Supports counter service at post offices and outlets.
whoUsesIt: Outlet staff; walk-in customers; finance staff
whatItDoes: Proposed: outlet staff record how a walk-in customer paid and print an 80 mm receipt or pickup slip, to be confirmed.
Staff close a shift by entering the cash counted; the expected and counted amounts and the difference are recorded.
Proposed: shifts with a difference are flagged for finance review, to be confirmed.
Cash payments from closed shifts appear in payment reconciliation.
clientRules: A closed shift cannot be changed.
benefit: Supports counter service at post offices and outlets.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: Direct payment to the seller
summary: The buyer pays the seller directly into the seller's own payment account, such as an M-Pesa till or paybill, card merchant account or bank account, instead of paying the client first.
description: The buyer pays the seller directly into the seller's own payment account (for example the seller's own M-Pesa till or paybill, card merchant account or bank account) instead of paying the client first. Each seller connects their own account through the payment connection kit, so the platform receives the payment result and records it against the order. The client decides which sellers or shops use this model; refunds are made by the seller, and the platform records them and opens a dispute case if the buyer contests. Split payments, escrow and seller payouts do not apply to orders paid this way; commission is collected through 'Commission invoicing to sellers'.
whyItMatters: Lets sellers keep full control of their own money and lets the client run a marketplace without holding sellers' funds.
whoUsesIt: Sellers; shoppers; business buyers; client administrators
whatItDoes: Sellers connect their own payment account; the platform receives the payment result and records it against the order.
The client decides which sellers or shops use direct payment; others use the normal flow.
Sellers make refunds themselves, and the platform records them.
A buyer who contests a refund can have a dispute case opened.
clientRules: Direct payment works only for orders from a single seller; these come from the checkout that splits a cart by seller, not from separate carts per seller.
Split payments, escrow and seller payouts do not apply; commission is collected by invoicing the seller.
benefit: Sellers keep full control of their own money, and the client runs a marketplace without holding sellers' funds.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: acceptance by the Product Owner of features recommended without a client source (ref PO-REC-v8); the payment model for paying sellers directly, and whether a payment-service or e-money licence is needed (Product Owner and legal advice) (ref PAY-DIRECT)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PO-REC-v8, PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 / PO-REC-v8 / PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 pending

name: Offline direct payment confirmation
clientName: Confirming payments made outside the platform
summary: When a buyer pays a seller outside the platform (bank transfer, cash, cheque or letter of credit), the seller marks the order as paid and uploads proof, and the buyer confirms or contests it.
description: When a buyer pays a seller outside the platform (bank transfer, cash, cheque or letter of credit), the seller marks the order as paid and uploads proof; the buyer can confirm, and a contested payment becomes a dispute case.
whyItMatters: Keeps the order record complete when a buyer pays a seller outside the platform, for example by bank transfer, cash, cheque or letter of credit.
whatItDoes: Sellers mark an order as paid and upload proof of payment.
Buyers confirm the payment, and the order is marked paid.
Buyers contest the payment, which opens a dispute case.
Proposed: uploaded proof files are checked before they are accepted, to be confirmed.
benefit: The order record stays complete when buyers pay sellers outside the platform.
status: On hold: WF-ENG, PO-REC-v8, PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG); acceptance by the Product Owner of features recommended without a client source (ref PO-REC-v8); the payment model for paying sellers directly, and whether a payment-service or e-money licence is needed (Product Owner and legal advice) (ref PAY-DIRECT)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision WF-ENG, PO-REC-v8, PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 / WF-ENG / PO-REC-v8 / PAY-DIRECT / LIC-01 pending

name: Order management console
summary: One screen where staff find, view and manage every order, with its full history in one place.
description: A screen where staff find, view and edit orders, add notes, change status, export or import orders and print invoices and packing slips. Staff can also see customers' current carts and wishlists to help them.
whyItMatters: Staff manage every order from one place.
whoUsesIt: Client order staff; authorised users who export orders
whatItDoes: Search orders by date, status, stage, payment, delivery, shop, seller, product, customer contact details and order number.
Open one view of an order with its stages, notes, audit record, payments, shipments, holds and documents.
Edit orders and add notes; every edit needs a reason.
Print the invoice and the packing slips of an order.
Export the selected orders to Excel or XML for offline analysis.
See customers' current carts and wishlists to help customers who are stuck.
See the stage and due time of each order so overdue orders can be handled first.
clientRules: Only users with export rights can export orders.
benefit: Staff manage every order from one place.

name: Configurable order status model
summary: The client defines its own order stages and which moves between stages are allowed.
description: The client defines its own order stages and which moves between stages are allowed.
whyItMatters: Order handling matches each client's real process.
whoUsesIt: Client administrators; client order staff; shoppers; business buyers
whatItDoes: Define the order stages and the allowed moves between them, without development work.
Use a ready-made stage set, for example for Malawi Post: Created, Awaiting Payment, Paid, Processing, Shipped, Ready for Pickup, Delivered, Completed, Cancelled, Returned, Refunded.
Move orders forward automatically when payment, dispatch, pickup readiness, delivery or refund happens.
Show shoppers the current stage of their order and send a message when a visible stage changes.
Decide when an order counts as confirmed: at placement, at payment, or after seller or staff acceptance.
Let a business buyer confirm acceptance of a delivered order so the seller can be paid and the order closed (proposed, to be confirmed).
clientRules: Moves that are not allowed are blocked and recorded.
Where an acceptance window is set, a delivered order with no response and no open dispute is treated as accepted when the window ends.
An order cannot be accepted while a dispute on it is open.
benefit: Order handling matches each client's real process.

name: Order interventions with reason codes and audit
clientName: Order changes with reasons and audit
summary: Every manual change to an order needs a reason, is approved where required and is recorded permanently.
description: Any manual change to an order needs a reason, is approved where required, and is recorded permanently with before-and-after snapshots. Simultaneous actions on the same order are handled safely and in the right sequence, and a snapshot of the order is saved at key stages such as settlement and close-out.
whyItMatters: Full accountability for order changes.
whoUsesIt: Client order staff; client managers; auditors
whatItDoes: Require a reason, chosen from a client list, for every manual change to an order.
Record every status change and key change (totals, items, addresses, delivery method) with before and after values.
Hold sensitive changes, such as editing an order total, until a different authorised person approves them.
Handle simultaneous actions on the same order safely, so no change is lost.
Save a read-only copy of the order at key stages, for example when paid, completed or cancelled.
clientRules: The audit record cannot be edited or deleted.
A deleted order note needs a reason, and its text is kept in the audit record.
benefit: Full accountability for every order change.

name: Cancellation rules
summary: Buyers and sellers cancel orders according to policy, giving a reason; orders are cancelled automatically if a seller misses its deadline.
description: Buyers and sellers cancel orders according to policy, giving a reason; orders are cancelled automatically if a seller misses its deadline.
whyItMatters: Fair, consistent cancellations.
whatItDoes: Buyers cancel an order before fulfilment starts, choosing a reason.
Sellers reject an order they cannot fulfil, giving a reason, and the buyer is told.
The platform cancels an order automatically when a seller does not accept it by the deadline.
Apply a penalty to the seller for a missed deadline or a rejection, deducted at the next settlement.
Start a refund automatically when a paid order is cancelled.
clientRules: Buyers can cancel only before the seller has packed or handed over the order and within the cancellation window set by the client.
A seller rejection always needs a reason.
An order on hold can still be cancelled.
If a seller can supply only part of an order, the partial fulfilment process (PRD-ORD-006) applies instead.
The platform can also cancel orders left unpaid after a set time; this standard option stays off unless the client asks for it, because unpaid orders are handled per payment method (PRD-INV-004).
benefit: Fair, consistent cancellations for buyers and sellers.

name: Seller order processing
summary: Sellers accept, pack and hand over their orders for delivery from their own dashboard.
description: Sellers accept orders, pack them and hand them over for delivery from their own dashboard, and receive notifications.
whyItMatters: Sellers fulfil marketplace orders efficiently.
whatItDoes: See a dashboard of own orders with the action due, stage, due time and any hold.
Accept, mark as packed and hand over each order; each step is recorded.
Receive messages for new orders, payment confirmation and approaching deadlines.
Print pick lists and packing lists for several orders at once.
clientRules: A seller can accept an order once it is paid, or before payment for payment methods the client allows, for example cash on delivery.
A seller acts only on own orders.
An order on hold cannot be handed over.
benefit: Sellers fulfil marketplace orders efficiently.

name: Partial fulfilment approval
summary: If only part of an order can be supplied, the buyer decides whether to accept the partial delivery.
description: If only part of an order can be supplied, the buyer is asked whether to accept the partial delivery.
whyItMatters: The buyer stays in control of what they receive.
whatItDoes: Sellers report which items or quantities they cannot supply.
The buyer is told which items are affected and the amount involved.
The buyer accepts the reduced order, and the difference is refunded.
The buyer rejects it, and the order is cancelled and refunded if paid.
clientRules: A paid order is never reduced without the buyer's acceptance.
If the buyer does not answer in the time set by the client, the default action set by the client applies.
Where the client turns this feature off, the seller either supplies the full order or rejects it.
benefit: The buyer stays in control of what they receive and pay for.

name: Order numbering
summary: The client chooses the order number format, for example MP-2026-000123.
description: The client chooses the order number format, for example MP-2026-000123.
whyItMatters: Order numbers fit the client's records.
whatItDoes: Set an order number format with prefix, year, month, day and running number.
Pad the running number to a fixed length, for example 000123.
Use a different format for each shop, for example to separate trade and retail orders.
Use a different format for each order type: goods, service, quote or repeat order (proposed, to be confirmed).
clientRules: A format with an unknown element is refused when saved.
benefit: Order numbers fit the client's records and reporting.

name: Reorder
summary: Customers repeat a past order with one click; prices and stock are checked again.
description: Customers repeat a past order with one click; prices and stock are checked again.
whyItMatters: Quick repeat buying.
whatItDoes: Repeat a past order in one click; items go into the cart at current prices.
Repeat only one seller part of an order that was split between sellers.
See a warning for items that can no longer be added.
benefit: Quick repeat buying.

name: Invoices
summary: PDF invoices for each order and each seller, a combined receipt, and the company, tax and seller details.
description: PDF invoices for each order and each seller, a combined receipt, the company and tax details, seller identity and fees.
whyItMatters: Proper invoices for customers and for accounting.
whatItDoes: Issue invoices automatically at the point the client chooses: order placed, paid or completed.
Produce a separate invoice for each seller in a marketplace order.
Produce one combined receipt listing every seller, amount and the total paid when a checkout is split.
Show the company name, address and tax number, the seller name and tax number, platform fees and tax per rate.
Attach the invoice to the order email.
Print the official tax number and QR code on the invoice where the tax authority provides them.
clientRules: An invoice is not issued while a required company detail is missing; administrators are told, and issuing resumes once it is filled in.
benefit: Proper invoices for customers and for accounting.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: which document and QR-code generation product is used (technical decision) (ref DOC-LIB)

name: Order holds
summary: Staff place an order on hold for fraud or compliance checks; it cannot be shipped until released.
description: Staff place an order on hold for fraud or compliance checks; it cannot be shipped until released.
whyItMatters: Stops suspicious orders being fulfilled.
whatItDoes: Place an order on hold with a reason; the hold shows on the order and on the seller dashboard.
Release the hold with a reason so fulfilment continues.
Place a hold automatically when a payment risk rule says so (proposed, to be confirmed).
Apply the same shipment checks to every client, with or without optional packs (proposed, to be confirmed).
clientRules: While a hold is active, no one can create a shipment, mark it shipped, ready for pickup or delivered, or hand it over.
A hold does not block cancellation or payment.
Placing and releasing holds is recorded.
benefit: Stops suspicious orders being fulfilled.

name: Cut-offs and service levels
summary: Daily order cut-off times and the promised handling time for each delivery service.
description: Sets daily cut-off times for orders and the promised handling time for each delivery service.
whyItMatters: Clear promises and on-time fulfilment.
whatItDoes: Set a daily cut-off time for each service level, using working days.
Set the handling time for each service level, such as standard, express and pickup.
Calculate and show the due time of each order to staff and sellers.
Flag overdue orders and escalate them to the people set for that service level.
Flag and escalate parcels not collected by the pickup deadline.
Publish the service levels to sellers.
clientRules: An order placed after the cut-off starts its clock on the next working day.
Missed seller deadlines lead to automatic cancellation and penalties (PRD-ORD-004).
The escalation levels are proposed, to be confirmed.
benefit: Clear promises and on-time fulfilment.

name: Request for quotation
summary: A buyer asks for a price for listed or custom items; suitable sellers reply with structured quotes and terms.
description: A buyer asks for a price for listed or custom items; the request goes to suitable sellers, who reply with structured quotes and terms. Sellers can ask clarification questions, and the answers are shared with all invited sellers.
whyItMatters: Supports negotiated and bulk purchases.
whatItDoes: Turn a cart into a price request with quantities, target prices and notes.
Add custom items that are not listed, with a description, quantity, unit and attachment.
Send the request to suitable sellers, who are notified; without the marketplace, the client prepares the quote.
Sellers reply with prices per item, validity date, payment terms, delivery commitment, warranty and documents.
Sellers ask the buyer questions; the answers are shared with all invited sellers.
Ask for a quote from the page of a price-on-request product or service without adding it to the cart (proposed, to be confirmed).
Link the request, the quote and the resulting order so the purchase can be traced.
clientRules: A seller sees only the requests it is invited to and its own quotes.
The identity of the seller asking a question is not shown to other sellers.
The client can add a check that a person, not a program, is sending the request (CAPTCHA) on the request page.
benefit: Supports negotiated and bulk purchases.

name: Quote negotiation and conversion
summary: The buyer compares quotes side by side, negotiates within limits and accepts one, which becomes an order.
description: The buyer compares quotes side by side, makes counter-offers within limits, and accepts one, which becomes an order. Quotes expire after a set date. (Whether KTDA's 'buyer bids' are handled here is decision K-01.)
whyItMatters: A structured negotiation instead of emails and phone calls.
whatItDoes: Compare all quotes for a request side by side, with the lowest total and differences highlighted.
Make counter-offers on prices; the seller accepts, counters or declines.
Accept one quote; its items go into the cart at the agreed prices and become an order.
Notify the buyer and seller when quotes expire.
clientRules: The number of negotiation rounds and the total time are limited by client settings.
Whether KTDA's 'buyer bids' are handled as counter-offers is to be confirmed.
Accepting one quote declines the other quotes for the same request.
Expired quotes cannot be accepted; the seller may issue a new quote.
benefit: A structured negotiation instead of emails and phone calls.

name: Seller offers
summary: The client or a seller posts an offer, for example a bulk lot of tea, and buyers respond to it. Scope is to be confirmed.
description: The client or a seller posts an offer, for example a bulk lot of tea, and buyers respond to it. (Scope depends on decision K-01.) Offers can be reviewed internally and scheduled to publish at a set date and time.
whyItMatters: Sells large lots to interested buyers.
whoUsesIt: KTDA sales staff; sellers; business buyers
whatItDoes: Post an offer with lot or product, quantity, minimum order, indicative price or price on request, validity and terms.
Review offers internally and publish them at a set date and time.
Buyers respond with the quantity and price they want.
Each response leads to a quote and an order, completing the purchase cycle.
clientRules: Responses are not ranked; there is no bidding or auction.
The remaining quantity falls with each order; the offer closes at zero or when its validity ends.
benefit: Sells large lots to interested buyers.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: how KTDA's request to 'receive buyer bids' fits the decision to leave bidding and auctions out of the product (KTDA to decide) (ref K-01)

name: Configurable requisition workflows
summary: Online request forms for custom products or services that go through the client's internal approval steps.
description: Online request forms for custom products or services (for example tea blends, contract packaging, forward contracts) that go through the client's internal approval steps.
whyItMatters: Turns complex custom requests into a tracked process.
whoUsesIt: Business buyers; KTDA staff; client administrators
whatItDoes: Request a custom tea blend, contract packaging or a forward contract through an online form.
Move each request through the internal approval steps.
Show the buyer the status of the request and the reason for any rejection.
Create a draft contract when a forward-contract request is approved.
Add new request types for each business model by configuration, without development work.
clientRules: A rejection needs a reason.
benefit: Turns complex custom requests into a tracked process.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)

name: Contract drafting
summary: Creates contracts from approved templates with the agreed terms, and sends them for internal review.
description: Creates contracts from templates with the agreed terms, and sends them for internal review.
whyItMatters: Faster, consistent contracts.
whoUsesIt: Legal and sales staff; client administrators; business buyers
whatItDoes: Draft a contract from a quote or request, with parties, value, scope, deliverables, schedule and terms filled in.
Send the draft for internal review; the reviewer approves it or returns it with comments.
Keep a library of approved templates for each transaction type, language and business model.
Create a draft contract automatically from an approved forward-contract request.
clientRules: Terms agreed in the quote or request take priority over template defaults.
Only approved contracts can be issued.
benefit: Faster, consistent contracts.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: which document and QR-code generation product is used (technical decision) (ref DOC-LIB)

name: Contract e-signature
summary: All parties sign contracts electronically through a signing provider, with a record of who signed and when.
description: All parties sign contracts electronically through a signing provider, with a record of who signed when. Signing rules can require a minimum number of signers from one party, for example 3 of 5.
whyItMatters: No printing or couriering of contracts.
whoUsesIt: Business buyers; client staff; legal staff; auditors
whatItDoes: Send an approved contract for signing, one signer after another or all at once.
Record each signer, the time and the signature check result returned by the provider.
Require a minimum number of signers from one party, for example 3 of 5.
clientRules: A contract counts as signed only when every party's minimum number of signers is met.
A decline by a signer stops the signing.
The signing provider is not yet named.
benefit: No printing or couriering of contracts.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: which document and QR-code generation product is used (technical decision) (ref DOC-LIB)

name: Contract amendments
summary: Changes to a signed contract go through approval, with versions and a view of what changed.
description: Changes to a signed contract go through approval, with versions and a marked-up view of what changed.
whyItMatters: Contract changes stay controlled and traceable.
whatItDoes: Propose a change to a signed contract; the other party accepts or rejects it.
Create a new version for each accepted change, keeping all earlier versions.
Send significant changes to value, scope or duration through an approval chain.
Compare two versions side by side, showing added, deleted and changed text.
clientRules: A signed contract is never edited; it is only amended.
Accepted changes are signed again.
benefit: Contract changes stay controlled and traceable.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)

name: Contract repository
summary: A searchable store of all contracts, with export.
description: A searchable store of all contracts, with export.
whyItMatters: Contracts are easy to find and audit.
whatItDoes: Search contracts by party, value, dates, terms text, status and type.
Export a full contract package: the signed document, signature record, supporting documents and amendment history.
benefit: Contracts are easy to find and audit.

name: Award and acceptance letters
summary: Creates and sends award or acceptance letters and tracks whether they were accepted by the deadline.
description: Creates and sends award or acceptance letters and tracks whether they were accepted by the deadline.
whyItMatters: Clear confirmation that a deal is agreed.
whoUsesIt: Client staff; business buyers; client administrators
whatItDoes: Generate a branded letter with the required legal clauses when a quote is accepted or a request approved.
Send the letter through the channels the client uses.
Record when the recipient accepts the letter.
Use letter templates for each transaction type, sector and language.
clientRules: A letter not accepted by its deadline lapses, and staff are told.
benefit: Clear confirmation that a deal is agreed.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: which document and QR-code generation product is used (technical decision) (ref DOC-LIB)

name: Performance securities
summary: Records bank guarantees given by suppliers, tracks their validity, and releases or claims them.
description: Records bank guarantees given by suppliers, tracks their validity, and releases or claims them.
whyItMatters: Protects the client if a supplier fails to deliver.
whatItDoes: Record a guarantee with bank, number, amount, currency and expiry date, linked to its contract.
Alert finance staff before expiry and send a renewal request.
Release the guarantee when the contract is completed.
Claim the guarantee if the supplier fails, producing a letter to the bank.
clientRules: A claim needs approval and supporting documents.
benefit: Protects the client if a supplier fails to deliver.

name: Contract-to-order execution
summary: Turns a signed contract into scheduled orders, call-offs or milestone releases, and passes them to fulfilment.
description: Turns a signed contract into scheduled orders, call-offs or milestone releases, and passes them to fulfilment.
whyItMatters: Contracts are carried out on time.
whoUsesIt: Sales and logistics staff; business buyers
whatItDoes: Create orders automatically on the scheduled dates of a signed contract, at contract prices.
Let buyers draw down against a framework contract.
Release each phase of a multi-phase contract as a tracked order when its milestone is complete.
Deliver forward contracts as agreed.
Show the contract and business model on each resulting order.
clientRules: Draw-downs cannot exceed the remaining contract quantity.
benefit: Contracts are carried out on time.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: how scheduled contract call-off orders are placed (technical decision) (ref CALLOFF-PLACE); which document and QR-code generation product is used (technical decision) (ref DOC-LIB)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision CALLOFF-PLACE, DOC-LIB / CALLOFF-PLACE / DOC-LIB pending

name: Group buying
summary: Buyers join together in one deal; when a target quantity is reached, everyone gets the lower price.
description: Buyers join together in one order; when a target quantity is reached, everyone gets the lower price.
whyItMatters: Small buyers get bulk prices.
whatItDoes: Staff set up a group deal with product, target quantity, group price and deadline.
Buyers see the deal and the quantity pledged so far, and pledge a quantity.
When the target is reached, participants are told and buy at the group price within a set window.
When the deadline passes below target, the deal closes and participants are told.
clientRules: Pledging does not require payment (proposed, to be confirmed).
No order is created for a deal that misses its target.
benefit: Small buyers get bulk prices.

name: Scheme applications
summary: People or businesses apply for a programme or scheme; eligibility is checked, and applications are reviewed and approved within a budget.
description: People or businesses apply for a programme or scheme; eligibility is checked, applications are reviewed and approved within a budget, and support goes to the intended groups.
whyItMatters: Supports government or development programmes delivered through the shop.
whatItDoes: Apply for a programme with documents and declarations, and receive a reference.
Check eligibility automatically, including against a programme register where one is set up.
Send failing or flagged applications to staff for review with all documents.
Approve applications within the budget and targeting rules, such as district, age or income band, and send the payment instruction.
clientRules: When the budget is used up, approval is blocked and the application waits for the next allocation.
The programme register is not yet named.
benefit: Supports government or development programmes delivered through the shop.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether the workflow engine is built or an existing product is embedded (architecture decision) (ref WF-ENG)

name: Proforma invoice
summary: A preliminary invoice issued before payment, from a cart or quote, for opening a letter of credit or paying in advance.
description: A preliminary invoice issued before payment, from a cart or quote, which buyers need to open a letter of credit or pay in advance.
whyItMatters: Gives buyers a formal priced document to open a letter of credit or pay in advance (inference from KTDA's letter-of-credit requirement).
whatItDoes: Generate a numbered proforma invoice with date and validity from a cart or accepted quote.
Link the proforma to the letter of credit record so the letter of credit matches the deal.
clientRules: An expired proforma cannot be used; prices are recalculated and a new proforma is needed.

Where the client allows it, buyers can also download a standard quote document from their account; it is not a proforma invoice, so the proforma is still produced. Whether banks accept the quote document is to be confirmed.
benefit: Gives buyers a formal priced document to open a letter of credit or pay in advance (inferred from KTDA's letter-of-credit requirement).
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF); which document and QR-code generation product is used (technical decision) (ref DOC-LIB)
prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision PH-INF, DOC-LIB / PH-INF / DOC-LIB pending

name: Incoterms
summary: Records the agreed international trade terms (Incoterms, such as FOB or CIF) on quotes and orders.
description: Records the agreed international trade terms (Incoterms, such as FOB or CIF) on quotes and orders, which decide who pays for and is responsible for transport.
whyItMatters: Avoids disputes in export deals.
whatItDoes: Choose an Incoterm and named place on a quote or at business checkout.
Show the Incoterm on the quote, order, invoice and proforma.
Drop the delivery fee and show buyer-arranged collection when the Incoterm puts transport on the buyer.
clientRules: The named place is required.
The Incoterms edition is not yet stated.
benefit: Avoids disputes in export deals.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: confirmation by the client that this feature is needed in phase 1 (it was placed there by inference from the client documents) (ref PH-INF)

name: Sample orders
summary: Small sample quantities of bulk products that buyers can order, with limits per buyer.
description: Small sample quantities of bulk products that buyers can order, with limits per buyer.
whyItMatters: Buyers can test quality before a large order.
whatItDoes: Mark products as samples with their own price.
Order samples like any other product.
Limit the number of samples each buyer can order in a period.
clientRules: Samples beyond the limit are refused at the cart.
benefit: Buyers can test quality before a large order.

name: Recurring and subscription orders
summary: Customers set up orders that repeat automatically, for example every month.
description: Customers set up orders that repeat automatically, for example every month.
whyItMatters: Convenience for regular purchases and steady sales.
whatItDoes: Buy a product on a repeating cycle with a set number of repeats.
Process each due repeat payment without manual action.
Tell the buyer when a repeat payment fails, or cancel the arrangement where the client chooses.
Remind the buyer by email a set number of days before the next payment is due; the client sets the number of days or switches it off.
clientRules: Only payment methods that support repeat payments are offered for repeating orders.
Each cycle is processed only once.
benefit: Convenience for regular purchases and steady sales.

name: Shipping methods and rates
summary: Delivery options by country with prices by weight or order value, free delivery above a threshold, and expected delivery ranges.
description: Delivery options by country with prices by weight or order value, free delivery above a threshold, and expected delivery date ranges.
whyItMatters: Customers see delivery cost and timing clearly.
whatItDoes: Set up several delivery options, such as standard, express and pickup, each with its price rule and delivery time.
Show shoppers the options allowed for their country, with name, description, price and expected delivery range.
Recalculate the delivery charge when the cart weight or value changes.
Offer free delivery above an order value the client chooses.
Keep the chosen option, price and promised delivery range with the order.
clientRules: Where no delivery option is available for the address, checkout stops and pickup points are offered if any exist.
benefit: Customers see delivery cost and timing clearly.

name: Delivery fee rule engine
summary: Calculates delivery fees from distance or zone, weight, service speed, rural or urban location and pickup versus delivery, and shows the breakdown.
description: Calculates delivery fees from distance or zone, service speed, rural or urban location and pickup versus delivery, shows the breakdown, and can share revenue with delivery partners.
whyItMatters: Fair, accurate delivery pricing.
whatItDoes: Define fees that follow the client's price lists: base fee by service and zone, weight bands, distance bands and rural or urban charges.
Show shoppers how the fee is made up before they pay.
Set pickup fees per outlet and delivery fees separately.
Keep dated versions of the fee lists so past orders keep the fee that applied.
Recalculate the fee when the address, cart weight or service changes.
Record the share of each delivery fee owed to the delivery partner that carries the parcel.
clientRules: Where distance cannot be measured, the zone price applies; if there is none, the option is not offered.
A new fee list applies only from its effective date.
Changes to fee lists are recorded.
benefit: Fair, accurate delivery pricing.

name: Pickup points and outlets
summary: A list of pickup points and outlets with opening hours, fee, capacity, temporary closures and a map.
description: A list of pickup points and outlets with opening hours, capacity, temporary closures and a map.
whyItMatters: Customers choose a convenient collection point.
whatItDoes: Choose a pickup point or outlet from a list or map, with address, opening hours and fee.
Maintain outlets with address, opening hours, fee and map position.
Mark an outlet as temporarily closed for a period or as full.
Link each outlet to the warehouse that supplies it.
Mark outlets that accept returns.
List orders already placed for an outlet whose status changes, for follow-up.
clientRules: Outlets that are closed on the expected arrival date, or full, are not offered.
An outlet removed in the Malawi Post source system is closed, not deleted.
Outlet status changes are recorded.
benefit: Customers choose a convenient collection point.

name: Serviceability rules
summary: Rules for where delivery is available, by location or outlet, and which areas each seller covers.
description: Rules for where delivery is available, by location or outlet, and which areas each seller covers.
whyItMatters: Customers are not offered delivery that cannot happen.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers; sellers; client administrators; logistics staff
whatItDoes: Define coverage areas by country, region, district and postcode, with the services and outlets for each, and whether the area is rural or urban.
Let sellers set the districts they deliver to.
Show shoppers only the delivery and pickup options available for their location.
Limit some products to certain services or outlets.
clientRules: Where neither delivery nor pickup is available, no order can be placed.
Items from a seller who does not cover the buyer's area cannot be delivered, and the buyer is told which items.
Coverage is checked again just before the order is placed.
benefit: Customers are not offered delivery that cannot happen.

name: Estimated delivery time engine
summary: Calculates the expected delivery or collection date from service standards, cut-off times and transport links.
description: Calculates the expected delivery time from service standards, cut-off times and transport links.
whyItMatters: Realistic delivery promises.
whatItDoes: Set delivery standards per route and service: transit days and the days transport departs.
Show the earliest and latest delivery date at checkout, on the order and on the tracking page.
Keep the promised range with each order for measuring on-time delivery.
Prepare delivery windows by product and district in advance so they can be shown quickly.
clientRules: Orders before the daily cut-off on a working day are dispatched the same day; otherwise the next working day.
Where transport departs only on certain days, dispatch moves to the next departure day.
Non-working days are skipped.
benefit: Realistic delivery promises.

name: DHL adapter
summary: Connects to DHL for delivery prices, booking, labels and tracking.
description: Connects to DHL for delivery prices, booking, labels and tracking.
whyItMatters: DHL is one of the couriers KTDA names.
whatItDoes: Get DHL prices using KTDA's DHL account, and offer DHL at checkout if enabled.
Book DHL shipments; the DHL waybill number becomes the tracking number.
Print the DHL label.
Show DHL tracking updates on the parcel timeline.
clientRules: Any step the DHL connection cannot perform is done manually or through the standard courier connection.
benefit: Lets KTDA ship with DHL, one of the couriers it names, from the platform.

name: Shipping labels and barcodes
summary: Prints shipping labels with barcodes that postal and courier scanners can read.
description: Prints shipping labels with barcodes that postal and courier scanners can read. Labels can be printed on network label printers (for example Zebra) as well as PDF.
whyItMatters: Parcels can be scanned and tracked at every step.
whatItDoes: Print a label with sender, recipient, weight, service, shipment number and a barcode of the tracking number.
Use the courier's own label when the parcel is booked with a courier.
Assign an international postal tracking number first for international postal parcels.
Print the digital postcode or address alias on the label where one exists.
Print on network label printers, for example Zebra, or produce a PDF.
Let sellers print packing slips and labels for their own orders.
Print return labels with the same layout and barcode rules.
clientRules: Labels are tested with the client's postal scanners during acceptance testing.
benefit: Parcels can be scanned and tracked at every step.

name: Fulfilment allocation and routing
summary: Decides who fulfils each order line (the seller, the client or a logistics company) and from which warehouse, choosing the nearest.
description: Decides who fulfils each order (the seller, the client or a logistics company) and from which warehouse, choosing the nearest.
whyItMatters: Faster, cheaper delivery.
whatItDoes: Send each order line to the party that fulfils it, according to the fulfilment model.
Route client-fulfilled lines to the nearest warehouse that has the stock.
Split a line across warehouses where no single warehouse has enough, or flag it for manual allocation.
Change an allocation with a reason (proposed, to be confirmed).
Run the steps of a KTDA fulfilment workflow with the same rules.
clientRules: Allocation happens when the order is paid, or when it is placed for cash on delivery and on-account orders.
Sellers who opt in to client fulfilment are fulfilled by the client unless the product says otherwise.
Allocation changes are recorded.
benefit: Faster, cheaper delivery.

name: Warehouse pick, pack, dispatch
summary: Picking lists, packing checks, dispatch confirmation and manifests for the warehouse, with a shelf location for each product.
description: Picking lists, packing confirmation, dispatch confirmation and manifests for the warehouse. Each product has a shelf location (zone, aisle, rack, shelf, bin), shown on pick lists and order lines.
whyItMatters: Organised, accurate dispatch.
whatItDoes: Print pick lists showing each product's shelf location (zone, aisle, rack, shelf, bin) in walking order.
Check each packed item against the order before sealing.
Move packed parcels to a staging area and confirm dispatch with the carrier and waybill number.
Print or export a daily dispatch manifest per transport operator.
Let sellers print one combined pick list and packing list for several orders.
Run the shipping steps in the same configured order every time.
clientRules: A parcel can be confirmed as packed only when every item and quantity matches the order.
Steps cannot be skipped.
Products without a shelf location are listed last and marked as missing.
For pickup orders, staff confirm arrival at the outlet instead of dispatch.
benefit: Organised, accurate dispatch.

name: Shipments
summary: One order can ship in several parcels, each with a tracking number, status and packing slip.
description: One order can ship in several parcels, each with a tracking number and status (shipped, ready for pickup, delivered) and a packing slip.
whyItMatters: Customers can follow each part of their order.
whatItDoes: Ship one order in several parcels.
Show the shopper each parcel with its tracking number and status: shipped, ready for pickup or delivered.
Print a packing slip for each parcel.
clientRules: Changing a shipped, ready-for-pickup or delivered date needs a reason and is recorded.
benefit: Customers can follow each part of their order.

name: Logistics task creation and seller pickup
clientName: Postal work tasks and seller collections
summary: Creates delivery work tasks (collect, sort, dispatch, deliver) from online orders and lets Malawi Post schedule collections from sellers.
description: Creates delivery work tasks (collect, sort, dispatch, deliver) and lets Malawi Post schedule collections from sellers and record that they happened.
whyItMatters: Connects online orders to postal operations.
whatItDoes: Create collect, sort, dispatch and deliver tasks from online orders that go through the postal network.
Mark each task complete when the matching scan is recorded, and make the next task due.
Schedule a collection from a seller with a date and time window.
Record the parcels collected, or a missed visit with a reason, and reschedule.
Create onward tasks for returned parcels handed in at the wrong outlet.
Show each parcel as awaiting pickup, sorting, dispatch or out for delivery.
benefit: Connects online orders to postal operations.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether postal operations, e-Government services and Malawi Post financial services are part of the product (Malawi Post to decide) (ref FG-06)

name: Proof of delivery record
summary: Stores proof that an order was delivered or collected, such as courier confirmation, a one-time code or a QR code checked at the pickup counter.
description: Stores proof that an order was delivered or collected, for example confirmation from the courier, or an OTP or QR code checked at the pickup counter.
whyItMatters: Settles 'I never received it' disputes.
whoUsesIt: Support staff; outlet staff; client administrators; shoppers
whatItDoes: Store proof of delivery with method, time, location where given, recipient name and the courier or collector.
Choose which proof methods (signature, one-time code, QR scan) each service requires.
Check the buyer's pickup code or QR at the counter before handing over the parcel.
Use the proof as evidence in disputes.
clientRules: An order cannot be marked delivered without the proof its service requires.
After a set number of wrong codes, code entry is locked.
Only authorised staff see signatures, photos and locations; others see the method and time.
Changes to proof requirements are recorded and apply to new shipments.
benefit: Settles 'I never received it' disputes.

name: Delivery exceptions
summary: Handles failed deliveries: redelivery, address corrections, return to sender, incident reports and escalation.
description: Handles failed deliveries: redelivery, address corrections, return to sender, incident reports and escalation.
whyItMatters: Problem deliveries are resolved, not forgotten.
whatItDoes: Record each failed delivery with a reason, such as unreachable, not at home or address issue, and a next action.
Let shoppers choose a new delivery date or correct their address from the message or the order page.
Return a parcel to the sender.
Report incidents such as a lost, damaged or delayed parcel, with evidence.
Escalate problems that stay open too long to the right contact.
Record the final outcome: redelivered, returned, lost or damaged.
clientRules: After the maximum number of failed attempts, no further redelivery is offered and the parcel returns to sender.
A corrected address is checked for coverage and fee, and the change is recorded.
benefit: Problem deliveries are resolved, not forgotten.

name: COD cash reconciliation
summary: Matches cash collected by couriers to the orders and delivery runs it belongs to.
description: Matches cash collected by couriers to the orders and delivery runs it belongs to.
whyItMatters: Cash is accounted for and losses are spotted.
whatItDoes: Add each cash-on-delivery amount to the courier's expected cash for that delivery run.
Record the cash handed over at the depot and compare it with the amount expected.
Alert finance staff to differences and resolve them with a note.
Match delivery partner cash reports to parcels by tracking number and list unmatched lines.
clientRules: Where delivery runs are not used, a run is the courier and delivery date (proposed, to be confirmed).
Resolved differences are locked and recorded.
benefit: Cash is accounted for and losses are spotted.

name: Address validation and geocoding
summary: Checks addresses and places them on the map, including digital postcodes where available.
description: Checks addresses and turns them into map coordinates, including digital postcodes where available.
whyItMatters: Fewer delivery failures.
whatItDoes: Check an address when it is entered and suggest a correction the shopper can accept or ignore.
Store the map position of each delivery address, from a map pin or the checking service.
Use the country's digital postcode or address alias system if one is adopted, and show it on labels and tracking.
clientRules: If the checking service is unavailable, the address is saved and the order goes ahead; the address is marked as not checked.
benefit: Fewer delivery failures.

name: Cross-border shipping
summary: Handles international postal shipping: customs declarations, international tracking and duties, using the postal systems CDS and IPS, and the UPU Global Monitoring System (GMS).
description: Handles international postal shipping: customs declarations, international tracking and duties, using the postal systems CDS and IPS. It also exchanges data with the UPU Global Monitoring System (GMS).
whyItMatters: International parcels can clear customs and be tracked across postal networks.

Exchange data with the UPU Global Monitoring System to monitor international service quality.
Show duties where the data is available.

name: Holding charges and pre-dispatch changes
clientName: Storage charges and changes before dispatch

whyItMatters: Encourages timely collection and covers storage costs.
whatItDoes: Let shoppers change the delivery address or instructions before dispatch.
Set the number of free storage days at an outlet and the daily charge after that.

clientRules: Address changes are allowed only before dispatch and within the window the client sets.

name: Logistics KPIs

description: Dashboards for on-time delivery, delivery success rate and transit times.

See the average transit time in days.
clientRules: Only authorised users can open the dashboard.
benefit: Shows how well delivery is performing.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether a licensed add-on is bought or the capability is built (technical and Product Owner decision) (ref PAID-STUB)

name: Specialised logistics
summary: Special handling for goods that must stay cold, with temperature monitoring, and for hazardous goods, with certified carriers and required documents.
description: Special handling for goods that must stay cold — with the temperature recorded throughout the journey and alerts when it goes out of range — and for hazardous goods, with compliant packaging, certified carriers and the required documents.
whyItMatters: Safe delivery of sensitive goods.
whatItDoes: Flag products that must stay cold.
Receive temperature readings during the journey and raise an incident when they go out of range.
Flag hazardous products.
clientRules: Cold goods go only with carriers able to carry them cold.
Hazardous goods go only with carriers certified for that class, and only once the required documents are attached.
benefit: Safe delivery of sensitive goods.

name: S10 identifiers

description: Creates and checks international postal tracking numbers in the UPU S10 format (for example RR123456789MW).

whatItDoes: Issue S10 numbers from Malawi Post's allocated range.
Check entered or received S10 numbers for format and check digit.
Find any parcel and its order items from any of its reference numbers.
clientRules: When a range is used up, no number is issued and staff are told to set up a new range.
Invalid numbers are refused.
benefit: Required for international postal tracking.

name: Carrier connector framework

description: A standard technical 'plug' for delivery companies: get a price, book, print a label, track and cancel, plus rules to choose the best carrier.

whatItDoes: Add a new courier by building one connection, not by changing the shop.
Offer a manual path, such as entering a waybill or uploading a label, for steps a courier does not support.
Assign each shipment to a delivery partner by rules for area, service, weight, seller and fulfilment model.
Compare courier prices and choose the cheapest that meets the service.
Receive courier tracking updates as they happen, or check for them at set intervals.
Book return collections with couriers that support them.
clientRules: Staff can reassign a partner with a reason; any booking with the old partner is cancelled first.
A booking retried after a delay never creates a second booking.
Updates from couriers are checked for authenticity before use.
benefit: A new courier is added by building one connection, not by changing the shop.

name: Post-office drop-off acceptance
summary: Post offices and agencies accept parcels dropped off by sellers, scanning them in.

whatItDoes: Show sellers the parcels to drop off and the outlets that accept them.
Scan a dropped-off parcel to accept it, recording outlet, staff and time.
Record the weight at acceptance and flag differences from the declared weight.
clientRules: Parcels the platform does not expect are refused.
benefit: Sellers hand over parcels at any post office.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether postal operations, e-Government services and Malawi Post financial services are part of the product (Malawi Post to decide) (ref FG-06)

name: Hub-and-spoke sorting

description: Parcels are sorted at central hubs and sent out to branches, with a scan at every handover.

whatItDoes: Record every hand-over scan at a hub or branch on the parcel timeline.
Set the expected sequence of hubs on each route.
Flag parcels that miss an expected scan for review.
clientRules: Scans that name an unknown hub go to review.
The postal sorting system is not yet named.
benefit: Parcels can be traced through the postal network.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether postal operations, e-Government services and Malawi Post financial services are part of the product (Malawi Post to decide) (ref FG-06)

name: Last-mile route lists and attempts

description: Daily delivery lists for drivers and couriers, where they record each delivery attempt.
whyItMatters: Organised last-mile delivery.
whatItDoes: Create the day's delivery list for each courier in a planned order.
Mark parcels as out for delivery when the round starts, which notifies the shopper.
Record each attempt as delivered, with proof, or failed, with a reason.
clientRules: A failed attempt opens a delivery problem case (PRD-LOG-013).
Couriers see only their own lists.
benefit: Organised last-mile delivery.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether postal operations, e-Government services and Malawi Post financial services are part of the product (Malawi Post to decide) (ref FG-06)

Record the waybill and hand-over manually where G4S offers no tracking connection.
clientRules: Where no tracking connection exists, the parcel is marked "carrier updates not available".
benefit: A local courier option for KTDA.

description: Connects to Skynet courier services. This includes shipment tracking events, which are fed into the tracking event hub.

Record the waybill and hand-over manually where Skynet offers no tracking connection.
clientRules: Where no tracking connection exists, the parcel is marked "carrier updates not available".
benefit: A courier option named by KTDA.

Record the waybill and hand-over manually where Wells Fargo offers no tracking connection.
clientRules: Where no tracking connection exists, the parcel is marked "carrier updates not available".
benefit: A local courier option named by KTDA.

summary: Connects to Aramex courier services, including tracking updates.
description: Connects to Aramex courier services. This includes shipment tracking events, which are fed into the tracking event hub.

whatItDoes: Use the Aramex services its system supports, with KTDA's account.

Record the waybill and hand-over manually where Aramex offers no tracking connection.
clientRules: Where no tracking connection exists, the parcel is marked "carrier updates not available".
benefit: A regional and international courier named by KTDA.

name: Shipping lines and agents adapter
summary: Connects to shipping lines and shipping agents for sea freight, including tracking updates.
description: Connects to shipping lines and shipping agents for sea freight. This includes shipment tracking events, which are fed into the tracking event hub.
whyItMatters: Supports export of bulk tea by sea.
whatItDoes: Use the services each shipping line supports, such as booking references and container or bill-of-lading tracking.
Show sea-freight milestones on the shipment timeline.
Enter milestones manually where a shipping line offers no connection.
benefit: Supports export of bulk tea by sea.

name: MPC delivery partner adapters
summary: Connects to Malawi Post's delivery partners once Malawi Post names them.
description: Connects to Malawi Post's delivery partners once Malawi Post names them.
whyItMatters: Lets partners carry Malawi Post deliveries.
whatItDoes: Assign shipments to a named partner under the assignment rules.
Use the services each partner supports.
Give partners without a connection a printable job list and record their hand-overs and deliveries manually.
clientRules: The partners are not yet named.
benefit: Lets partners carry Malawi Post deliveries.

Keep working without signal; the original capture time is kept when the phone syncs.
Add further evidence to a parcel already delivered.

Location is captured with the consent recorded by the app.
benefit: Strong proof of delivery for the operator's own fleet.

prototypeDefaultLabel: Prototype default — decision FG-06, PAID-STUB / FG-06 / PAID-STUB pending

name: Buyer shipment tracking
summary: Customers enter an order or tracking number and see a timeline of where the parcel has been, can share a tracking link and refresh it.
description: Customers enter an order or tracking number and see a timeline of where the parcel has been, can share a tracking link and refresh it.
whyItMatters: Customers know where their order is without calling support.
whatItDoes: Track a parcel by tracking number, including international postal and waybill numbers.
See a timeline of each step with date, time and place, newest first, and the expected delivery range.
See all own orders in one place with the latest status and expected delivery of each.
Share a tracking link with the recipient without showing account details.
Have the page refresh by itself, or refresh it on request.
Revoke a shared link at any time.
clientRules: The public tracking page never shows the customer name, address, phone or email.
Shared links expire after a period the client sets.
Repeated lookups from one location must pass a check that a person, not a machine, is asking (proposed, to be confirmed).
benefit: Customers know where their order is without calling support.

name: Tracking event hub
summary: Collects tracking updates from the client's own scanners, courier companies and international postal systems into one place, using one common list of step names, and flags parcels that missed an expected scan.
description: Collects tracking updates from the client's own scanners, from courier companies and from international postal systems into one place, using one common list of event names, and flags parcels that missed an expected scan.
whyItMatters: One reliable tracking picture whatever carrier moves the parcel.
whatItDoes: Collect updates from scanners, couriers, postal systems, PostGlobal and manual entry into one timeline.
Translate each source's own codes into one common list of step names.
Set rules for the scan expected next and the time allowed; open an alert when it does not arrive.
Escalate alerts that stay open too long as delivery problems.
Place updates that cannot be matched in a review list, and reprocess them once fixed.
Search any order or parcel by order number, tracking number or customer phone and see its full history.
Keep and archive tracking history according to retention rules.
Show updates for return parcels on the return timeline.
clientRules: Duplicate updates are ignored.
Updates arriving out of order are shown in time order, and a parcel status never moves backwards.
Unmatched updates never send a customer message.
Changes to code translations are recorded and apply to later updates.
benefit: One reliable tracking picture whatever carrier moves the parcel.

name: Scanning and field operations app
summary: A mobile app for staff at collection points, hubs and on delivery rounds to scan parcels. It records who scanned on which device, works without signal, and adds location, photos, voice notes and video as evidence.
description: A mobile app for field and hub staff to scan parcels at collection, sorting and delivery. It records who scanned and on which device, works without signal, and adds location, photos, voice notes and video as evidence.
whyItMatters: Every handover of a parcel is recorded.
whoUsesIt: Malawi Post staff at collection points, hubs and on delivery rounds; logistics staff
whatItDoes: Scan parcels at collection, hub arrival and departure, and delivery; each scan appears on the timeline.
Record the staff member and device for every scan.
Keep scanning without signal; scans keep their original time when the phone syncs.
Add location, photos, voice notes and video as evidence.
Give each staff member their own delivery or collection list (proposed, to be confirmed).
clientRules: Only registered devices linked to a staff member can send scans.
Scans synced very late are accepted but marked late.
Location is captured with the consent recorded by the app.
Only authorised staff can view scan photos and recordings.
benefit: Every handover of a parcel is recorded.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: whether postal operations, e-Government services and Malawi Post financial services are part of the product (Malawi Post to decide) (ref FG-06)

name: Email notifications and templates
summary: Automatic emails sent when something happens to an order, such as placed or shipped, using templates that fill in details such as name and order number, in each language and shop.
description: Automatic emails triggered by events (order placed, shipped and so on), using templates that fill in details such as name and order number, in each language and shop. Bounced emails are detected and the address is flagged.
whyItMatters: Customers are kept informed automatically.
whatItDoes: Send emails automatically when an order is placed, shipped and at other steps.
Fill in details such as name, order number, outlet opening hours, pickup code and expected delivery range.
Use the customer's language and a separate version for each shop.
Let staff change subject, wording, timing and attachments without developers.
Detect bounced emails, flag the address and use another channel instead.
clientRules: The bounce flag clears when the customer changes or confirms their email.
Template changes are recorded.
benefit: Customers are kept informed automatically.

name: Notification engine (multi-channel)
summary: The central messaging service: a message is written once and sent by SMS, email, app notification or WhatsApp in the right language, with a backup channel if the first fails.
description: The central messaging engine: one message is written once and sent by SMS, email, app notification or WhatsApp in the right language, with a fallback channel if the first fails.
whyItMatters: Consistent messages on every channel without building each one separately.
whatItDoes: Write one message for each occasion and send it by every channel the client uses.
Send messages in the customer's language.
Use a backup channel when the first one fails or the customer has no phone or email.
Send an order confirmation and a message when the order status changes.
Switch channels on or off for each client, and set content for each occasion and channel.
Send SMS to customers who registered with a mobile number and no email.
clientRules: Where no translation exists in the customer's language, the client's default language is used (proposed, to be confirmed).
Disabled channels are skipped and the skip is recorded.
benefit: Consistent messages on every channel without building each one separately.

name: Notification preferences
summary: Customers choose which messages they want and on which channels, set quiet hours and limits, and follow or stop updates for a single order.
description: Customers choose which messages they want and on which channels, set quiet hours and limits, and follow a particular order. Customers can also subscribe to, or unsubscribe from, updates for a single order.
whyItMatters: Customers get useful messages, not spam.
whatItDoes: Choose, in My account, which kinds of message to receive on which channel.
Set quiet hours; non-urgent messages wait until they end.
Subscribe to or unsubscribe from updates for a single order, including by a one-click link in each message.
Set default quiet hours and a limit on how many messages a customer receives.
Stop SMS by texting the opt-out keyword, including for phone numbers without an account.
Opt in before receiving WhatsApp, Telegram, push or voice messages.
clientRules: Messages the client marks as mandatory are always sent on their main channel.
Urgent messages are sent at once, even in quiet hours.
Customers who have not set their own values follow the client defaults.
Preference changes are recorded.
benefit: Customers get useful messages, not spam.

name: Notification delivery tracking and audit
summary: Records whether each message was sent, delivered or failed on each channel, linked to the order or shipment.
description: Records whether each message was sent, delivered or failed on each channel, linked to the order or shipment.
whyItMatters: Proves customers were notified, and failed messages can be fixed.
whatItDoes: Keep a record of each message with channel, recipient, order, shipment, status and times.
Update the record when the provider confirms delivery or failure, and start the backup channel on failure.
Show every message for an order and its shipments on the order page.
Report sent, delivered, failed, held and suppressed messages by channel and type, with export.
Keep proof of delivery for each person when one notice goes to many people.
clientRules: Records are deleted after the retention period the client sets.
benefit: Proves customers were notified, and failed messages can be fixed.

name: In-app notification feed
summary: A bell icon in the customer's account showing their recent notifications.
description: A bell icon in the customer's account showing their recent notifications.
whyItMatters: Customers can see past messages in one place.
whatItDoes: See the number of unread notifications on every page.
Open a list of notifications, newest first, with a link to the order or parcel.
Mark a notification as read by opening it, or clear it.
benefit: Customers can see past messages in one place.

name: Proactive outreach and outage notices
summary: Sends messages to chosen groups of customers, for example everyone affected by a delay, and shows a banner when a service is disrupted.
description: Sends messages to chosen groups of customers (for example everyone affected by a delay) and shows a banner on the site when a service is disrupted.
whyItMatters: Customers hear about problems before they complain.
whatItDoes: Choose affected customers by parcel status, outlet, area, carrier, order status or dates, and preview the number and a sample.
Send the notice now or schedule it; customers receive it in their language.
Cancel a scheduled notice before it goes.
Show a banner on the site and tracking pages for a set period.
Show a banner automatically when a tracking source stops sending updates.
clientRules: Customers' message preferences apply to service notices.
benefit: Customers hear about problems before they complain.

name: Seller shipment visibility
summary: Sellers see when their parcels were handed over and delivered.
description: Sellers see when their parcels were handed over and delivered.
whyItMatters: Sellers can answer their own customers' questions.
whatItDoes: See own shipments with shipped, ready-for-pickup and delivered dates.
See the full tracking timeline of own shipments, including collection, drop-off and delivery.
clientRules: Sellers cannot see other sellers' shipments.
benefit: Sellers can answer their own customers' questions.

name: Guest order-status lookup
summary: Anyone can check an order's status with the order number and their phone number or email, without logging in.
description: Anyone can check an order's status with the order number and their phone number or email, without logging in.
whyItMatters: Easy tracking for guest buyers.
whatItDoes: Enter the order number and the phone number or email used on the order.
See the order status, its parcels and the tracking timeline.
clientRules: Only a partly hidden contact detail is shown; no other personal details.
A failed check does not say which detail was wrong.
After repeated failed checks from one location, a check that a person, not a machine, is asking is required.
benefit: Easy tracking for guest buyers.

name: Shipment and pickup event notifications
summary: Automatic messages when a parcel is on its way, ready for pickup, when a delivery attempt failed, and reminders before the pickup deadline.
description: Automatic messages when a parcel is on its way, ready for pickup (with where, when and what to bring), when a delivery attempt failed and why, and reminders before the pickup deadline or when a parcel is still uncollected.
whyItMatters: Fewer missed deliveries and uncollected parcels.
whoUsesIt: Shoppers; Malawi Post outlet and operations staff
whatItDoes: Tell the shopper when the parcel is shipped, with the tracking number and link.
Tell the shopper when the parcel is out for delivery, with the delivery code where the service needs one.
Tell the shopper when the parcel is delivered or collected.
Tell the shopper when the parcel is ready for pickup: outlet, address, opening hours, pickup code, identification to bring and the deadline.
Tell the shopper when a delivery attempt failed, why, and how to reschedule.
Remind the shopper before the pickup deadline, and tell the shopper and the outlet when a parcel is still uncollected.
clientRules: Each message is sent only once per parcel and step.
benefit: Fewer missed deliveries and uncollected parcels.

name: Return requests

description: Customers ask to return an item within the allowed time, choose a reason and what they want (refund, replacement), attach photos and follow the status; the returns policy is shown.

whatItDoes: Request a return of items from a completed order, choosing a quantity, a reason and the outcome wanted (refund, replacement or another option the client sets).
Describe the problem and attach photos.
Follow the status of each return in My account, including approval and return tracking.
Read the returns policy on the return form.
Set the return window and the lists of reasons and outcomes, shown in the shopper's language.
clientRules: Returns can be requested only within the return window the client sets, and only for completed orders.
Digital products that are downloaded cannot be returned unless the client allows it.
File size and number of photos are limited.
Only the shopper and authorised staff can open the photos.
The shopper and the client are notified of each new return request.
benefit: A clear, fair returns process.

name: Return eligibility rules
summary: Rules for which items can be returned, and within which window and conditions, by category, seller policy and product.
description: Rules for which items can be returned, by category and by seller policy.
whyItMatters: Returns follow policy automatically.
whatItDoes: Mark categories or products as not returnable.
Give each seller its own return window, counted from the order date or the delivery date.
Show conditions for an item, such as its required state, which the shopper must confirm.
Offer shoppers only the items they are allowed to return.
clientRules: A product marked not returnable is never returnable; after that, product, seller, category and general rules apply in that order.
A request that includes an ineligible item or too many items is refused as a whole.
Rule changes are recorded.
benefit: Returns follow policy automatically.

name: Return logistics
summary: How returned items travel back: return labels or instructions, collection from the customer or drop-off, and routing back to the right place.
description: How returned items travel back: return labels or instructions, collection from the customer or drop-off, and routing back to the right place.
whyItMatters: Returns arrive back where they should.
whatItDoes: Choose collection from the shopper's address in a time slot, or drop-off at an outlet that accepts returns.
Download a return label, or read instructions where no label is needed.
Create a return collection or drop-off task with a tracking number automatically when a return is approved.
Follow the return parcel; the return is marked received when it arrives.
Set who pays for return delivery: the seller, the customer, shared, or the client, and when each applies.
Send each returned item to the seller, warehouse or outlet that should receive it (proposed, to be confirmed).

Items dropped at the wrong outlet are sent onward.
benefit: Returns arrive back where they should.
availability: Depends on a pending decision: content that Malawi Post has not yet provided (service lists, return shipping models, priority e-Government services and the complaints and dispute policy) (ref T-MISS)

name: Return inspection

description: Staff inspect returned items at the outlet or warehouse, record the condition with photos and decide the outcome.
whyItMatters: Fair decisions based on evidence.
whatItDoes: Record the location, condition grade, photos, notes and accepted quantity.
Accept the return, accept part of it or reject it.
Put accepted items back into stock.
Start the refund for the accepted quantity.
Let sellers inspect returns of their own products where the client allows it.
clientRules: An item can be inspected only after it has been received.
